# ARS-Codex

This is a Codex adapter for the ARS suite. The vendored ARS content lives under
`ars/`; keep it as source material and route through this file first.

## Versioning

This Codex package is version `0.1.28`. The repo-root `VERSION`, this
`SKILL.md` metadata version, and `manifest.json` `adapter_version` must match.
Vendored ARS suite versions are tracked separately by source repository commit
in `manifest.json`.

## First Rule

Do not load the whole suite by default. Select one workflow, read that workflow's
`WORKFLOW.md`, then load only the agent, reference, template, or shared files needed
for the user's current stage.

The internal workflow entry files are named `WORKFLOW.md`, not `SKILL.md`, so
Codex registers only this root router skill instead of exposing every vendored
upstream workflow as a separate skill.

## Workflow Router

Choose the workflow by intent:

| User intent | Read first |
|---|---|
| Deep research, literature review, systematic review, meta-analysis, fact-checking, research question refinement | `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Academic paper writing, paper outline, abstract, revision, citation formatting, AI disclosure, LaTeX/DOCX/PDF formatting guidance | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Paper review, peer review simulation, editorial decision, reviewer calibration, re-review after revision | `ars/academic-paper-reviewer/WORKFLOW.md` |
| End-to-end research-to-paper pipeline, integrity gate, staged review/revision/finalization workflow | `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Experiment planning, code experiment execution plan, human study protocol, statistical interpretation, reproducibility validation | `ars/experiment-agent/WORKFLOW.md` |

If the request spans multiple workflows, start with `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md`
unless the user clearly asked for a single phase.

### Paper Topic Scoping Override

Apply this override before the general paper/pipeline routing rule and before the Claude-Style Alias Router below.
The override applies regardless of whether the user invokes ARS via natural
language or via an `ars-*` alias.

If the user says they want to write a paper, thesis, proposal, article, journal
article, or manuscript, but they only provide a broad topic, tentative title,
research interest, or "??/??/??" and do **not** provide a clear,
answerable research question, route to `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` in
`socratic` mode first. This matches the upstream ARS experience where vague
paper-topic requests start with SCR/Socratic narrowing instead of immediate
outline or drafting.

Treat these as Socratic triggers even when the wording contains paper-writing
intent:

- "I want to write a paper on ..."
- "I have a paper topic/title ..."
- "???????,???..."
- "????????/??,???????"
- "???????/??????"
- "??? ?? ??? ?? ??? ?? ???? ??"
- "?? ??/?? ??? ??? ??? ???? ????"

First response in this path:

1. State that the request is being routed to `deep-research` `socratic` mode
   because the research question is not yet precise.
2. Ask 3-5 Socratic narrowing questions using `socratic_mentor_agent` and
   `research_question_agent` guidance.
3. Do not produce an outline, draft, literature review, or full pipeline
   dashboard until the user has converged on at least one candidate RQ.

Route directly to `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` only when the user already
has a clear RQ, approved study frame, data/results, literature matrix, draft,
or explicitly asks to skip scoping and proceed to outline/drafting. Route to
`ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` only when the user explicitly asks for the
full research-to-paper pipeline or says to continue after Socratic scoping.

## Claude-Style Alias Router

Codex does not install Claude slash commands, but this package emulates their
intent. If the user's request starts with a slash alias (`/ars-plan`) or a plain
alias (`ars-plan`), treat it as a mode shortcut, strip the alias token from the
task text, read the matching `ars/commands/ars-*.md` prompt recipe, then route
to the workflow `WORKFLOW.md` below.

The `model:` field in command frontmatter is a Claude routing hint only. Codex
uses the current model unless the user explicitly requests another model.

| Alias | Read command recipe | Then route to |
|---|---|---|
| `/ars-plan`, `ars-plan` | `ars/commands/ars-plan.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `plan` mode |
| `/ars-outline`, `ars-outline` | `ars/commands/ars-outline.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `outline-only` mode |
| `/ars-abstract`, `ars-abstract` | `ars/commands/ars-abstract.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `abstract-only` mode |
| `/ars-lit-review`, `ars-lit-review` | `ars/commands/ars-lit-review.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `lit-review` mode; if the user wants source discovery and synthesis instead, route to `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` in `lit-review` mode |
| `/ars-3w`, `ars-3w` | `ars/commands/ars-3w.md` | `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` in `three-way-scan` mode |
| `/ars-citation-check`, `ars-citation-check` | `ars/commands/ars-citation-check.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `citation-check` mode |
| `/ars-disclosure`, `ars-disclosure` | `ars/commands/ars-disclosure.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `disclosure` mode |

| `/ars-rebuttal-audit`, `ars-rebuttal-audit` | `ars/commands/ars-rebuttal-audit.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `rebuttal-audit` mode; requires both reviewer comments and an existing response draft |

| `/ars-full`, `ars-full` | `ars/commands/ars-full.md` | `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` |

If the request body after the alias is a vague topic, tentative title, research
direction, or "??/??/??" without a clear research question, defer to the Paper Topic Scoping Override above before routing to the alias's target mode.
This applies to `ars-plan`, `ars-outline`, `ars-abstract`, `ars-lit-review`,
and `ars-full`.

If the Codex client reserves slash-prefixed input before it reaches the model,
tell the user to use the plain alias form, for example `ars-plan my topic`.

### Bibliographic Network Routing

The upstream prompt contracts, Python resolver clients, and v3.21
claim-standing adapters are distinct execution paths. Apply this table before
following any vendored instruction that says a lookup happens automatically:

| Path | Default ARS-Codex behavior | Dedicated client trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary topic or candidate discovery | Use Codex browsing and authoritative web sources. | Never launches the Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Crossref, or arXiv Python resolver clients. |
| Agent-side ingest, deduplication, and source verification | In the default inline route, translate prompt-level `WebSearch` or index lookups into Codex browsing or official metadata pages. | Upstream prompt wording such as "automatic S2 lookup" does not itself launch a Python client in Codex. |
| Script-backed citation-existence gate | Do not infer this from an `ars-full` request alone. Stage 2.5 and 4.5 remain mandatory integrity checkpoints, but default Codex routing performs their source work through browsing unless the user also requests programmatic verification. | An explicit request to run `verify_passport.py`, `verification_gate`, or equivalent programmatic reference verification. Once invoked, cache misses may call Crossref, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar for non-manual references; arXiv runs only when `arxiv_id` is present. Manual references skip all four. |
| Claim-standing discovery | Offer only after an eligible Claim Registry row at Stage 2.5 or 4.5. It is advisory and separate from citation verification. | A separate user request plus affirmative, plan-bound consent. It uses the v3.21 keyword-discovery adapters, not the four single-reference resolver clients; absent, cancelled, invalidated, or stale consent means no call. |
| Contamination backfill or migration | No automatic migration. | Only the explicitly selected migration CLI and its documented indexes. |

The canonical upstream network map remains available at
`ars/docs/DATA_FLOWS.md`; this section is the Codex adapter override for when
those flows are actually launched here.

### ARS v3.21.1 Contract-Honesty Boundaries

- Phase E evidence rows are deterministic, source-bound checkpoint artifacts.
  They preserve the existing citation verdict and gate, do not mark a source as
  human-read, and must replay against explicit session-held source bytes.
- Revision roadmaps remain non-ranking proposals. Only an explicit author
  adjudication may authorize exact choices or integrity-correction targets;
  never infer, fabricate, or auto-apply author decisions. Optional cross-run
  adjudication-activity capture is local, best-effort, and advisory only.
- Review-target context must be author-confirmed, and criteria are carried by
  resolved pointers across formative, internal, and external review. Do not
  infer a missing venue/track, invent evidence, or let binding conformance alter
  integrity verdicts, editorial arithmetic, checkpoints, or author triage.
- Human-subjects authority resolution keeps review-ethics and data-protection
  axes separate and fails closed when scope, currency, or applicability is
  unresolved. Outputs remain institution-owned navigation aids, never legal
  advice, an IRB/REC determination, an authorization, or a fabricated timeline.

28:{"round": "S1/open", "candidate": "astra_1", "prior": "KNOWN", "refs": ["https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08076 (Tian, Eriksson, Vitos 2020, pressure effect on order-disorder in L1_0 FeNi, doi:10.1038/s41598-020-71551-4)", "https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0622 (Geng, Chen, Sluiter, PRB 70 094203, fcc Ni-Al phase stability under pressure)", "https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0646 (Geng, Sluiter, Chen, PRB 72 014204, order-disorder effects on EOS in fcc Ni-Al)", "volume-dependent ECIs, Alling/Ruban 2011, already logged in ledger 0dffc5bf40"], "verdict": "DROP", "why": "The arithmetic checks out. data/r3b_l12.csv:30 gives E_ord +1.49 meV and S_ord +231.6 meV. Recomputing with the h1 grid points emix_2 and emix_4 at lnV -0.030 and +0.030 gives about +1.40 and +214, and -S_ord/V0 = -2.91 GPa. The Co3Ir control (row 21: -41.5 meV, slope 259) also matches. But this is not a regularity. It is a linear extrapolation of two numbers for one compound: any cell with E_ord near 0 and a nonzero ordering slope crosses zero at t = -E_ord/S_ord. Ni3Ir and Co3Ir have the same slope sign and similar size, so the only real contrast is E_ord(V0). Volume-dependent cluster expansion and the pressure-dependent ordering literature already give this, and the candidate admits CE can represent it. The 1.4 meV signal is below noise. It comes from a single seed=0 108-atom random cell. For equiatomic Ni-Ir, seeds 0/1/2 give E_mix -190.9/-192.4/-178.9 meV (13.5 meV spread) and slopes spread about 85 meV per unit lnV (data/h1_ev_rows_fixed.csv, data/binary_seeds.csv), so the crossing at t = -0.0065 is not resolved. MACE's MAE on ordered-cell energies vs PBE is 7.0 meV (ledger 7e0ff785d1), so even the sign at V0 is outside L1 accuracy. Ni magnetism is not separated out. Clamped equal-volume energies are also the wrong thermodynamic comparison under pressure. Letting each phase relax to its own volume already lowers E_ord by about S_ord^2/(2BV), roughly 1.3 meV at B about 230 GPa. So at P=0 the two phases are degenerate within that correction, and the real test would be dH(P), not dE at fixed t. Nothing here tests or corrects a mechanical-property formula."}

The 2:1 split has a physical reading Astra did not give: with nearest-neighbour central forces in fcc, C11:C12:C44 = 2:1:1, so C' = C44/2. The size of -14 implies r^2 phi''/phi of about -168, i.e. a steep effective bond (around r^-12). This is plausible but not derived. Problems: (a) Input noise. The E and K binaries come from the same seed 1 and 2 cells, so their errors are correlated. Per-cell noise (E 3.4 meV median, common shear 0.70 GPa) can carry up to about 15 to 25% of the h3 covariance. The proposed main test measures E and shear on the same cell, so it cannot separate a composition term from cell noise. E and shear targets need disjoint seeds. (c) Baseline. Against an intercept-only correction (the validate.py convention), hm gains about 8%, below the 10% gate. (d) No universal coefficient. With Co: -19/-11. Co-free: -9/-4 (h3) and -11/-1.6 (hm). (e) Both numeric predictions reproduce exactly, but they use the hm V0 11.959779, while the shear protocol uses ctx.vegard 11.949863 (a 0.17 GPa shift). Both compositions use seeds 1000 to 1009, so they share the (seed, n) random field; each needs its own seeds. Each test is at the 2 to 3 GPa noise level, so it cannot settle the claim. Prior work: the modulus vs mixing-enthalpy correlation is known (Temesi 2023), and tensorial CE expands Cij on the same cluster basis as the energy. I found no fixed-coefficient prediction of clamped shear residuals from the pair-rule energy residual with a 2:1 split. KEEP as L0 only if the pre-registration fixes (a) to (c): disjoint binary seeds for E and K, disjoint target seeds for E and shear, and an intercept-only baseline. Report and gate Co and Co-free separately."}

# Academic Paper Reviewer v1.11.1 - Multi-Perspective Academic Paper Review Agent Team

Simulates a complete international journal peer review process: automatically identifies the paper's field, dynamically configures 4 card-backed identities (Journal-Fit Reviewer + 3 peer reviewers), and adds the fixed Devil's Advocate as the fifth execution seat. The five role-separated perspectives cover journal fit, methodology, domain expertise, cross-disciplinary viewpoints, and core argument challenges; a separate editorial synthesizer produces the structured Editorial Decision and Revision Roadmap.

**v1.1 Improvements**:
1. Added Devil's Advocate Reviewer - specifically challenges core arguments, detects logical fallacies, and identifies the strongest counter-arguments
2. Added `re-review` mode - verification review, focused on checking whether revisions address the review comments
3. Expanded review team from 4 to 5 members

> **Routing discipline (v3.9.2):** see `.claude/CLAUDE.md` "Routing Discipline (v3.9.2)" + `shared/references/intent_clarification_protocol.md` for cross-skill routing rules. This skill assumes routing has already settled - ambiguous cross-phase materials should have been clarified upstream.

---

## Quick Start

**Simplest command:**
```
Review this paper: [paste paper or provide file]
```

**Output:**
1. Automatically identifies the paper's field and methodology type
2. Dynamically configures four card-backed reviewer identities; the fixed Devil's Advocate is the fifth execution seat
3. 5 role-separated review reports (4 configuration cards plus the fixed Devil's Advocate, with typed execution provenance)
4. 1 Editorial Decision Letter + Revision Roadmap

---

## Trigger Conditions

### Trigger Keywords

**English**: review paper, peer review, manuscript review, referee report, review my paper, critique paper, simulate review, editorial review, calibrate reviewer, reviewer calibration, measure reviewer accuracy

**???**: ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ???, ??? ???? ??, ??? ??, ?? ??? ??

**????**: ????, ????, ????, ????, ?????, ????????, ?????

### Non-Trigger Scenarios

| Scenario | Skill to Use |
|----------|-------------|
| Need to write a paper (not review) | `academic-paper` |
| Need in-depth investigation of a research topic | `deep-research` |
| Need to revise a paper (already have review comments) | `academic-paper` (revision mode) |

### Quick Mode Selection Guide

| Your Situation | Recommended Mode | Spectrum |
|----------------|-----------------|----------|
| Need comprehensive review (first submission) | full | balanced |
| Checking if revisions addressed comments | re-review | fidelity |
| Quick quality assessment (15 min) | quick | fidelity |
| Focus only on methods/statistics | methodology-focus | fidelity |
| Want to learn by doing (guided review) | guided | originality |
| Want to measure this reviewer's bounded decision-error profile on an adjudicated target set | calibration | fidelity |

**Spectrum** (v3.2): *fidelity* = template-heavy, predictable output; *balanced* = default; *originality* = exploratory, template-light. See `shared/mode_spectrum.md` for the full cross-skill spectrum table.

Not sure? Use `full` for pre-submission review, `re-review` for post-revision verification. Current live reviews and Schema 6 packages declare `NOT_CALIBRATED`; a full-tier calibration run may produce a bounded candidate profile, but live-profile application remains unavailable until its closed artifact and replay validator ship. `calibration` is opt-in: its default full tier measures bounded decision-level FNR/FPR, while the explicitly selected 3-paper directional tier gives only a low-cost Minor/Major boundary signal and remains `NOT_CALIBRATED`.

---

## Agent Team (7 Agents)

| # | Agent | Role | Phase |
|---|-------|------|-------|
| 1 | `field_analyst_agent` | Analyzes the paper's field and dynamically configures 4 card-backed identities; the Devil's Advocate remains a fixed fifth seat | Phase 0 |
| 2 | `eic_agent` | Journal-Fit Reviewer - journal fit, originality, overall quality; one panel card, no final-decision authority | Phase 1 |
| 3 | `methodology_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 1 - research design, statistical validity, reproducibility | Phase 1 |
| 4 | `domain_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 2 - literature coverage, theoretical framework, domain contribution | Phase 1 |
| 5 | `perspective_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 3 - cross-disciplinary connections, practical impact, challenging fundamental assumptions | Phase 1 |
| 6 | **`devils_advocate_reviewer_agent`** | **Devil's Advocate - core argument challenges, logical fallacy detection, strongest counter-arguments** | **Phase 1** |
| 7 | `editorial_synthesizer_agent` | Synthesizes all reviews, identifies consensus and disagreements, makes editorial decision | Phase 2 |

**Role-name compatibility (#611):** the public display name is **Journal-Fit Reviewer**. The stable implementation identifiers remain `eic_agent` (agent), `eic` (`contract_role` / dispatch role), and `EIC` (serialized reviewer/source ID, including `EIC-W<n>`). Those compatibility tokens do not select a Stage 3' agent file: `editorial_synthesizer_agent` emits first-round decisions, while contract-governed re-review uses its three dedicated calls and checker-derived outcome.

---

## Orchestration Workflow (3 Phases)

```
User: "Review this paper"
     |
=== Phase 0: FIELD ANALYSIS & PERSONA CONFIGURATION ===
     |
     +-> [field_analyst_agent] -> Reviewer Configuration Card (x4)
         - Reads the complete paper
         - Identifies: primary discipline, secondary discipline, research paradigm, methodology type, target journal tier, paper maturity
         - Dynamically generates specific identities for 4 card-backed reviewers:
           * Journal-Fit Reviewer (internal `EIC`): which journal/editor perspective, area of expertise, review preferences
           * Reviewer 1 (Methodology): Methodological expertise, what they particularly focus on
           * Reviewer 2 (Domain): Domain expertise, research interests
           * Reviewer 3 (Perspective): Cross-disciplinary angle, what unique perspective they bring
         - The fifth execution seat is the fixed Devil's Advocate, which receives no dynamic configuration card
     |
     ** Presents Reviewer Configuration to user for confirmation (adjustable) **
     |
=== Phase 1: PARALLEL MULTI-PERSPECTIVE REVIEW ===
     |
     |-> [eic_agent] -------> Journal-Fit Review Report
     |   - Journal fit, originality, significance, relevance to readership
     |   - Does not go deep into methodology (that's Reviewer 1's job)
     |   - One role-separated card among five - no peer-output channel before commitment (Iron Rule #2)
     |
     |-> [methodology_reviewer_agent] -> Methodology Review Report
     |   - Research design rigor, sampling strategy, data collection
     |   - Analysis method selection, statistical validity, effect sizes
     |   - Reproducibility, data transparency
     |
     |-> [domain_reviewer_agent] -------> Domain Review Report
     |   - Literature review completeness, theoretical framework appropriateness
     |   - Academic argument accuracy, incremental contribution to the field
     |   - Missing key references
     |
     |-> [perspective_reviewer_agent] --> Perspective Review Report
     |   - Cross-disciplinary connections and borrowing opportunities
     |   - Practical applications and policy implications
     |   - Broader social or ethical implications
     |
     +-> [devils_advocate_reviewer_agent] --> Devil's Advocate Report
         - Core argument challenges (strongest counter-arguments)
         - Cherry-picking detection
         - Confirmation bias detection
         - Logic chain validation
         - Overgeneralization detection
         - Alternative paths analysis
         - Stakeholder blind spots
         - "So what?" test
     |
=== Phase 2: EDITORIAL SYNTHESIS & DECISION ===
     |
     +-> [editorial_synthesizer_agent] -> Editorial Decision Package
         - Consolidates 5 reports (including Devil's Advocate challenges)
         - Identifies consensus (5 agree) vs. disagreement (divergent opinions)
         - Arbitration and argumentation for disputed issues
         - Devil's Advocate CRITICAL issues are specially flagged in the Editorial Decision
         - Editorial Decision Letter
         - Immutable non-ranking Revision Roadmap core (directly consumed with a separate explicit author sidecar)
     |
=== Phase 2.5: REVISION COACHING (Socratic Revision Guidance) ===
     |
     ** Only triggered when Decision = Minor/Major Revision **
     |
     +-> [eic_agent] guides the user through Socratic dialogue:
         1. Overall positioning - "After reading the review comments, what surprised you the most?"
         2. Core issue focus - Guides user to understand consensus issues
         3. Contribution framing probe - ask the Layer-5 later-stage anchored forms
            L5-W1 / L5-W2 / L5-W3 (single-sourced under Layer 5 in
            deep-research/agents/socratic_mentor_agent.md - read the question text
            there), anchored to what the manuscript already claims ("the revised
            paper"). Questions only - never propose, substitute, rank, expand, or
            select a contribution claim (Kong L2 verb test); the user answers.
         4. Explicit author triage - records `will_address`, `wont_address`, or `not_on_point` for every source-ordered item, with no inferred work order
         5. Counter-argument response - Guides user to think about how to respond to Devil's Advocate challenges
         6. Implementation planning - confirms exact block/operation scope and any registered-claim or declined-overlap authorization

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:406:41: def e_strained(atoms, v_atom, F):
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:407:42:     a = atoms.copy()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:408:43:     a.set_cell(a.cell * (v_atom * len(a) / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:409:44:     a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:410:45:     a.calc = calc
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:411:46:     t = time.perf_counter()

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:413:48:     time.sleep(time.perf_counter() - t)  # 50% duty cycle, keeps the laptop cool
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:414:49:     return e

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:418:53: def F_of(name, s):
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:419:54:     if name == "K44":
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:420:55:         F = np.eye(3)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:421:56:         F[0, 1] = s
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:422:57:         return F
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:423:58:     return np.diag([np.exp(s), np.exp(-s), 1.0])
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:424:59:

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:430:65:         em = [e_strained(alloy, v, F_of(name, s)) - sum(xi * e_strained(pures[el], v, F_of(name, s))

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:433:68:         out[name] = (2 * c2 if name == "K44" else c2 / 2) / v * GPA

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:493:.orchestra/LESSONS.md
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:494:1: # Lessons for derivation agents (Astra, Opus)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:495:2: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:496:3: Read before proposing. Each line is a way a candidate died or nearly died for the wrong reason. Updated 2026-10-31.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:497:4: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:498:5: 1. Ratios of energies blow up where the denominator crosses zero (R3: n_eff = -3 b/a reached -102 for Cu-Ir). Prefer
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:499:6:    predictions linear in measured quantities; if a ratio is essential, say where it is undefined.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:500:7: 2. Compare like with like: clamped with clamped, relaxed with relaxed, random with random. R3 compared a relaxed random
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:501:8:    volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:502:9: 3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:503:10:    that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:504:11: 4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:505:12:    to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:506:13: 5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:507:14:    input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:508:15: 6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:509:16:    (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:510:17: 7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:511:18:    carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:512:19: 8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:513:20:    so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:514:21:    (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:515:22: 9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:516:23:    ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:517:24:    multicomponent cells can be used.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:518:25: 10. Round R2 (Astra): the arena's permutation count capped the smallest reachable p at 1/501, so after five tests no
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:519:26:     candidate could pass however good it was. Fixed: n_perm grows with m. Also open: generators set V0 from nominal
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:520:27:     fractions while comp_actual differs (~0.5% in volume, ~0.06 meV RMSE effect, not the cause of k ~ 0.8).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:521:28: 11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:522:29:     energies at the alloy volume give k 0.94 [0.90, 0.98] and RMSE 10.3 meV with no parameter (data/binary_vgrid.csv).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:523:30: 12. Swarm S1 audit (Astra): (a) scripts/hiso_l12.py did not use ecut_elements, and harness/dft.py picks the k-grid
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:524:31:     from the strained cell (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18), so 0.1 meV/atom of strain-dependent error moves K by 1.6 to 4.7
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:525:32:     GPa. H-iso results before the fix are not evidence either way; the run is stopped. (b) fix_counts.py treated
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:526:33:     0.3333 as the reference weight of equiatomic ternaries (36+36+36 atoms are exact): +0.3 to +0.7 meV added.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:527:34:     (c) B_chem and R in *_fixed.csv are stale. (d) K44 ~ K' is not Zener invariance.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:528:35: 13. k at fixed composition (h1/h3 E(V) curves vs exact binary response): 0.976 [0.956, 1.001]. No reduced volume
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:529:36:     response; k ~ 0.8 is the curvature the linear transfer leaves out (94% of the shift).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:530:37: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:531:38: 14. Shear-curvature volume transfer (prereg 4c29d9754c, result 6e0923b413), 113 unseen h3 alloys, binary curvatures
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:532:39:     at the alloy volume, no parameter. Kp: 4.77 -> 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08 (pass). K44: 3.29 -> 2.62,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:533:40:     gain 0.20, p 0.023, refit k 0.86 (fail at p < 0.005). Joint claim FAIL. The first design (sigma = pair-sum residual,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:534:41:     which contains the signal) had power 0.45 and was stopped before any target existed. K44's worst rule errors are
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:535:42:     Co-rich (Co ~0.46 with Pt or Cu), where the rule is worse than no transfer; cause not yet audited (hypothesis,
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:536:43:     design or numerics). Do not re-split the joint claim after the fact: a K44 or Kp claim needs its own fresh test.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:537:44: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:538:45: 15. K' alone, fresh blind test (prereg 67a358fc59, result d92844787f, L2 entry recorded): 94 hm_fresh alloys, K' 4.22 ->
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:539:46:     1.89 GPa, gain 0.55, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08, 75/94 better. Two independent blind sets now agree for K' (k 1.08 both).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:540:47:     K44 again weaker (gain 0.12, k 0.69, not gated). Why K44 transfers worse than K' is open: Co-rich outliers, or
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:541:48:     internal (non-affine) relaxation channels that the clamped protocol suppresses differently for the two shears.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:542:49: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:543:50: 16. Model swap of the K' rule (prereg 851aec6883, result 86767e478d): medium-mpa-0, same geometry, same 94 hm_fresh
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:544:51:     alloys, binaries seed 0 only. K' 4.73 -> 2.28 GPa, gain 0.52, p 2.5e-4, but refit k 1.33 [1.11, 1.51]: the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:545:52:     pre-registered k-contains-1 condition FAILS. K44 gain 0.16, k 0.77. Reading: that the alloy's K' follows the binaries
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:546:53:     at the alloy volume and cuts the error in half survives a model with a different shear bias; that the coefficient is
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:547:54:     exactly 1 does not (omat 1.08 twice, mpa 1.33). Binary seed noise would pull k down, not up. The two models disagree
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:548:55:     most at |dlnV| > 0.2 (K' corr 0.80 vs 0.96 within 0.1). Cause not yet audited. Do not claim "parameter-free" across
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:549:56:     models; the PBE check decides which k is physical.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:550:57: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:551:58: 17. K44 transfer fails only with Co (prereg e410c96a32, result d9460850ce). 120 fresh Co-free alloys: K44 pair 4.68 ->
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:552:59:     rule 2.30 GPa, gain 0.51, p 2.5e-4, k 1.23 (PASS). 60 fresh alloys with Co >= 15%: gain 0.11, p 0.08, k 0.70. K'
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:553:60:     passes in both. Open confound: the Co-free set has a larger volume signal (pair error 4.68 vs 3.36), so "Co breaks

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:976:36: def site_counts(comp: dict[str, float], n: int) -> dict[str, int]:

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:982:42: def actual_fractions(atoms: Atoms) -> dict[str, float]:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:983:43:     """Composition the cell really has. Subtract pure references with these, not the nominal fractions (the

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:990:50:     """Random solid solution on a cubic conventional supercell (no SQS optimisation). Counts are rounded to whole

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:993:53:     atoms = bulk("X", lattice, a=a, cubic=True).repeat((reps, reps, reps))

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:995:55:     symbols = [el for el, c in counts.items() for _ in range(c)]
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:996:56:     np.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle(symbols)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:997:57:     atoms.set_chemical_symbols(symbols)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:998:58:     return atoms

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1017:77: def elastic_tensor(atoms: Atoms, eps: float = 0.005, relax_ions: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1018:78:     """Full 6x6 Voigt tensor (GPa) from central differences of stress, ions relaxed at each strain."""
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1019:79:     cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1020:80:     C = np.zeros((6, 6))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1021:81:     voigt = [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1)]
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1022:82:     for j, (k, l) in enumerate(voigt):
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1023:83:         sig = []
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1024:84:         for s in (+eps, -eps):
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1025:85:             e = np.zeros((3, 3))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1026:86:             if k == l:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1027:87:                 e[k, k] = s
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1028:88:             else:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1029:89:                 e[k, l] = e[l, k] = s / 2  # engineering shear strain = s
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1030:90:             strained = atoms.copy()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1031:91:             strained.set_cell(cell0 @ (np.eye(3) + e), scale_atoms=True)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1032:92:             strained.calc = calculator()
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1033:93:             if relax_ions and len(strained) > 1:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1034:94:                 relax(strained, cell=False, fmax=5e-4)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1035:95:             sig.append(strained.get_stress(voigt=True) * GPA)  # ASE: tensile stress positive
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1036:96:         C[:, j] = (sig[0] - sig[1]) / (2 * eps)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1037:97:     return 0.5 * (C + C.T)

.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1041:harness/power.py
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1042:1: """Power check for a pre-registered test, run before the test data exist.
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1043:2: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1044:3: A test is only informative if (a) data generated with the hypothesis TRUE, at realistic noise, pass it most of the
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1045:4: time and (b) data with the hypothesis FALSE rarely pass. Both are estimated by simulation. Two failures this tool is
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1046:5: meant to catch, from 2026-10-31: the L3 ordered-cell design (an intercept absorbed the rule's main signal) and R3
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1047:6: (the observable compared relaxed with clamped volumes, so even the exact formula had slope 0.20).
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1048:7: """
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1049:8: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1050:9: from __future__ import annotations
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1051:10: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1052:11: from typing import Callable
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1053:12: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1054:13: import numpy as np
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1055:14: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1056:15: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1057:16: def power(test: Callable[[object], bool], simulate_true: Callable[[np.random.Generator], object],
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1058:17:           simulate_null: Callable[[np.random.Generator], object], n: int = 300, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1059:18:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1060:19:     p = np.mean([bool(test(simulate_true(rng))) for _ in range(n)])
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1061:20:     f = np.mean([bool(test(simulate_null(rng))) for _ in range(n)])
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1062:21:     return {"power": round(float(p), 3), "false_pass": round(float(f), 3), "n_sims": n}
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1063:22: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1064:23: 
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1065:24: def near_zero_divisor(x, name: str, frac: float = 0.1) -> list[int]:
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1066:25:     """Indices where a quantity used as a divisor is small relative to its spread (ratio predictions blow up there)."""
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1067:26:     x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1068:27:     bad = np.flatnonzero(np.abs(x) < frac * np.std(x))
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1069:28:     if len(bad):
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1070:29:         print(f"warning: {name} near zero at rows {bad.tolist()}; a ratio-based prediction is unstable there")
.orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:1071:30:     return bad.tolist()

"""Is the volume-transfer gain a reference-state effect? Compare, on clamped E_mix(V0) of multicomponent alloys:
 pair    : sum 4 x_i x_j E_ij(V_ij)                     (L2 baseline, references at the common volume)
 transfer: sum 4 x_i x_j E_ij(V0) exact, from binary_vgrid splines (k_direct, no parameter)
 own-ref : Muggianu of binary formation energies (pures at their own volumes), converted back:
           sum 4 x_i x_j F_ij - sum x_i [e_i(V0) - e_i(V_i)],  F_ij = E_ij(V_ij) + mean_k [e_k(V_ij) - e_k(V_k)]
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(r"C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science"); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
from harness.context import context
from harness.features import parse_comp
SP = Path(r"C:/Users/can02/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-can02-Projects-AI-driven-Science/3207d5f7-4dac-4457-8adb-411f78b4d2c2/scratchpad")
ctx = context()
pe = pd.read_csv(SP/"pure_ev.csv")
ES = {el: CubicSpline(np.log(g.V), g.E) for el, g in pe.groupby("el")}
pv = {el: ctx.pure[el]["V"] for el in ctx.pure}

rm = lambda x: float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(x))))*1000
def signflip(y, a, b, n=20000):
    d = (y-b)**2-(y-a)**2; rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    null = np.array([np.mean(d*rng.choice([-1, 1], len(d))) for _ in range(n)]); return (np.sum(null >= d.mean())+1)/(n+1)
# how much of D_ij is the strained-pure pressure?
Dp = {k: -0.5*sum(float(ES[el](np.log(p["V"]), 1)) for el in k) for k, p in ctx.pair.items()}
ks = sorted(ctx.pair); D = np.array([ctx.pair[k]["D"] for k in ks]); P = np.array([Dp[k] for k in ks])
print(f"binary D_ij vs strained-pure term -mean_k de_k/dlnV(V_ij): n {len(ks)} corr {np.corrcoef(D, P)[0,1]:.3f}  slope {np.polyfit(P, D, 1)[0]:.2f}  rms D {np.sqrt(np.mean(D**2)):.3f}  rms(D-P) {np.sqrt(np.mean((D-P)**2)):.3f} eV")
for f in ("h1_ev_rows_fixed.csv", "h3_fresh_rows_fixed.csv", "hm_fresh_rows_fixed.csv"):
    df = pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data"/f); df = df[df.n_el >= 3]
    rows = []
    for r in df.itertuples():
        c = parse_comp(r.comp_actual)
        if not all((a, b) in VS for a, b, _, _ in ctx.pairs(c)): continue
        v0 = ctx.vegard(c)
        L = {(a, b): np.log(v0/ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"]) for a, b, _, _ in ctx.pairs(c)}
        pair = sum(4*xa*xb*ctx.pair[(a, b)]["E"] for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))
        lin = sum(4*xa*xb*ctx.pair[(a, b)]["D"]*L[(a, b)] for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))
        tr = sum(4*xa*xb*float(VS[(a, b)](L[(a, b)])) for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))
        own = sum(4*xa*xb*F[(a, b)] for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c)) - sum(x*de(el, v0) for el, x in c.items())
        rows.append((r.E_mix, pair, pair+lin, pair+0.81*lin, tr, own))
    a = np.array(rows); y = a[:, 0]
    print(f"{f:24s} n {len(a):3d} RMSE meV  pair {rm(y-a[:,1]):5.1f} | champion k=1 {rm(y-a[:,2]):5.1f}  k=0.81 {rm(y-a[:,3]):5.1f}  exact {rm(y-a[:,4]):5.1f} | own-ref Muggianu {rm(y-a[:,5]):5.1f}"

Independent audit of a pre-registered PBE test. You did not write it. Do not edit files.

Criterion (ledger claims/claims.jsonl id 6cb3c2a936, registered before any output): H-iso holds in PBE iff among cells with max(|K44|,|Kp|) > 10 GPa (need n >= 4): all K44, Kp same sign and median K44/Kp in [0.75, 1.33]. MACE passes L1 for this quantity iff sign of K44 and Kp agrees with PBE in all cells and median |MACE-PBE| <= 30% of median |PBE|.

Code: scripts/hiso_l12_v2.py (v2 fixes the S1 audit: shared cutoff and k-grid for alloy and pure refs), harness/dft.py. Results: data/hiso_l12_dft_v2.csv (PBE, 8 cells), data/hiso_l12_mace.csv. Raw runs under data/dft_runs/hiso2/. A dense-k check (kspacing 0.08, Cu3Ir and Ag3Rh) is running now and is not available.

My reading: n=6 (Cu3Ir Cu3Rh Au3Ir Ag3Ir Ag3Rh Pt3Cu), each cell has K44 and Kp of the same sign, median ratio 0.94, so H-iso PASS in PBE; Ag cells are off (0.54, 0.39) and Pt3Cu is 2.6. MACE L1 FAIL (K44 sign wrong in Pd3Ir, Au3Ir, Ag3Rh; median |diff| 53% of median |PBE|).

Check: (1) is "all K44, Kp same sign" fairly read per cell, or does the text demand one global sign (Pt3Cu is a positive control)? Say which reading the registration supports and the verdict under each. (2) numerics: strain size, three-point curvature, symmetry shortcut (g-/t- copied from g+/t+ except Cu3Ir), unit conversion of K44 and Kp, Vegard volume, same cutoff/k for refs, convergence of the output files (scf converged, no warnings). (3) selection effects or criterion drift. (4) whether the result says anything about the paper's K' transfer rule (paper/draft_v3.md), which rests on MACE mixing shear curvatures.
End with one line: VERDICT PASS / FAIL / PLAUSIBLE for H-iso in PBE, and one line for MACE L1.

"""Quantum ESPRESSO (pw.x in WSL) as the L3 reference for stresses and elastic constants.

QE lives in a conda-forge env inside WSL (micromamba env "qe", no sudo needed).
Pseudopotentials: SSSP 1.3.0 PBE efficiency, md5 a58f1b3373f330179fd0832c48bb9a52,
Materials Cloud Archive 2023.65, doi:10.24435/materialscloud:f3-ym.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from ase import Atoms
from ase.io import read, write

from harness.compute import GPA, cubic_average, voigt_reuss_hill

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RUNS = ROOT / "data" / "dft_runs"
DISTRO = "Ubuntu-22.04"
PSEUDO_DIR = "/home/can02/pseudo/sssp_eff_1.3"
SSSP = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "data" / "sssp_1.3.0_pbe_efficiency.json").read_text())

# Collinear starting moments for the magnetic 3d metals. Cr gets an antiferromagnetic
# start on the two bcc sublattices; a commensurate AFM cell is an approximation of its SDW.
MAGNETIC = {"Fe": 0.4, "Co": 0.4, "Ni": 0.3, "Mn": 0.4, "Cr": 0.4}


@dataclass
class Settings:
    kspacing: float = 0.15          # 1/A, Monkhorst-Pack density (2*pi included)
    ecut_scale: float = 1.25        # stresses need a margin above the SSSP energy cutoff
    degauss: float = 0.01           # Ry, Marzari-Vanderbilt
    np: int = 8                     # 8 physical cores
    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    # Elements whose cutoffs also set this run's cutoff. For mixing energies and curvatures pass the alloy's elements
    # to the pure references too, so all terms share one basis (before 2026-10-31 each run used only its own).
    ecut_elements: tuple = ()
    # Fixed Monkhorst-Pack grid. Finite-strain curvatures must use one grid for every strain; the default picks it from
    # the strained cell, which changes it between strains (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18 for Cu3Ir, found 2026-10-31).
    kpts: tuple | None = None


def wsl_path(p: Path) -> str:
    s = str(p.resolve()).replace("\\", "/")
    return f"/mnt/{s[0].lower()}{s[2:]}"


def kgrid(atoms: Atoms, kspacing: float) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    rec = np.linalg.norm(atoms.cell.reciprocal(), axis=1) * 2 * np.pi
    return tuple(max(1, int(np.ceil(r / kspacing))) for r in rec)


def magnetize(atoms: Atoms) -> bool:
    """Set initial moments in place; AFM checkerboard for Cr. Returns True if spin polarised."""
    mags = np.array([MAGNETIC.get(s, 0.0) for s in atoms.get_chemical_symbols()])
    if not mags.any():
        return False
    if "Cr" in atoms.get_chemical_symbols():
        a = (2 * atoms.get_volume() / len(atoms)) ** (1 / 3)  # bcc conventional lattice parameter
        parity = np.round(2 * atoms.positions[:, 0] / a).astype(int) % 2  # corner vs body centre
        mags = np.where(np.array(atoms.get_chemical_symbols()) == "Cr", mags * (1 - 2 * parity), mags)
    atoms.set_initial_magnetic_moments(mags * 5)  # ASE maps moments to starting_magnetization
    return True


def run_pw(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, relax_ions: bool = False) -> Atoms:
    """Run one pw.x scf/relax with stress. Cached: an existing finished output is reused."""
    d = RUNS / tag
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = d / "pw.out"
    els = sorted(set(atoms.get_chemical_symbols()))
    basis = set(els) | set(s.ecut_elements)
    ecut = float(s.extra.get("system.ecutwfc", s.ecut_scale * max(SSSP[e]["cutoff_wfc"] for e in basis)))
    ecutrho = s.ecut_scale * max(SSSP[e]["cutoff_rho"] for e in basis)
    if out.exists() and "JOB DONE" in out.read_text(errors="ignore"):
        cached = re.search(r"ecutwfc\s*=\s*([\d.]+)", (d / "pw.in").read_text())
        if cached and abs(float(cached.group(1)) - ecut) > 1e-6:  # a cache hit must not silently change the basis
            raise RuntimeError(f"{tag}: cached run used ecutwfc {cached.group(1)}, requested {ecut}; use a new tag")
        return read(out, format="espresso-out", index=-1)
    scratch = tag.replace("/", "__")
    atoms = atoms.copy()
    # extra={'system.nspin': 1} must switch magnetism off: initial moments make ASE write nspin 2 back (S3 audit)
    spin = s.extra.get("system.nspin", 2) != 1 and magnetize(atoms)
    data = {"control": {"calculation": "relax" if relax_ions else "scf", "tstress": True,
                        "tprnfor": True, "pseudo_dir": PSEUDO_DIR, "outdir": f"/tmp/qe/{scratch}",
                        "disk_io": "low", "forc_conv_thr": 1e-4},
            "system": {"ecutwfc": ecut, "ecutrho": ecutrho, "occupations": "smearing",
                       "smearing": "mv", "degauss": s.degauss, "nspin": 2 if spin else 1},
            "electrons": {"conv_thr": 1e-10 * len(atoms), "mixing_beta": 0.3}}
    for k, v in s.extra.items():
        data.setdefault(k.split(".")[0], {})[k.split(".")[1]] = v
    write(d / "pw.in", atoms, format="espresso-in", input_data=data,
          pseudopotentials={e: SSSP[e]["filename"] for e in els}, kpts=s.kpts or kgrid(atoms, s.kspacing))
    cmd = (f"export MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX=~/mamba OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; mkdir -p /tmp/qe/{scratch}; cd '{wsl_path(d)}' && "
           f"~/bin/micromamba run -n qe mpirun -np {s.np} pw.x -nk {min(s.np, 4)} -in pw.in > pw.out 2> pw.err; "
           f"rm -rf /tmp/qe/{scratch}")
    subprocess.run(["wsl", "-d", DISTRO, "--", "bash", "-lc", cmd], check=True)
    text = out.read_text(errors="ignore")
    if "JOB DONE" not in text or "convergence NOT achieved" in text:
        raise RuntimeError(f"pw.x failed for {tag}, see {out}")
    return read(out, format="espresso-out", index=-1)


def stress(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, relax_ions: bool) -> np.ndarray:
    return read_stress(run_pw(atoms, tag, s, relax_ions))


def read_stress(a: Atoms) -> np.ndarray:
    return a.get_stress(voigt=True) * GPA  # ASE sign: tensile positive


def elastic_cubic(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, eps: float = 0.01, full: bool = False,
                  relax_ions: bool | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """6x6 tensor (GPa) by central differences. full=False uses only e_xx and e_yz,
    which is exact for a cubic crystal and enough for pure elements (4 pw.x runs)."""
    if relax_ions is None:
        relax_ions = len(set(atoms.get_chemical_symbols())) > 1
    cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
    voigt = [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1)]
    cols = range(6) if full else (0, 3)
    C = np.full((6, 6), np.nan)
    for j in cols:
        k, l = voigt[j]
        sig = []
        for sign in (+1, -1):
            e = np.zeros((3, 3))
            if k == l:
                e[k, k] = sign * eps
            else:
                e[k, l] = e[l, k] = sign * eps / 2
            st = atoms.copy()
            st.set_cell(cell0 @ (np.eye(3) + e), scale_atoms=True)
            sig.append(stress(st, f"{tag}/e{j}{'p' if sign > 0 else 'm'}", s, relax_ions))
        C[:, j] = (sig[0] - sig[1]) / (2 * eps)
    if not full:  # fill the cubic tensor from the two columns
        c11, c12, c44 = C[0, 0], 0.5 * (C[1, 0] + C[2, 0]), C[3, 3]
        C = np.zeros((6, 6))
        C[:3, :3] = c12
        np.fill_diagonal(C[:3, :3], c11)
        C[3:, 3:] = np.eye(3) * c44
    return 0.5 * (C + C.T)


def relax_lattice(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, eps: float = 0.01) -> Atoms:
    """Cubic lattice parameter from a parabola fit of pressure vs volume (3 pw.x runs).
    Avoids vc-relax Pulay stress issues and keeps every run cached and inspectable."""
    cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
    scales = np.array([1 - eps, 1.0, 1 + eps])
    P = []
    for sc in scales:
        a = atoms.copy()
        a.set_cell(cell0 * sc, scale_atoms=True)
        sig = stress(a, f"{tag}/lat{sc:.3f}", s, relax_ions=len(set(a.symbols)) > 1)
        P.append(-sig[:3].mean())
    root = np.roots(np.polyfit(scales, P, 2))
    root = root[np.isreal(root)].real
    best = root[np.argmin(abs(root - 1))]
    out = atoms.copy()
    out.set_cell(cell0 * best, scale_atoms=True)
    return out


def run_alloy(comp_atoms: Atoms, label: str, s: Settings, full: bool | None = None) -> dict:
    full = (len(set(comp_atoms.symbols)) > 1) if full is None else full
    tag = f"{label}_k{s.kspacing}_e{s.ecut_scale}"
    a = relax_lattice(comp_atoms, tag, s)
    c11, c12, c44 = cubic_average(elastic_cubic(a, tag, s, full=full))
    row = {"label": label, "formula": a.get_chemical_formula(mode="metal"), "natoms": len(a),
           "vol_per_atom": a.get_volume() / len(a), "C11": c11, "C12": c12, "C44": c44,
           "method": f"QE7.6 PBE SSSP1.3eff k{s.kspacing} ecut x{s.ecut_scale} mv{s.degauss}",
           "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    row.update(voigt_reuss_hill(c11, c12, c44))
    return row

# Lessons for derivation agents (Astra, Opus)

Read before proposing. Each line is a way a candidate died or nearly died for the wrong reason. Updated 2026-10-31.

1. Ratios of energies blow up where the denominator crosses zero (R3: n_eff = -3 b/a reached -102 for Cu-Ir). Prefer
   predictions linear in measured quantities; if a ratio is essential, say where it is undefined.
2. Compare like with like: clamped with clamped, relaxed with relaxed, random with random. R3 compared a relaxed random
   volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
   that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
   to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
   input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
   (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
   carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
   so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
   (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
   ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
   multicomponent cells can be used.
10. Round R2 (Astra): the arena's permutation count capped the smallest reachable p at 1/501, so after five tests no
    candidate could pass however good it was. Fixed: n_perm grows with m. Also open: generators set V0 from nominal
    fractions while comp_actual differs (~0.5% in volume, ~0.06 meV RMSE effect, not the cause of k ~ 0.8).
11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary
    energies at the alloy volume give k 0.94 [0.90, 0.98] and RMSE 10.3 meV with no parameter (data/binary_vgrid.csv).
12. Swarm S1 audit (Astra): (a) scripts/hiso_l12.py did not use ecut_elements, and harness/dft.py picks the k-grid
    from the strained cell (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18), so 0.1 meV/atom of strain-dependent error moves K by 1.6 to 4.7
    GPa. H-iso results before the fix are not evidence either way; the run is stopped. (b) fix_counts.py treated
    0.3333 as the reference weight of equiatomic ternaries (36+36+36 atoms are exact): +0.3 to +0.7 meV added.
    (c) B_chem and R in *_fixed.csv are stale. (d) K44 ~ K' is not Zener invariance.
13. k at fixed composition (h1/h3 E(V) curves vs exact binary response): 0.976 [0.956, 1.001]. No reduced volume
    response; k ~ 0.8 is the curvature the linear transfer leaves out (94% of the shift).

14. Shear-curvature volume transfer (prereg 4c29d9754c, result 6e0923b413), 113 unseen h3 alloys, binary curvatures
    at the alloy volume, no parameter. Kp: 4.77 -> 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08 (pass). K44: 3.29 -> 2.62,
    gain 0.20, p 0.023, refit k 0.86 (fail at p < 0.005). Joint claim FAIL. The first design (sigma = pair-sum residual,
    which contains the signal) had power 0.45 and was stopped before any target existed. K44's worst rule errors are
    Co-rich (Co ~0.46 with Pt or Cu), where the rule is worse than no transfer; cause not yet audited (hypothesis,
    design or numerics). Do not re-split the joint claim after the fact: a K44 or Kp claim needs its own fresh test.

15. K' alone, fresh blind test (prereg 67a358fc59, result d92844787f, L2 entry recorded): 94 hm_fresh alloys, K' 4.22 ->
    1.89 GPa, gain 0.55, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08, 75/94 better. Two independent blind sets now agree for K' (k 1.08 both).
    K44 again weaker (gain 0.12, k 0.69, not gated). Why K44 transfers worse than K' is open: Co-rich outliers, or
    internal (non-affine) relaxation channels that the clamped protocol suppresses differently for the two shears.

16. Model swap of the K' rule (prereg 851aec6883, result 86767e478d): medium-mpa-0, same geometry, same 94 hm_fresh
    alloys, binaries seed 0 only. K' 4.73 -> 2.28 GPa, gain 0.52, p 2.5e-4, but refit k 1.33 [1.11, 1.51]: the
    pre-registered k-contains-1 condition FAILS. K44 gain 0.16, k 0.77. Reading: that the alloy's K' follows the binaries
    at the alloy volume and cuts the error in half survives a model with a different shear bias; that the coefficient is
    exactly 1 does not (omat 1.08 twice, mpa 1.33). Binary seed noise would pull k down, not up. The two models disagree
    most at |dlnV| > 0.2 (K' corr 0.80 vs 0.96 within 0.1). Cause not yet audited. Do not claim "parameter-free" across
    models; the PBE check decides which k is physical.

17. K44 transfer fails only with Co (prereg e410c96a32, result d9460850ce). 120 fresh Co-free alloys: K44 pair 4.68 ->
    rule 2.30 GPa, gain 0.51, p 2.5e-4, k 1.23 (PASS). 60 fresh alloys with Co >= 15%: gain 0.11, p 0.08, k 0.70. K'
    passes in both. Open confound: the Co-free set has a larger volume signal (pair error 4.68 vs 3.36), so "Co breaks
    K44" and "K44 needs a large signal" are not yet separated; match the two sets on |rule - pair| before claiming
    a Co mechanism (magnetism is a guess, MACE has no spin).
    Confound check (exploratory, same fresh rows, tertiles of |rule - pair|): at matched signal Co-free gain 0.37 / 0.58
    vs Co 0.08 / 0.22 (mid / large), and Co alloys carry a larger floor at small signal (rule rms 2.61 vs 1.73 GPa).
    The Co effect survives signal matching; not yet a registered claim.

18. Why K44 looked broken (Opus, swarm S2, blind by file timestamp, confirmed on 60 Co alloys). The part the pair rule
    misses is the same in both shears (corr 0.71, slope ~1). K44's volume signal is half of K''s, so the shared floor
    swamps it; in Co alloys the floor anticorrelates with the signal and drags k to 0.7. Remove the floor (A = K44 - K'
    or e' as covariate) and K44 transfers with k ~1. LESSONS 14-16 failure reason: design, not hypothesis.

19. Shared SQS seed leak (Opus S2 audit, Astra confirmed). compute.py:56 draws the site permutation from (seed, n)
    only, so every seed-0 cell thresholds one random field: seed-0 targets and seed-0 binaries share configuration
    noise. K' is immune (gain 0.55-0.58, k 1.07-1.10 for every seed split). K44 is not: leak-free gain 0.06-0.14,
    k 0.60-0.77. d9460850ce and the LESSONS 18 Co check used the leak; 9cfc8edaf0 was withdrawn before reading and
    re-registered as c2eff007ad with target seed 100. Rule: targets and inputs never share a seed.

20. Shared floor, disjoint seeds (c2eff007ad -> b86e0d8a40 PASS, 150 alloys): A = K44 - K' transfers (gain 0.49),
    corr(e44, e') 0.77, joint k 0.91, b 0.94; plain K44 Co-free gain 0.47, Co 0.09. Astra audit: PLAUSIBLE, the
    null could not separate a compositional floor from same-cell noise. A shared-channel claim needs targets for the
    two channels from different cells. Test fd786169e3.

21. The shared floor is compositional (fd786169e3 PASS, two cells per composition, unique seeds): cross-cell corr
    0.75 vs same-cell 0.79, k 0.92, b 0.95; Astra audit PLAUSIBLE (cell noise ~5% of the shared covariance). Next
    doubt is a known identity: clamped curvatures carry the initial stress, K44 = C44 + s_yy, K' = C' + (s_xx+s_yy)/2.
    A floor claim must survive subtracting it (k_floor_stress.py). Pre-register every step; one audit, one test.

22. The floor survives the known pre-stress identity (ede47f1d65 PASS; Astra PLAUSIBLE): corrected cross-cell r
    0.67, k 0.99, b 0.79. Mixing pre-stress is 7 GPa rms but pair-additive (rule leaves 0.7 GPa), so it was never the
    floor. Remaining doubt: error shared through the binary references (b drops to 0.4-0.5 with single disjoint
    seeds). Shared-residual claims need two independent binary panels, as in k_mpa_equiv.py.
23. k = 1 is retired (88b9465108 FAIL, cause hypothesis; Astra found no coding error). Under mpa, 1200 alloys: k 1.14
    [1.10, 1.18]; the rule still halves the error (4.81 to 2.21 GPa). k is not a model constant but composition
    dependent: 3 elements 1.00, Cu-free 1.00, Cu 1.24, alloys with max|dlnV| > 0.25 1.41; omat shows the same pattern
    (1.11). The pair transfer under-predicts at large size mismatch. A power sim that treats the target residual as
    cell noise is optimistic: most of it is compositional and does not average out over cells.
"""H-iso check in cubic L1_2 cells: clamped mixing shear curvatures K44, Kp with MACE or PBE.

python scripts/hiso_l12.py mace | dft
A3B L1_2 (4-atom cubic cell, B on the corner site), clamped at Vegard volume, pure fcc references at the same volume
and the same deformation. Strains +-0.02 (three-point curvature). PBE uses kspacing 0.10 (shear needs the fine grid).
"""

import datetime as dt
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402

from harness.compute import GPA  # noqa: E402

CELLS = [("Cu", "Ir"), ("Cu", "Rh"), ("Pd", "Ir"), ("Au", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Rh"),  # A3B with Ir/Rh
         ("Cu", "Au"), ("Pt", "Cu")]  # controls without Ir/Rh; order = MACE |K| (PBE is slow, strongest first)
S = 0.02
SYM_DONE = {"Cu3Ir": ("g-", "t-")}  # computed both signs here; used as the symmetry check
METHOD = sys.argv[1]
pv = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv").set_index("el")["vol_per_atom"]

if METHOD == "mace":
    from harness import compute
    calc = compute.calculator()

    def energy(atoms, tag):
        atoms.calc = calc
        return atoms.get_potential_energy() / len(atoms)
else:
    from harness import dft
    st = dft.Settings(kspacing=0.10, np=int(os.environ.get("HISO_NP", "4")))

    def energy(atoms, tag):
        return dft.run_pw(atoms, f"hiso/{tag}", st).get_potential_energy() / len(atoms)

DEF = {"0": np.eye(3), "g+": np.eye(3) + S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
       "g-": np.eye(3) - S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
       "t+": np.diag([np.exp(S), np.exp(-S), 1.0]), "t-": np.diag([np.exp(-S), np.exp(S), 1.0])}


def strained(symbols, v, F):
    a = bulk("Cu", "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True)
    a.symbols = list(symbols)
    a.set_cell(a.cell * (v * 4 / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
    a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
    return a

python scripts/hiso_l12_v2.py [dense]
Fixes found by the swarm S1 audit in scripts/hiso_l12.py: the alloy and both pure references now share one cutoff
(ecut_elements = (A, B)) and one k-grid, taken from the unstrained cell, for every strain. "dense" repeats Cu3Ir and
Ag3Rh at kspacing 0.08 as a convergence check. Criteria 6cb3c2a936 are unchanged; the old results are not used.
A3B L1_2 (4-atom cubic cell, B on the corner site), clamped at Vegard volume, pure fcc references at the same volume
and the same deformation. Strains +-0.02 (three-point curvature). PBE uses kspacing 0.10 (shear needs the fine grid).
"""

import datetime as dt
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402

from harness.compute import GPA  # noqa: E402

CELLS = [("Cu", "Ir"), ("Cu", "Rh"), ("Pd", "Ir"), ("Au", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Rh"),  # A3B with Ir/Rh
         ("Cu", "Au"), ("Pt", "Cu")]  # controls without Ir/Rh; order = MACE |K| (PBE is slow, strongest first)
S = 0.02
SYM_DONE = {"Cu3Ir": ("g-", "t-")}  # computed both signs here; used as the symmetry check
METHOD = "dft"
DENSE = "dense" in sys.argv
KSP = 0.08 if DENSE else 0.10
if DENSE:
    CELLS = [("Cu", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Rh")]
pv = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv").set_index("el")["vol_per_atom"]

from harness import dft  # noqa: E402

NP = int(os.environ.get("HISO_NP", "2"))
ST = {}


def energy(atoms, tag):
    return dft.run_pw(atoms, f"hiso2{'d' if DENSE else ''}/{tag}", ST["s"]).get_potential_energy() / len(atoms)

DEF = {"0": np.eye(3), "g+": np.eye(3) + S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
       "g-": np.eye(3) - S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
       "t+": np.diag([np.exp(S), np.exp(-S), 1.0]), "t-": np.diag([np.exp(-S), np.exp(S), 1.0])}


def strained(symbols, v, F):
    a = bulk("Cu", "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True)
    a.symbols = list(symbols)
    a.set_cell(a.cell * (v * 4 / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
    a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
    return a


OUT = ROOT / "data" / f"hiso_l12_dft_v2{'_dense' if DENSE else ''}.csv"
done = set(pd.read_csv(OUT)["cell"]) if OUT.exists() else set()
for A, B in CELLS:
    name = f"{A}3{B}"
    if name in done:
        continue
    v = 0.75 * pv[A] + 0.25 * pv[B]
    vt = f"{v:.3f}"
    ST["s"] = dft.Settings(kspacing=KSP, np=NP, ecut_elements=(A, B),
                           kpts=dft.kgrid(strained([B, A, A, A], v, np.eye(3)), KSP))
    em = {}
    for k, F in DEF.items():
        if k in ("g-", "t-") and k not in SYM_DONE.get(name, ()):  # cubic L1_2: y -> -y and x <-> y are symmetries
            continue
        e_ab = energy(strained([B, A, A, A], v, F), f"{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
        e_a = energy(strained([A] * 4, v, F), f"{A}_{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
        e_b = energy(strained([B] * 4, v, F), f"{B}_{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
        em[k] = e_ab - 0.75 * e_a - 0.25 * e_b
    em.setdefault("g-", em["g+"])
    em.setdefault("t-", em["t+"])
    c44 = (em["g+"] + em["g-"] - 2 * em["0"]) / (2 * S**2)   # E = c s^2
    cp = (em["t+"] + em["t-"] - 2 * em["0"]) / (2 * S**2)
    r = {"cell": name, "method": "dft_v2", "kpts": "x".join(map(str, ST["s"].kpts)), "V": v, "E_mix": em["0"], "K44": 2 * c44 / v * GPA, "Kp": cp / (2 * v) * GPA,
         "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(OUT, mode="a", header=not OUT.exists(), index=False)
    print(name, f"E_mix {em['0']*1000:+7.1f} meV  K44 {r['K44']:+7.2f}  Kp {r['Kp']:+7.2f} GPa", flush=True)

1: # Binary shear curvatures read at the alloy's volume: a preregistered test of a transfer rule for fcc solid solutions with machine-learned potentials
2: 
3: Muhammet Can Ergani���
4: Independent researcher, METU graduate, Ankara, T���rkiye. ORCID 0009-0001-1397-6366
5: 
6: Draft v3, 2026-11-01, after the Astra audit of v2 (`.orchestra/audits/draft_v2_astra.md`). Numerical provenance is
7: given through ledger entries in `claims/claims.jsonl` and named analysis files. Exploratory calculations are marked
8: as such and kept apart from preregistered tests. The only open item before submission is the archive DOI.
9: 
10: ## Abstract
11: 
12: Building on established binary extrapolation, volume-dependent interactions and tensorial cluster expansions, we test
13: one specific, fixed-coefficient prescription for the clamped mixing part of the tetragonal shear curvature K' of
14: random fcc solid solutions: each equiatomic binary curvature is evaluated at the multicomponent alloy's Vegard volume
15: rather than at the binary's own. For 3 to 5 component alloys of Ag, Au, Co, Cu, Ir, Ni, Pd, Pt and Rh evaluated with
16: the MACE machine-learned potential, this halves the error of the same pair sum taken at the binary volumes (4.2 to
17: 1.9 GPa on 94 compositions; 4.8 to 2.2 GPa on 1200 further compositions under a second MACE model). The transfer is
18: not exact. The refit slope is 1.08 under one model and 1.14 (90% CI 1.10 to 1.18) under the other, and in
19: exploratory splits it rises with the size mismatch between components, so the rule under-predicts alloys with large
20: volume differences. For the C44-type shear K44 the rule is weak. Correlated residuals of the two shears persist
21: across independent target cells and after removal of the clamped pre-stress, which supports a composition-dependent
22: shared residual, but error shared through the binary references remains an unresolved alternative. Primary tests
23: were entered in an append-only ledger, with simulated power, before their new target calculations, and passing
24: results received separate code-and-data audits by a second language model. All targets are machine-learned-potential
25: energies; first-principles validation is pending and is the main limit of this work.
26: 
27: ## 1. Introduction
28: 
29: 1. Liu et al. (2010) developed CALPHAD-style models for elastic coefficients, and Marker et al. (2017) applied this
30:    approach to bcc Ti alloys using relaxed first-principles inputs, each at its own equilibrium volume. Marker
31:    reported average Young's modulus deviations of about 7 GPa with binary parameters and 5 GPa with ternary terms for
32:    13 multicomponent alloys. Huhn et al. (2014) compared alloy moduli with effective-medium estimates based on pure
33:    elements. Linton and Aidhy (2023) trained ML models on binaries, and Mirzaee et al. (2024) a CNN on charge densities
34:    including binary and ternary data. These studies motivate testing how shear transfers from simpler systems.
35: 2. Volume-dependent effective cluster interactions (Asta et al. 1992; Geng et al. 2005), the alloy-volume formalism
36:    for binaries (Ferreira et al. 1987, 1989) and tensorial or strain-dependent cluster expansions (van de
37:    Walle 2008; Behara et al. 2023, which includes shear strain variables) are established. Our search did not
38:    identify the specific fixed-coefficient transfer tested here: clamped multicomponent mixing K' estimated from
39:    equiatomic binary curvatures at the alloy Vegard volume. This is a search-bounded statement, not proof that no
40:    prior work exists.
41: 3. Formally the rule is a pair-truncated tensorial cluster expansion or a zeroth-order Redlich-Kister sum with a
42:    specified evaluation volume. The contribution is this prescription and its tested performance: (i) where the
43:    binary terms are evaluated, (ii) a preregistered test of that choice, (iii) where it stops working, and (iv) how
44:    the C44-type shear differs. In a different field, Hofgard et al. (2026) obtained large gains by changing the
45:    target representation of an ML model while keeping the model. Here the target stays K'_mix; what changes is the
46:    volume at which unchanged binary inputs are read.
47: 
48: ## 2. Methods
49: 
50: **Cells.** Random fcc solid solutions in 108-atom cubic supercells (3x3x3), built by randomly shuffling species over
51: the sites without SQS optimisation. Atoms stay on ideal sites (no ionic or cell relaxation). The volume is fixed at
52: the composition's Vegard volume V0 from the model's pure-element volumes.
53: 
54: **Observable.** E_mix(V, F) = E_alloy - sum x_i E_i per atom, every pure reference at the same volume and the same
55: deformation F. K' from F = diag(e^t, e^-t, 1), K44 from F = I + g e_x e_y, five amplitudes in [-0.01, 0.01],
56: quadratic fit, K' = c2/(2V), K44 = 2 c2/V. The target generators use the cell's actual integer-count fractions for
57: the pure references; the historical exploratory a2 dataset is an exception (Section 3.1). With tensile-positive
58: mixing stress and Green-Lagrange energy coefficients, K44 = C^L_xyxy + s_yy and K' = (C^L_xxxx + C^L_yyyy -
59: 2 C^L_xxyy)/4 + (s_xx + s_yy)/2. The elastic part reduces to (C11 - C12)/2 only in the cubic limit, and subtracting
60: the stress terms does not give relaxed, zero-pressure elastic constants.
61: 
62: **Binary inputs.** All 36 equiatomic pairs, 13 log-volume points ln(V/V_ij) in [-0.4, 0.4], cubic spline per pair.
63: The omat grid uses seeds 0 to 2; the first mpa grid seed 0; the 1200-composition test two three-seed panels (20 to 22,
64: 23 to 25).
65: 
66: **Rule.** K'_mix(alloy) = sum_{i<j} 4 x_i x_j K'_ij(ln V0/V_ij). Baselines: the same sum at ln V0/V_ij = 0 ("pair at
67: V_ij"), and two own-volume Muggianu analogues built from pure-element curvatures (Section 3.4).
68: 
69: **Seeds.** The site permutation of a cell depends only on (seed, n), so cells with equal seed and size share a
70: permutation field. The original h3 and hm_fresh shear tests used target seed 0 and binary seeds 0 to 2, and the first
71: mpa model swap used seed 0 for both; these historical tests shared a permutation field between targets and inputs.
72: After this was found (Section 4) target and binary seeds were separated: the floor tests use target seeds of 100 and
73: above, and the 1200-composition test uses unique target seeds from 10000 with binary panels 20 to 25. Omat seed-split
74: checks kept the K' improvement (gain 0.55 to 0.58, k 1.07 to 1.10) but showed sensitivity for K44.
75: 
76: **Models.** MACE medium-omat-0 (Batatia et al.), calibrated in this project on 14 cubic metals (fcc B, G MAE about
77: 12%, e5ef5a57a3). Second model: medium-mpa-0, with omat geometry (V_ij, V0) so that only the energies change.
78: 
79: **Protocol.** Hypotheses come from two LLM agents (GPT-6-Astra via Codex, Claude Opus), who see the problem, the
80: limits and the training data, never sealed holdouts. Before the new target calculations of a primary test, the

170: ## 5. Discussion and limits
171: 
172: 1. Model only. Every target is a MACE energy. The slope already differs between datasets and models (1.08 to 1.14).
173:    In an eight-cell ordered L1_2 A3B diagnostic (preliminary, subject to convergence checks and audit), Au3Ir has
174:    K44 = -32.4 GPa in PBE and +3.2 GPa in MACE; sign agreement is 8/8 for K' and 5/8 for K44. This does not validate
175:    transfer to random alloys. An L3 test needs at least 15 independent DFT or experimental rows from composition
176:    families absent from training, with the rule and coefficient frozen beforehand. This is future work.
177: 2. Clamped, unrelaxed cells: K'_mix is not the measured C'. On 43 previously examined equiatomic ternaries, relaxed-
178:    binary Muggianu gives C' RMSE 3.08 GPa and a volume-transfer chain 2.53 GPa (gain 0.18, p about 0.08). The chain
179:    also uses the measured relaxed target volume. This exploratory comparison shows neither a significant improvement
180:    nor equivalence at zero pressure.
181: 3. The rule under-predicts at large size mismatch (Section 3.5). A correction has not been tested.
182: 4. fcc late transition and noble metals only. None of the three calibrated MACE models passed the bcc shear
183:    criterion in this project.
184: 5. The rule is a regular-solution or tensorial-CE truncation with a specified volume; we do not claim a new law.

exec
"C:\\Users\\can02\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\pwsh.exe" -Command '
$records = @(Get-ChildItem data/dft_runs/hiso2 -Directory | ForEach-Object {
 $d=$_
 $ins=Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d.FullName '"'pw.in') -Raw
 "'$outs=Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d.FullName '"'pw.out') -Raw
 "'$errs=Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d.FullName '"'pw.err') -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
 "'$energies=[regex]::Matches($outs,'"'"'!'"\\s+total energy\\s*=\\s*([-\\d.]+)')
 "'$acc=[regex]::Matches($outs,'"'estimated scf accuracy\\s*<\\s*([\\d.Ee+-]+)')
 [pscustomobject]@{
 name="'$d.Name
 energyRy=$energies[$energies.Count-1].Groups[1].Value
 energyCount=$energies.Count
 accuracyRy=$acc[$acc.Count-1].Groups[1].Value
 done=$outs.Contains('"'JOB DONE')
 converged="'$outs.Contains('"'convergence has been achieved')
 badConvergence="'$outs.Contains('"'convergence NOT achieved')
 warnings=@("'$outs -split "'"\\r?\\n\" | Where-Object {"'$_ -match '"'(?i)warning|error|negative|not converged|not achieved'})
 err="'$errs
 ecutwfc=[regex]::Match($ins,'"'ecutwfc\\s*=\\s*([\\d.]+)').Groups[1].Value
 ecutrho=[regex]::Match("'$ins,'"'ecutrho\\s*=\\s*([\\d.]+)').Groups[1].Value
 degauss=[regex]::Match("'$ins,'"'degauss\\s*=\\s*([\\d.]+)').Groups[1].Value
 conv_thr=[regex]::Match("'$ins,'"'conv_thr\\s*=\\s*([\\d.eE+-]+)').Groups[1].Value
 kgrid=[regex]::Match("'$ins,'"'K_POINTS automatic\\s*\\r?\\n(["'^'"\\r\\n]+)').Groups[1].Value
 matrix=[regex]::Match("'$ins,'"'CELL_PARAMETERS angstrom\\s*\\r?\\n((?:["'^'"\\r\\n]+\\r?\\n){3})').Groups[1].Value
 positions=[regex]::Match("'$ins,'"'ATOMIC_POSITIONS angstrom\\s*\\r?\\n((?:["'^'"\\r\\n]+\\r?\\n){4})').Groups[1].Value
 cutOutput=[regex]::Match("'$outs,'"'kinetic-energy cutoff\\s*=\\s*([\\d.]+)').Groups[1].Value
 }
})

.orchestra/audits\draft_v3_astra.md:5774:59:{"round": "S3/cobalt", "candidate": "astra_3", "prior": "UNCLEAR", "refs": ["arXiv:2605.28395", "arXiv:2312.17596", "arXiv:2507.18935 (non-magnetic vs spin-polarized DP for Fe-Cr-C: static properties need the spin branch)"], "verdict": "KEEP", "why": "Sound intervention. Switching spin on and off at fixed chemistry, volume and positions isolates the magnetic term. It says correctly that the nonspin arm is not paramagnetic, that the ordered cell is not the random alloy, and that this is not L3. It runs only after astra_2 and after the astra_1 fix. Fix before running: (1) CoCu2Pt in the 4-atom cubic cell is tetragonal (Co on the corner, Pt on one face centre, Cu on two). So C44 differs from C66, and Kp depends on the axes. Fix the Pt axis and use the exact F matrices from k_shear_transfer.py F_of in MACE and in both PBE arms. (2) Report D for the total cell curvature as well as the mixing curvature. Pure Co at 12.6 A^3/atom is expanded about 16% and strongly magnetic, so a mixing D alone can be driven by the reference. (3) Compare MACE on the Co minus Ni difference, so MACE's common shear softening cancels. Four numbers (2 cells x 2 channels) cannot carry an RMSE ratio on their own. (4) The cost is underestimated. Measured hiso2 runs (4-atom L12, kspacing 0.10, 2 MPI, nonmagnetic): 5 min wall unstrained, 18-51 min sheared. With lower symmetry and spin, about 50 SCF is more like 60-150 core-h than 20-50. Prior: implicit magnetism in MLIPs and MACE's partial magnetoelastic failures in Fe-Ni are known. No prior was found for Co in Cu/Pt fcc shear mixing curvatures."}
