810: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:1:# Lessons for derivation agents (Astra, Opus)
811: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:2:
812: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:3:Read before proposing. Each line is a way a candidate died or nearly died for the wrong reason. Updated 2026-10-31.
813: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:4:
814: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:5:1. Ratios of energies blow up where the denominator crosses zero (R3: n_eff = -3 b/a reached -102 for Cu-Ir). Prefer
815: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:6:   predictions linear in measured quantities; if a ratio is essential, say where it is undefined.
816: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:7:2. Compare like with like: clamped with clamped, relaxed with relaxed, random with random. R3 compared a relaxed random
817: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:8:   volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
818: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:9:3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
819: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:10:   that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
820: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:11:4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
821: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:12:   to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
822: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:13:5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
823: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:14:   input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
824: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:15:6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
825: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:16:   (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
826: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:17:7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
827: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:18:   carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
828: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:19:8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
829: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:20:   so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
830: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:21:   (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
831: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:22:9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
832: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:23:   ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
833: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:24:   multicomponent cells can be used.
834: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:25:10. Round R2 (Astra): the arena's permutation count capped the smallest reachable p at 1/501, so after five tests no
835: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:26:    candidate could pass however good it was. Fixed: n_perm grows with m. Also open: generators set V0 from nominal
836: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:27:    fractions while comp_actual differs (~0.5% in volume, ~0.06 meV RMSE effect, not the cause of k ~ 0.8).
837: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:28:11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary
838: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:29:    energies at the alloy volume give k 0.94 [0.90, 0.98] and RMSE 10.3 meV with no parameter (data/binary_vgrid.csv).
839: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:30:12. Swarm S1 audit (Astra): (a) scripts/hiso_l12.py did not use ecut_elements, and harness/dft.py picks the k-grid
840: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:31:    from the strained cell (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18), so 0.1 meV/atom of strain-dependent error moves K by 1.6 to 4.7
841: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:32:    GPa. H-iso results before the fix are not evidence either way; the run is stopped. (b) fix_counts.py treated
842: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:33:    0.3333 as the reference weight of equiatomic ternaries (36+36+36 atoms are exact): +0.3 to +0.7 meV added.
843: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:34:    (c) B_chem and R in *_fixed.csv are stale. (d) K44 ~ K' is not Zener invariance.
844: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:35:13. k at fixed composition (h1/h3 E(V) curves vs exact binary response): 0.976 [0.956, 1.001]. No reduced volume
845: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:36:    response; k ~ 0.8 is the curvature the linear transfer leaves out (94% of the shift).
846: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:37:
847: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:38:14. Shear-curvature volume transfer (prereg 4c29d9754c, result 6e0923b413), 113 unseen h3 alloys, binary curvatures
848: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:39:    at the alloy volume, no parameter. Kp: 4.77 -> 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08 (pass). K44: 3.29 -> 2.62,
849: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:40:    gain 0.20, p 0.023, refit k 0.86 (fail at p < 0.005). Joint claim FAIL. The first design (sigma = pair-sum residual,
850: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:41:    which contains the signal) had power 0.45 and was stopped before any target existed. K44's worst rule errors are
851: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:42:    Co-rich (Co ~0.46 with Pt or Cu), where the rule is worse than no transfer; cause not yet audited (hypothesis,
852: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:43:    design or numerics). Do not re-split the joint claim after the fact: a K44 or Kp claim needs its own fresh test.
853: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:44:
854: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:45:15. K' alone, fresh blind test (prereg 67a358fc59, result d92844787f, L2 entry recorded): 94 hm_fresh alloys, K' 4.22 ->
855: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:46:    1.89 GPa, gain 0.55, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08, 75/94 better. Two independent blind sets now agree for K' (k 1.08 both).
856: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:47:    K44 again weaker (gain 0.12, k 0.69, not gated). Why K44 transfers worse than K' is open: Co-rich outliers, or
857: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:48:    internal (non-affine) relaxation channels that the clamped protocol suppresses differently for the two shears.
858: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:49:
859: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:50:16. Model swap of the K' rule (prereg 851aec6883, result 86767e478d): medium-mpa-0, same geometry, same 94 hm_fresh
860: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:51:    alloys, binaries seed 0 only. K' 4.73 -> 2.28 GPa, gain 0.52, p 2.5e-4, but refit k 1.33 [1.11, 1.51]: the
861: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:52:    pre-registered k-contains-1 condition FAILS. K44 gain 0.16, k 0.77. Reading: that the alloy's K' follows the binaries
862: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:53:    at the alloy volume and cuts the error in half survives a model with a different shear bias; that the coefficient is
863: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:54:    exactly 1 does not (omat 1.08 twice, mpa 1.33). Binary seed noise would pull k down, not up. The two models disagree
864: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:55:    most at |dlnV| > 0.2 (K' corr 0.80 vs 0.96 within 0.1). Cause not yet audited. Do not claim "parameter-free" across
865: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:56:    models; the PBE check decides which k is physical.
866: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:57:
867: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:58:17. K44 transfer fails only with Co (prereg e410c96a32, result d9460850ce). 120 fresh Co-free alloys: K44 pair 4.68 ->
868: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:59:    rule 2.30 GPa, gain 0.51, p 2.5e-4, k 1.23 (PASS). 60 fresh alloys with Co >= 15%: gain 0.11, p 0.08, k 0.70. K'
869: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:60:    passes in both. Open confound: the Co-free set has a larger volume signal (pair error 4.68 vs 3.36), so "Co breaks
870: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:61:    K44" and "K44 needs a large signal" are not yet separated; match the two sets on |rule - pair| before claiming
871: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:62:    a Co mechanism (magnetism is a guess, MACE has no spin).
872: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:63:    Confound check (exploratory, same fresh rows, tertiles of |rule - pair|): at matched signal Co-free gain 0.37 / 0.58
873: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:64:    vs Co 0.08 / 0.22 (mid / large), and Co alloys carry a larger floor at small signal (rule rms 2.61 vs 1.73 GPa).
874: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:65:    The Co effect survives signal matching; not yet a registered claim.
875: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:66:
876: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:67:18. Why K44 looked broken (Opus, swarm S2, blind by file timestamp, confirmed on 60 Co alloys). The part the pair rule
877: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:68:    misses is the same in both shears (corr 0.71, slope ~1). K44's volume signal is half of K''s, so the shared floor
878: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:69:    swamps it; in Co alloys the floor anticorrelates with the signal and drags k to 0.7. Remove the floor (A = K44 - K'
879: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:70:    or e' as covariate) and K44 transfers with k ~1. LESSONS 14-16 failure reason: design, not hypothesis.
880: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:71:
881: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:72:19. Shared SQS seed leak (Opus S2 audit, Astra confirmed). compute.py:56 draws the site permutation from (seed, n)
882: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:73:    only, so every seed-0 cell thresholds one random field: seed-0 targets and seed-0 binaries share configuration
883: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:74:    noise. K' is immune (gain 0.55-0.58, k 1.07-1.10 for every seed split). K44 is not: leak-free gain 0.06-0.14,
884: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:75:    k 0.60-0.77. d9460850ce and the LESSONS 18 Co check used the leak; 9cfc8edaf0 was withdrawn before reading and
885: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:76:    re-registered as c2eff007ad with target seed 100. Rule: targets and inputs never share a seed.
886: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:77:
887: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:78:20. Shared floor, disjoint seeds (c2eff007ad -> b86e0d8a40 PASS, 150 alloys): A = K44 - K' transfers (gain 0.49),
888: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:79:    corr(e44, e') 0.77, joint k 0.91, b 0.94; plain K44 Co-free gain 0.47, Co 0.09. Astra audit: PLAUSIBLE, the
889: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:80:    null could not separate a compositional floor from same-cell noise. A shared-channel claim needs targets for the
890: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:81:    two channels from different cells. Test fd786169e3.
891: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:82:
892: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:83:21. The shared floor is compositional (fd786169e3 PASS, two cells per composition, unique seeds): cross-cell corr
893: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:84:    0.75 vs same-cell 0.79, k 0.92, b 0.95; Astra audit PLAUSIBLE (cell noise ~5% of the shared covariance). Next
894: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:85:    doubt is a known identity: clamped curvatures carry the initial stress, K44 = C44 + s_yy, K' = C' + (s_xx+s_yy)/2.
895: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:86:    A floor claim must survive subtracting it (k_floor_stress.py). Pre-register every step; one audit, one test.
896: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:87:
897: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:88:22. The floor survives the known pre-stress identity (ede47f1d65 PASS; Astra PLAUSIBLE): corrected cross-cell r
898: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:89:    0.67, k 0.99, b 0.79. Mixing pre-stress is 7 GPa rms but pair-additive (rule leaves 0.7 GPa), so it was never the
899: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:90:    floor. Remaining doubt: error shared through the binary references (b drops to 0.4-0.5 with single disjoint
900: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:91:    seeds). Shared-residual claims need two independent binary panels, as in k_mpa_equiv.py.
901: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:92:23. k = 1 is retired (88b9465108 FAIL, cause hypothesis; Astra found no coding error). Under mpa, 1200 alloys: k 1.14
902: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:93:    [1.10, 1.18]; the rule still halves the error (4.81 to 2.21 GPa). k is not a model constant but composition
903: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:94:    dependent: 3 elements 1.00, Cu-free 1.00, Cu 1.24, alloys with max|dlnV| > 0.25 1.41; omat shows the same pattern
904: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:95:    (1.11). The pair transfer under-predicts at large size mismatch. A power sim that treats the target residual as
905: .orchestra/LESSONS.md:96:    cell noise is optimistic: most of it is compositional and does not average out over cells.

951: paper/draft_v2.md:1:# Binary shear curvatures transfer to multicomponent fcc alloys at the alloy's volume: a blind, preregistered test with machine-learned potentials
952: paper/draft_v2.md:2:
953: paper/draft_v2.md:3:Muhammet Can Ergani?
954: paper/draft_v2.md:4:Independent researcher, METU graduate, Ankara, T?rkiye. ORCID 0009-0001-1397-6366
955: paper/draft_v2.md:5:
956: paper/draft_v2.md:6:Draft v2, 2026-11-01. Every number cites a ledger id in `claims/claims.jsonl`. Items marked TODO block submission.
957: paper/draft_v2.md:7:
958: paper/draft_v2.md:8:## Abstract
959: paper/draft_v2.md:9:
960: paper/draft_v2.md:10:Pair-additive extrapolation from binaries (regular solution, Muggianu, Redlich-Kister) is the default way to estimate
961: paper/draft_v2.md:11:properties of high-entropy alloys, and it works poorly for shear elastic constants. We show that for the clamped
962: paper/draft_v2.md:12:mixing part of the tetragonal shear curvature K' of random fcc alloys most of the failure is a volume mismatch: each
963: paper/draft_v2.md:13:50:50 binary curvature has to be read at the multicomponent alloy's Vegard volume, not at the binary's own. With no
964: paper/draft_v2.md:14:fitted parameter, the pair sum then predicts K'_mix of 3 to 5 component alloys of Ag, Au, Co, Cu, Ir, Ni, Pd, Pt, Rh
965: paper/draft_v2.md:15:with half the error of the same sum at the binaries' own volumes (4.2 to 1.9 GPa on 94 blind alloys; 4.8 to 2.2 GPa
966: paper/draft_v2.md:16:on 1200 more under a second model) and a third of the error of standard own-volume Muggianu extrapolation (5.7 to
967: paper/draft_v2.md:17:1.9 GPa). The transfer is not exact: the refit slope is 1.08 under one model and 1.14 [1.10, 1.18] under another, and
968: paper/draft_v2.md:18:it grows with size mismatch, so the rule under-predicts alloys with large volume differences between components. For
969: paper/draft_v2.md:19:the C44-type shear K44 the same rule is weak, and we show that the reason is a composition-level residual shared by
970: paper/draft_v2.md:20:both shears that survives separate cells, separate seeds and removal of the clamped pre-stress. All tests were
971: paper/draft_v2.md:21:registered with measured power in an append-only ledger before their data existed, and every pass was audited by an
972: paper/draft_v2.md:22:agent that did not propose it. All targets come from universal machine-learned potentials (MACE); first-principles
973: paper/draft_v2.md:23:validation is pending and is the main limit of this work.
974: paper/draft_v2.md:24:
975: paper/draft_v2.md:25:## 1. Introduction
976: paper/draft_v2.md:26:
977: paper/draft_v2.md:27:1. HEA screening uses binary data. CALPHAD elastic databases fit Redlich-Kister parameters to the c_ij of relaxed
978: paper/draft_v2.md:28:   SQS, each at its own equilibrium volume (Liu et al. 2010; Marker et al. 2017, bcc Ti-Mo-Nb-Sn-Ta-Zr, Young's
979: paper/draft_v2.md:29:   modulus of 13 alloys within 5 to 7 GPa of experiment). Others average binary moduli (Huhn et al. 2014) or train ML
980: paper/draft_v2.md:30:   models on binaries for Ni-Cu-Au-Pd-Pt (Linton and Aidhy 2023; Mirzaee et al. 2024). Shear transfers worse than
981: paper/draft_v2.md:31:   bulk in all of them and C44 worst; none explains why.
982: paper/draft_v2.md:32:2. Volume-dependent interactions are old: volume-dependent ECIs (Asta et al. 1992; Geng et al. 2005), the alloy-volume
983: paper/draft_v2.md:33:   formalism for binaries (Ferreira, Mbaye, Zunger 1987-89), strain-dependent cluster expansion (Behara et al. 2023).
984: paper/draft_v2.md:34:   They are used for energies and bulk moduli, not for shear, and not as a binary-to-multicomponent transfer rule.
985: paper/draft_v2.md:35:3. Formally the rule is a pair-truncated tensorial cluster expansion (van de Walle 2008) or a zeroth-order
986: paper/draft_v2.md:36:   Redlich-Kister sum. The contribution is not the algebra. It is (i) where the binary terms must be evaluated, (ii) a
987: paper/draft_v2.md:37:   blind preregistered test of that choice, (iii) where it stops working, and (iv) why the C44-type shear behaves
988: paper/draft_v2.md:38:   differently. A similar lesson holds in ML for diffraction, where changing the prediction target, not the model,
989: paper/draft_v2.md:39:   cut errors several fold (Hofgard et al., Acta Cryst. A, 2026, TODO exact reference): here the binary data are
990: paper/draft_v2.md:40:   unchanged and only the volume at which they are read changes.
991: paper/draft_v2.md:41:
992: paper/draft_v2.md:42:## 2. Methods
993: paper/draft_v2.md:43:
994: paper/draft_v2.md:44:**Cells.** Random fcc solid solutions, 108-atom cubic supercells (3x3x3), atoms on ideal sites (no ionic or cell
995: paper/draft_v2.md:45:relaxation), volume fixed at the composition's Vegard volume V0 from the model's pure-element volumes.
996: paper/draft_v2.md:46:
997: paper/draft_v2.md:47:**Observable.** E_mix(V, F) = E_alloy - sum x_i E_i, every pure reference at the same volume and the same deformation
998: paper/draft_v2.md:48:F. K' from F = diag(e^t, e^-t, 1), K44 from F = I + g e_x e_y, five amplitudes in [-0.01, 0.01], quadratic fit,
999: paper/draft_v2.md:49:K' = c2/(2V), K44 = 2 c2/V. References use the cell's actual (integer-count) fractions. At V0 a clamped cell is not
1000: paper/draft_v2.md:50:stress free, so K44 = C44 + s_yy and K' = C' + (s_xx + s_yy)/2; Section 3.6 removes this term explicitly.
1001: paper/draft_v2.md:51:
1002: paper/draft_v2.md:52:**Binary inputs.** All 36 pairs at 50:50, three SQS seeds per panel, 13 log-volume points ln(V/V_ij) in [-0.4, 0.4],
1003: paper/draft_v2.md:53:cubic spline per pair.
1004: paper/draft_v2.md:54:
1005: paper/draft_v2.md:55:**Rule.** K'_mix(alloy) = sum_{i<j} 4 x_i x_j K'_ij(ln V0/V_ij). Baselines: the same sum at ln V0/V_ij = 0, and
1006: paper/draft_v2.md:56:own-volume Muggianu (pure-element K'(V) at their own volumes, converted to the clamped reference).
1007: paper/draft_v2.md:57:
1008: paper/draft_v2.md:58:**Seeds.** The site permutation of a cell depends only on (seed, n). Target cells and input cells (binaries,
1009: paper/draft_v2.md:59:references) therefore never share a seed: targets use seeds of 100 and above, binaries 0 to 25. An earlier test that
1010: paper/draft_v2.md:60:broke this rule was withdrawn before its targets were read (Section 4).
1011: paper/draft_v2.md:61:
1012: paper/draft_v2.md:62:**Models.** MACE medium-omat-0, calibrated on 14 cubic metals (fcc B, G MAE about 12%, e5ef5a57a3). Second model:
1013: paper/draft_v2.md:63:medium-mpa-0, with omat geometry (V_ij, V0) so that only the energies change.
1014: paper/draft_v2.md:64:
1015: paper/draft_v2.md:65:**Protocol.** Hypotheses come from two LLM agents (GPT-6-Astra via Codex, Claude Opus) who see the problem, the
1016: paper/draft_v2.md:66:limits and the data, never sealed holdouts. Before any test datum exists the harness owner writes the claim, the
1017: paper/draft_v2.md:67:pass criterion and a simulated power (>= 0.8) and false-pass rate (<= 0.05) to the ledger. A failed test is closed
1018: paper/draft_v2.md:68:with a cause (hypothesis, design, numerics) after an independent audit; only "hypothesis" retires a candidate. Every
1019: paper/draft_v2.md:69:pass is audited by the model that did not propose it, which recomputes the key numbers from the raw files.
1020: paper/draft_v2.md:70:
1021: paper/draft_v2.md:71:**Statistics.** Gain = 1 - RMSE(rule)/RMSE(baseline); paired sign-flip test on squared-error differences; refit slope
1022: paper/draft_v2.md:72:k from (y - base) = k (rule - base). With two independent binary panels A and B the slope is estimated cross-panel,
1023: paper/draft_v2.md:73:k = sum[T_A (y - p_B) + T_B (y - p_A)] / (2 sum T_A T_B), so binary noise does not bias it; CIs bootstrap over
1024: paper/draft_v2.md:74:compositions and over seeds within each panel.
1025: paper/draft_v2.md:75:
1026: paper/draft_v2.md:76:## 3. Results
1027: paper/draft_v2.md:77:
1028: paper/draft_v2.md:78:**3.1 Exploration.** On 62 ternary to quinary alloys used for exploration (a2): K' pair sum 5.67 to rule 1.80 GPa,
1029: paper/draft_v2.md:79:k 1.05.
1030: paper/draft_v2.md:80:
1031: paper/draft_v2.md:81:**3.2 Blind test 1 (h3, 113 alloys, prereg 4c29d9754c).** K': 4.77 to 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, k 1.08. The
1032: paper/draft_v2.md:82:registered claim was joint (K44 and K'); it failed on K44 (p 0.023, 6e0923b413), so K' got a fresh test rather than a
1033: paper/draft_v2.md:83:post-hoc split.
1034: paper/draft_v2.md:84:
1035: paper/draft_v2.md:85:**3.3 Blind test 2 (hm_fresh, 94 alloys never computed, prereg 67a358fc59).** K': 4.22 to 1.89 GPa, gain 0.55,
1036: paper/draft_v2.md:86:p 2.5e-4, k 1.08, rule better in 75 of 94 alloys (d92844787f, L2 697c2d6d75).
1037: paper/draft_v2.md:87:
1038: paper/draft_v2.md:88:**3.4 Against the standard method.** Own-volume Muggianu, the clamped analogue of the CALPHAD c_ij practice (Marker
1039: paper/draft_v2.md:89:et al. 2017: every input at its own volume, no volume dependence in the interaction parameters): 5.45 / 5.71 / 5.41
1040: paper/draft_v2.md:90:GPa on h3 / hm_fresh / a2; rule 2.03 / 1.89 / 1.94 (p 5e-5). For the mixing energy the same comparison shows no gain
1041: paper/draft_v2.md:91:(13.3 vs 11.5 meV): there the volume term is mostly the reference strain energy, which the standard reference already
1042: paper/draft_v2.md:92:removes. K' is different because the binary curvatures themselves change steeply with volume (median dlnK'/dlnV =
1043: paper/draft_v2.md:93:-3.2 for pairs with |K'| > 10 GPa).
1044: paper/draft_v2.md:94:
1045: paper/draft_v2.md:95:**3.5 Second model, and the size of k (prereg 88b9465108, result 43370bbb27, verdict 736bcac471).** Under
1046: paper/draft_v2.md:96:medium-mpa-0, on 1200 new compositions (Co yes/no x 3/4/5 elements, 200 each, two cells each) with two independent
1047: paper/draft_v2.md:97:binary panels, the rule cuts the RMSE from 4.81 to 2.21 GPa (gain 0.54) and wins in 934 of 1200 alloys. The
1048: paper/draft_v2.md:98:preregistered equivalence claim k in [0.90, 1.10] failed: k = 1.138, 90% CI [1.098, 1.182]. The audit found no coding
1049: paper/draft_v2.md:99:error; all 3+3 panel splits give 1.138 to 1.139. The slope is not a constant. Exploratory splits (not preregistered):
1050: paper/draft_v2.md:100:3-component 1.00 [0.91, 1.09], 4-component 1.25, 5-component 1.17; Cu-free 1.00 [0.94, 1.07], Cu-containing 1.24;
1051: paper/draft_v2.md:101:alloys whose largest pair |ln V0/V_ij| is at most 0.15 give 1.07, above 0.25 give 1.41. Co content does not matter
1052: paper/draft_v2.md:102:(1.137 vs 1.139). Under omat, cells of Section 3.6 give k 1.11 [1.02, 1.20] with the same stratification. We read
1053: paper/draft_v2.md:103:this as an under-prediction at large size mismatch: the pair transfer captures most of the volume effect but not all
1054: paper/draft_v2.md:104:of it. A refit k adds only 3% over k = 1, so the parameter-free rule remains the practical form.
1055: paper/draft_v2.md:105:
1056: paper/draft_v2.md:106:**3.6 The C44-type shear.** The same rule is weak for K44 (leak-free gain 0.06 to 0.14). Three preregistered tests
1057: paper/draft_v2.md:107:show why: K44 and K' share a residual that belongs to the composition, not to the cell or the noise.
1058: paper/draft_v2.md:108:- Shared floor, disjoint seeds (150 new alloys, half with Co >= 15%; prereg c2eff007ad, result b86e0d8a40): the
1059: paper/draft_v2.md:109:  difference A = K44 - K' follows the rule (gain 0.49), the residuals of the two shears correlate (r 0.77), and a joint
1060: paper/draft_v2.md:110:  fit gives k 0.91 and floor slope b 0.94. Plain K44 gains 0.47 in Co-free alloys and 0.09 in Co alloys.
1061: paper/draft_v2.md:111:- Two cells per composition with seeds unique to each cell (prereg fd786169e3): the K44 residual of one cell
1062: paper/draft_v2.md:112:  correlates with the K' residual of the other (r 0.75; same cell 0.79), k 0.92, b 0.95.
1063: paper/draft_v2.md:113:- After subtracting the clamped mixing pre-stress from targets and binaries alike (prereg ede47f1d65): cross-cell
1064: paper/draft_v2.md:114:  r 0.67, k 0.99, b 0.79. The pre-stress is large (7 GPa rms) but pair-additive (the rule leaves 0.7 GPa of it), so
1065: paper/draft_v2.md:115:  it was never the floor.
1066: paper/draft_v2.md:116:So K44 = rule44 + b (K' - rule') with b near 1: the C44-type shear fails because it carries a composition floor that
1067: paper/draft_v2.md:117:K' also carries, while its own volume signal is about half as large. Open doubt (audit of ede47f1d65): b drops to 0.4
1068: paper/draft_v2.md:118:to 0.5 when single disjoint binary seeds are used, so part of the floor may be error shared through the binary
1069: paper/draft_v2.md:119:references. TODO: two independent binary panels for K44, K' and stress.
1070: paper/draft_v2.md:120:
1071: paper/draft_v2.md:121:## 4. What the audits caught
1072: paper/draft_v2.md:122:
1073: paper/draft_v2.md:123:The loop's most useful outputs were errors, each found by the agent that did not write the code and confirmed by the
1074: paper/draft_v2.md:124:other.
1075: paper/draft_v2.md:125:
1076: paper/draft_v2.md:126:| Error | Found by | Size | What it changed |
1077: paper/draft_v2.md:127:|---|---|---|---|
1078: paper/draft_v2.md:128:| Integer-count reference mismatch | audit | up to 57 meV/atom | all mixing quantities recomputed |
1079: paper/draft_v2.md:129:| PBE cutoff mismatch between alloy and pure references | audit | (TODO size) | rule added: references use the alloy cutoff |
1080: paper/draft_v2.md:130:| Holdout used for model selection | audit, d26bd71285 | (TODO) | holdout sealed, targets shuffled |
1081: paper/draft_v2.md:131:| Shared SQS permutation between targets and binaries (seed 0) | S2 audit, Opus, confirmed by Astra | K44 Co-free gain inflated | test withdrawn (42c0fd3ee0) before reading, seeds separated |
1082: paper/draft_v2.md:132:| Weak baseline made a known energy rule look new | audit | 13.3 vs 11.5 meV | energy rule demoted |
1083: paper/draft_v2.md:133:| Power simulation treated a compositional residual as cell noise | audit of 88b9465108 | power 1.0 reported | lesson: simulate residuals at composition level |
1084: paper/draft_v2.md:134:| PBE runs with nspin 1 still magnetize Co and Ni | Astra, S3 | not used in any result | Co/Ni PBE blocked until fixed |
1085: paper/draft_v2.md:135:
1086: paper/draft_v2.md:136:## 5. Discussion and limits
1087: paper/draft_v2.md:137:
1088: paper/draft_v2.md:138:1. Model only. Every target is a MACE energy. The slope already differs between two MACE models (1.08, 1.14), and in
1089: paper/draft_v2.md:139:   a small set of ordered L1_2 A3B cells (preliminary, unaudited) MACE gets the sign of K44 wrong where PBE gives
1090: paper/draft_v2.md:140:   -32 GPa (Au3Ir). K' agreed better. Only PBE on random alloys decides how much of the rule is physical. TODO: PBE
1091: paper/draft_v2.md:141:   SQS check on 10 to 15 alloys.
1092: paper/draft_v2.md:142:2. Clamped, unrelaxed cells: K'_mix is not the measured C'. On 43 seen equiatomic ternaries with fully relaxed MACE
1093: paper/draft_v2.md:143:   constants, own-volume Muggianu of relaxed binaries already reaches 3.1 GPa for C' and a chain built on the volume
1094: paper/draft_v2.md:144:   rule 2.5 GPa (gain 0.18, p 0.08, exploratory). At zero pressure the advantage is small and not yet significant.
1095: paper/draft_v2.md:145:3. The rule under-predicts at large size mismatch (Section 3.5). A correction for this has not been tested.
1096: paper/draft_v2.md:146:4. fcc late transition and noble metals only; bcc shear fails calibration for every model available.
1097: paper/draft_v2.md:147:5. The rule is a regular-solution / tensorial-CE truncation with a specified volume; we do not claim a new law.
1098: paper/draft_v2.md:148:
1099: paper/draft_v2.md:149:## Data and code

1544: 1:# Binary shear curvatures transfer to multicomponent fcc alloys at the alloy's volume: a blind, preregistered test with machine-learned potentials
1545: 2:
1546: 3:Muhammet Can Ergani?
1547: 4:Independent researcher, METU graduate, Ankara, T?rkiye. ORCID 0009-0001-1397-6366
1548: 5:
1549: 6:Draft v2, 2026-11-01. Every number cites a ledger id in `claims/claims.jsonl`. Items marked TODO block submission.
1550: 7:
1551: 8:## Abstract
1552: 9:
1553: 10:Pair-additive extrapolation from binaries (regular solution, Muggianu, Redlich-Kister) is the default way to estimate
1554: 11:properties of high-entropy alloys, and it works poorly for shear elastic constants. We show that for the clamped
1555: 12:mixing part of the tetragonal shear curvature K' of random fcc alloys most of the failure is a volume mismatch: each
1556: 13:50:50 binary curvature has to be read at the multicomponent alloy's Vegard volume, not at the binary's own. With no
1557: 14:fitted parameter, the pair sum then predicts K'_mix of 3 to 5 component alloys of Ag, Au, Co, Cu, Ir, Ni, Pd, Pt, Rh
1558: 15:with half the error of the same sum at the binaries' own volumes (4.2 to 1.9 GPa on 94 blind alloys; 4.8 to 2.2 GPa
1559: 16:on 1200 more under a second model) and a third of the error of standard own-volume Muggianu extrapolation (5.7 to
1560: 17:1.9 GPa). The transfer is not exact: the refit slope is 1.08 under one model and 1.14 [1.10, 1.18] under another, and
1561: 18:it grows with size mismatch, so the rule under-predicts alloys with large volume differences between components. For
1562: 19:the C44-type shear K44 the same rule is weak, and we show that the reason is a composition-level residual shared by
1563: 20:both shears that survives separate cells, separate seeds and removal of the clamped pre-stress. All tests were
1564: 21:registered with measured power in an append-only ledger before their data existed, and every pass was audited by an
1565: 22:agent that did not propose it. All targets come from universal machine-learned potentials (MACE); first-principles
1566: 23:validation is pending and is the main limit of this work.
1567: 24:
1568: 25:## 1. Introduction
1569: 26:
1570: 27:1. HEA screening uses binary data. CALPHAD elastic databases fit Redlich-Kister parameters to the c_ij of relaxed
1571: 28:   SQS, each at its own equilibrium volume (Liu et al. 2010; Marker et al. 2017, bcc Ti-Mo-Nb-Sn-Ta-Zr, Young's
1572: 29:   modulus of 13 alloys within 5 to 7 GPa of experiment). Others average binary moduli (Huhn et al. 2014) or train ML
1573: 30:   models on binaries for Ni-Cu-Au-Pd-Pt (Linton and Aidhy 2023; Mirzaee et al. 2024). Shear transfers worse than
1574: 31:   bulk in all of them and C44 worst; none explains why.
1575: 32:2. Volume-dependent interactions are old: volume-dependent ECIs (Asta et al. 1992; Geng et al. 2005), the alloy-volume
1576: 33:   formalism for binaries (Ferreira, Mbaye, Zunger 1987-89), strain-dependent cluster expansion (Behara et al. 2023).
1577: 34:   They are used for energies and bulk moduli, not for shear, and not as a binary-to-multicomponent transfer rule.
1578: 35:3. Formally the rule is a pair-truncated tensorial cluster expansion (van de Walle 2008) or a zeroth-order
1579: 36:   Redlich-Kister sum. The contribution is not the algebra. It is (i) where the binary terms must be evaluated, (ii) a
1580: 37:   blind preregistered test of that choice, (iii) where it stops working, and (iv) why the C44-type shear behaves
1581: 38:   differently. A similar lesson holds in ML for diffraction, where changing the prediction target, not the model,
1582: 39:   cut errors several fold (Hofgard et al., Acta Cryst. A, 2026, TODO exact reference): here the binary data are
1583: 40:   unchanged and only the volume at which they are read changes.
1584: 41:
1585: 42:## 2. Methods
1586: 43:
1587: 44:**Cells.** Random fcc solid solutions, 108-atom cubic supercells (3x3x3), atoms on ideal sites (no ionic or cell
1588: 45:relaxation), volume fixed at the composition's Vegard volume V0 from the model's pure-element volumes.
1589: 46:
1590: 47:**Observable.** E_mix(V, F) = E_alloy - sum x_i E_i, every pure reference at the same volume and the same deformation
1591: 48:F. K' from F = diag(e^t, e^-t, 1), K44 from F = I + g e_x e_y, five amplitudes in [-0.01, 0.01], quadratic fit,
1592: 49:K' = c2/(2V), K44 = 2 c2/V. References use the cell's actual (integer-count) fractions. At V0 a clamped cell is not
1593: 50:stress free, so K44 = C44 + s_yy and K' = C' + (s_xx + s_yy)/2; Section 3.6 removes this term explicitly.
1594: 51:
1595: 52:**Binary inputs.** All 36 pairs at 50:50, three SQS seeds per panel, 13 log-volume points ln(V/V_ij) in [-0.4, 0.4],
1596: 53:cubic spline per pair.
1597: 54:
1598: 55:**Rule.** K'_mix(alloy) = sum_{i<j} 4 x_i x_j K'_ij(ln V0/V_ij). Baselines: the same sum at ln V0/V_ij = 0, and
1599: 56:own-volume Muggianu (pure-element K'(V) at their own volumes, converted to the clamped reference).
1600: 57:
1601: 58:**Seeds.** The site permutation of a cell depends only on (seed, n). Target cells and input cells (binaries,
1602: 59:references) therefore never share a seed: targets use seeds of 100 and above, binaries 0 to 25. An earlier test that
1603: 60:broke this rule was withdrawn before its targets were read (Section 4).
1604: 61:
1605: 62:**Models.** MACE medium-omat-0, calibrated on 14 cubic metals (fcc B, G MAE about 12%, e5ef5a57a3). Second model:
1606: 63:medium-mpa-0, with omat geometry (V_ij, V0) so that only the energies change.
1607: 64:
1608: 65:**Protocol.** Hypotheses come from two LLM agents (GPT-6-Astra via Codex, Claude Opus) who see the problem, the
1609: 66:limits and the data, never sealed holdouts. Before any test datum exists the harness owner writes the claim, the
1610: 67:pass criterion and a simulated power (>= 0.8) and false-pass rate (<= 0.05) to the ledger. A failed test is closed
1611: 68:with a cause (hypothesis, design, numerics) after an independent audit; only "hypothesis" retires a candidate. Every
1612: 69:pass is audited by the model that did not propose it, which recomputes the key numbers from the raw files.
1613: 70:
1614: 71:**Statistics.** Gain = 1 - RMSE(rule)/RMSE(baseline); paired sign-flip test on squared-error differences; refit slope
1615: 72:k from (y - base) = k (rule - base). With two independent binary panels A and B the slope is estimated cross-panel,
1616: 73:k = sum[T_A (y - p_B) + T_B (y - p_A)] / (2 sum T_A T_B), so binary noise does not bias it; CIs bootstrap over
1617: 74:compositions and over seeds within each panel.
1618: 75:
1619: 76:## 3. Results
1620: 77:
1621: 78:**3.1 Exploration.** On 62 ternary to quinary alloys used for exploration (a2): K' pair sum 5.67 to rule 1.80 GPa,
1622: 79:k 1.05.
1623: 80:
1624: 81:**3.2 Blind test 1 (h3, 113 alloys, prereg 4c29d9754c).** K': 4.77 to 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, k 1.08. The
1625: 82:registered claim was joint (K44 and K'); it failed on K44 (p 0.023, 6e0923b413), so K' got a fresh test rather than a
1626: 83:post-hoc split.
1627: 84:
1628: 85:**3.3 Blind test 2 (hm_fresh, 94 alloys never computed, prereg 67a358fc59).** K': 4.22 to 1.89 GPa, gain 0.55,
1629: 86:p 2.5e-4, k 1.08, rule better in 75 of 94 alloys (d92844787f, L2 697c2d6d75).
1630: 87:
1631: 88:**3.4 Against the standard method.** Own-volume Muggianu, the clamped analogue of the CALPHAD c_ij practice (Marker
1632: 89:et al. 2017: every input at its own volume, no volume dependence in the interaction parameters): 5.45 / 5.71 / 5.41
1633: 90:GPa on h3 / hm_fresh / a2; rule 2.03 / 1.89 / 1.94 (p 5e-5). For the mixing energy the same comparison shows no gain
1634: 91:(13.3 vs 11.5 meV): there the volume term is mostly the reference strain energy, which the standard reference already
1635: 92:removes. K' is different because the binary curvatures themselves change steeply with volume (median dlnK'/dlnV =
1636: 93:-3.2 for pairs with |K'| > 10 GPa).
1637: 94:
1638: 95:**3.5 Second model, and the size of k (prereg 88b9465108, result 43370bbb27, verdict 736bcac471).** Under
1639: 96:medium-mpa-0, on 1200 new compositions (Co yes/no x 3/4/5 elements, 200 each, two cells each) with two independent
1640: 97:binary panels, the rule cuts the RMSE from 4.81 to 2.21 GPa (gain 0.54) and wins in 934 of 1200 alloys. The
1641: 98:preregistered equivalence claim k in [0.90, 1.10] failed: k = 1.138, 90% CI [1.098, 1.182]. The audit found no coding
1642: 99:error; all 3+3 panel splits give 1.138 to 1.139. The slope is not a constant. Exploratory splits (not preregistered):
1643: 100:3-component 1.00 [0.91, 1.09], 4-component 1.25, 5-component 1.17; Cu-free 1.00 [0.94, 1.07], Cu-containing 1.24;
1644: 101:alloys whose largest pair |ln V0/V_ij| is at most 0.15 give 1.07, above 0.25 give 1.41. Co content does not matter
1645: 102:(1.137 vs 1.139). Under omat, cells of Section 3.6 give k 1.11 [1.02, 1.20] with the same stratification. We read
1646: 103:this as an under-prediction at large size mismatch: the pair transfer captures most of the volume effect but not all
1647: 104:of it. A refit k adds only 3% over k = 1, so the parameter-free rule remains the practical form.
1648: 105:
1649: 106:**3.6 The C44-type shear.** The same rule is weak for K44 (leak-free gain 0.06 to 0.14). Three preregistered tests
1650: 107:show why: K44 and K' share a residual that belongs to the composition, not to the cell or the noise.
1651: 108:- Shared floor, disjoint seeds (150 new alloys, half with Co >= 15%; prereg c2eff007ad, result b86e0d8a40): the
1652: 109:  difference A = K44 - K' follows the rule (gain 0.49), the residuals of the two shears correlate (r 0.77), and a joint
1653: 110:  fit gives k 0.91 and floor slope b 0.94. Plain K44 gains 0.47 in Co-free alloys and 0.09 in Co alloys.
1654: 111:- Two cells per composition with seeds unique to each cell (prereg fd786169e3): the K44 residual of one cell
1655: 112:  correlates with the K' residual of the other (r 0.75; same cell 0.79), k 0.92, b 0.95.
1656: 113:- After subtracting the clamped mixing pre-stress from targets and binaries alike (prereg ede47f1d65): cross-cell
1657: 114:  r 0.67, k 0.99, b 0.79. The pre-stress is large (7 GPa rms) but pair-additive (the rule leaves 0.7 GPa of it), so
1658: 115:  it was never the floor.
1659: 116:So K44 = rule44 + b (K' - rule') with b near 1: the C44-type shear fails because it carries a composition floor that
1660: 117:K' also carries, while its own volume signal is about half as large. Open doubt (audit of ede47f1d65): b drops to 0.4
1661: 118:to 0.5 when single disjoint binary seeds are used, so part of the floor may be error shared through the binary
1662: 119:references. TODO: two independent binary panels for K44, K' and stress.
1663: 120:
1664: 121:## 4. What the audits caught
1665: 122:
1666: 123:The loop's most useful outputs were errors, each found by the agent that did not write the code and confirmed by the
1667: 124:other.
1668: 125:
1669: 126:| Error | Found by | Size | What it changed |
1670: 127:|---|---|---|---|
1671: 128:| Integer-count reference mismatch | audit | up to 57 meV/atom | all mixing quantities recomputed |

1679: 136:## 5. Discussion and limits
1680: 137:
1681: 138:1. Model only. Every target is a MACE energy. The slope already differs between two MACE models (1.08, 1.14), and in
1682: 139:   a small set of ordered L1_2 A3B cells (preliminary, unaudited) MACE gets the sign of K44 wrong where PBE gives
1683: 140:   -32 GPa (Au3Ir). K' agreed better. Only PBE on random alloys decides how much of the rule is physical. TODO: PBE
1684: 141:   SQS check on 10 to 15 alloys.
1685: 142:2. Clamped, unrelaxed cells: K'_mix is not the measured C'. On 43 seen equiatomic ternaries with fully relaxed MACE
1686: 143:   constants, own-volume Muggianu of relaxed binaries already reaches 3.1 GPa for C' and a chain built on the volume
1687: 144:   rule 2.5 GPa (gain 0.18, p 0.08, exploratory). At zero pressure the advantage is small and not yet significant.
1688: 145:3. The rule under-predicts at large size mismatch (Section 3.5). A correction for this has not been tested.
1689: 146:4. fcc late transition and noble metals only; bcc shear fails calibration for every model available.
1690: 147:5. The rule is a regular-solution / tensorial-CE truncation with a specified volume; we do not claim a new law.

1720: # ARS-Codex
1721: 
1722: This is a Codex adapter for the ARS suite. The vendored ARS content lives under
1723: `ars/`; keep it as source material and route through this file first.
1724: 
1725: ## Versioning
1726: 
1727: This Codex package is version `0.1.28`. The repo-root `VERSION`, this
1728: `SKILL.md` metadata version, and `manifest.json` `adapter_version` must match.
1729: Vendored ARS suite versions are tracked separately by source repository commit
1730: in `manifest.json`.
1731: 
1732: ## First Rule
1733: 
1734: Do not load the whole suite by default. Select one workflow, read that workflow's
1735: `WORKFLOW.md`, then load only the agent, reference, template, or shared files needed
1736: for the user's current stage.
1737: 
1738: The internal workflow entry files are named `WORKFLOW.md`, not `SKILL.md`, so
1739: Codex registers only this root router skill instead of exposing every vendored
1740: upstream workflow as a separate skill.
1741: 
1742: ## Workflow Router
1743: 
1744: Choose the workflow by intent:
1745: 
1746: | User intent | Read first |
1747: |---|---|
1748: | Deep research, literature review, systematic review, meta-analysis, fact-checking, research question refinement | `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` |
1749: | Academic paper writing, paper outline, abstract, revision, citation formatting, AI disclosure, LaTeX/DOCX/PDF formatting guidance | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` |
1750: | Paper review, peer review simulation, editorial decision, reviewer calibration, re-review after revision | `ars/academic-paper-reviewer/WORKFLOW.md` |
1751: | End-to-end research-to-paper pipeline, integrity gate, staged review/revision/finalization workflow | `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` |
1752: | Experiment planning, code experiment execution plan, human study protocol, statistical interpretation, reproducibility validation | `ars/experiment-agent/WORKFLOW.md` |
1753: 
1754: If the request spans multiple workflows, start with `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md`
1755: unless the user clearly asked for a single phase.
1756: 
1757: ### Paper Topic Scoping Override
1758: 
1759: Apply this override before the general paper/pipeline routing rule and before the Claude-Style Alias Router below.
1760: The override applies regardless of whether the user invokes ARS via natural
1761: language or via an `ars-*` alias.
1762: 
1763: If the user says they want to write a paper, thesis, proposal, article, journal
1764: article, or manuscript, but they only provide a broad topic, tentative title,
1765: research interest, or "??/??/??" and do **not** provide a clear,
1766: answerable research question, route to `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` in
1767: `socratic` mode first. This matches the upstream ARS experience where vague
1768: paper-topic requests start with SCR/Socratic narrowing instead of immediate
1769: outline or drafting.
1770: 
1771: Treat these as Socratic triggers even when the wording contains paper-writing
1772: intent:
1773: 
1774: - "I want to write a paper on ..."
1775: - "I have a paper topic/title ..."
1776: - "???????,???..."
1777: - "????????/??,???????"
1778: - "???????/??????"
1779: - "??? ?? ??? ?? ??? ?? ???? ??"
1780: - "?? ??/?? ??? ??? ??? ???? ????"
1781: 
1782: First response in this path:
1783: 
1784: 1. State that the request is being routed to `deep-research` `socratic` mode
1785:    because the research question is not yet precise.
1786: 2. Ask 3-5 Socratic narrowing questions using `socratic_mentor_agent` and
1787:    `research_question_agent` guidance.
1788: 3. Do not produce an outline, draft, literature review, or full pipeline
1789:    dashboard until the user has converged on at least one candidate RQ.
1790: 
1791: Route directly to `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` only when the user already
1792: has a clear RQ, approved study frame, data/results, literature matrix, draft,
1793: or explicitly asks to skip scoping and proceed to outline/drafting. Route to
1794: `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` only when the user explicitly asks for the
1795: full research-to-paper pipeline or says to continue after Socratic scoping.
1796:

1863: 
1864: The upstream prompt contracts, Python resolver clients, and v3.21
1865: claim-standing adapters are distinct execution paths. Apply this table before
1866: following any vendored instruction that says a lookup happens automatically:
1867: 
1868: | Path | Default ARS-Codex behavior | Dedicated client trigger |
1869: |---|---|---|
1870: | Ordinary topic or candidate discovery | Use Codex browsing and authoritative web sources. | Never launches the Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Crossref, or arXiv Python resolver clients. |
1871: | Agent-side ingest, deduplication, and source verification | In the default inline route, translate prompt-level `WebSearch` or index lookups into Codex browsing or official metadata pages. | Upstream prompt wording such as "automatic S2 lookup" does not itself launch a Python client in Codex. |
1872: | Script-backed citation-existence gate | Do not infer this from an `ars-full` request alone. Stage 2.5 and 4.5 remain mandatory integrity checkpoints, but default Codex routing performs their source work through browsing unless the user also requests programmatic verification. | An explicit request to run `verify_passport.py`, `verification_gate`, or equivalent programmatic reference verification. Once invoked, cache misses may call Crossref, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar for non-manual references; arXiv runs only when `arxiv_id` is present. Manual references skip all four. |
1873: | Claim-standing discovery | Offer only after an eligible Claim Registry row at Stage 2.5 or 4.5. It is advisory and separate from citation verification. | A separate user request plus affirmative, plan-bound consent. It uses the v3.21 keyword-discovery adapters, not the four single-reference resolver clients; absent, cancelled, invalidated, or stale consent means no call. |
1874: | Contamination backfill or migration | No automatic migration. | Only the explicitly selected migration CLI and its documented indexes. |

1880: ### ARS v3.21.1 Contract-Honesty Boundaries
1881: 
1882: - Phase E evidence rows are deterministic, source-bound checkpoint artifacts.
1883:   They preserve the existing citation verdict and gate, do not mark a source as
1884:   human-read, and must replay against explicit session-held source bytes.
1885: - Revision roadmaps remain non-ranking proposals. Only an explicit author
1886:   adjudication may authorize exact choices or integrity-correction targets;
1887:   never infer, fabricate, or auto-apply author decisions. Optional cross-run
1888:   adjudication-activity capture is local, best-effort, and advisory only.
1889: - Review-target context must be author-confirmed, and criteria are carried by
1890:   resolved pointers across formative, internal, and external review. Do not
1891:   infer a missing venue/track, invent evidence, or let binding conformance alter
1892:   integrity verdicts, editorial arithmetic, checkpoints, or author triage.
1893: - Human-subjects authority resolution keeps review-ethics and data-protection
1894:   axes separate and fails closed when scope, currency, or applicability is
1895:   unresolved. Outputs remain institution-owned navigation aids, never legal
1896:   advice, an IRB/REC determination, an authorization, or a fabricated timeline.

2013: 28:{"round": "S1/open", "candidate": "astra_1", "prior": "KNOWN", "refs": ["https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08076 (Tian, Eriksson, Vitos 2020, pressure effect on order-disorder in L1_0 FeNi, doi:10.1038/s41598-020-71551-4)", "https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0622 (Geng, Chen, Sluiter, PRB 70 094203, fcc Ni-Al phase stability under pressure)", "https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0646 (Geng, Sluiter, Chen, PRB 72 014204, order-disorder effects on EOS in fcc Ni-Al)", "volume-dependent ECIs, Alling/Ruban 2011, already logged in ledger 0dffc5bf40"], "verdict": "DROP", "why": "The arithmetic checks out. data/r3b_l12.csv:30 gives E_ord +1.49 meV and S_ord +231.6 meV. Recomputing with the h1 grid points emix_2 and emix_4 at lnV -0.030 and +0.030 gives about +1.40 and +214, and -S_ord/V0 = -2.91 GPa. The Co3Ir control (row 21: -41.5 meV, slope 259) also matches. But this is not a regularity. It is a linear extrapolation of two numbers for one compound: any cell with E_ord near 0 and a nonzero ordering slope crosses zero at t = -E_ord/S_ord. Ni3Ir and Co3Ir have the same slope sign and similar size, so the only real contrast is E_ord(V0). Volume-dependent cluster expansion and the pressure-dependent ordering literature already give this, and the candidate admits CE can represent it. The 1.4 meV signal is below noise. It comes from a single seed=0 108-atom random cell. For equiatomic Ni-Ir, seeds 0/1/2 give E_mix -190.9/-192.4/-178.9 meV (13.5 meV spread) and slopes spread about 85 meV per unit lnV (data/h1_ev_rows_fixed.csv, data/binary_seeds.csv), so the crossing at t = -0.0065 is not resolved. MACE's MAE on ordered-cell energies vs PBE is 7.0 meV (ledger 7e0ff785d1), so even the sign at V0 is outside L1 accuracy. Ni magnetism is not separated out. Clamped equal-volume energies are also the wrong thermodynamic comparison under pressure. Letting each phase relax to its own volume already lowers E_ord by about S_ord^2/(2BV), roughly 1.3 meV at B about 230 GPa. So at P=0 the two phases are degenerate within that correction, and the real test would be dH(P), not dE at fixed t. Nothing here tests or corrects a mechanical-property formula."}

The size of -14 implies r^2 phi''/phi of about -168, i.e. a steep effective bond (around r^-12). This is plausible but not derived. Problems: (a) Input noise. The E and K binaries come from the same seed 1 and 2 cells, so their errors are correlated. (b) Shared cells. In h3, E and shear both come from the seed 0 cell. In hm, E averages seeds 0 to 2. Per-cell noise (E 3.4 meV median, common shear 0.70 GPa) can carry up to about 15 to 25% of the h3 covariance. The proposed main test measures E and shear on the same cell, so it cannot separate a composition term from cell noise. E and shear targets need disjoint seeds. (c) Baseline. Against an intercept-only correction (the validate.py convention), hm gains about 8%, below the 10% gate. (d) No universal coefficient. With Co: -19/-11. Co-free: -9/-4 (h3) and -11/-1.6 (hm). (e) Both numeric predictions reproduce exactly, but they use the hm V0 11.959779, while the shear protocol uses ctx.vegard 11.949863 (a 0.17 GPa shift). Prior work: the modulus vs mixing-enthalpy correlation is known (Temesi 2023), and tensorial CE expands Cij on the same cluster basis as the energy. I found no fixed-coefficient prediction of clamped shear residuals from the pair-rule energy residual with a 2:1 split. KEEP as L0 only if the pre-registration fixes (a) to (c): disjoint binary seeds for E and K, disjoint target seeds for E and shear, and an intercept-only baseline. 2145: # Academic Paper Reviewer v1.11.1 - Multi-Perspective Academic Paper Review Agent Team
2146: 
2147: Simulates a complete international journal peer review process: automatically identifies the paper's field, dynamically configures 4 card-backed identities (Journal-Fit Reviewer + 3 peer reviewers), and adds the fixed Devil's Advocate as the fifth execution seat. The five role-separated perspectives cover journal fit, methodology, domain expertise, cross-disciplinary viewpoints, and core argument challenges; a separate editorial synthesizer produces the structured Editorial Decision and Revision Roadmap.
2148: 
2149: **v1.1 Improvements**:
2150: 1. Added Devil's Advocate Reviewer - specifically challenges core arguments, detects logical fallacies, and identifies the strongest counter-arguments
2151: 2. Added `re-review` mode - verification review, focused on checking whether revisions address the review comments
2152: 3. Expanded review team from 4 to 5 members
2153: 
2154: > **Routing discipline (v3.9.2):** see `.claude/CLAUDE.md` "Routing Discipline (v3.9.2)" + `shared/references/intent_clarification_protocol.md` for cross-skill routing rules. This skill assumes routing has already settled - ambiguous cross-phase materials should have been clarified upstream.
2155: 
2156: ---
2157: 
2158: ## Quick Start
2159: 
2160: **Simplest command:**
2161: ```
2162: Review this paper: [paste paper or provide file]
2163: ```
2164: 
2165: **Output:**
2166: 1. Automatically identifies the paper's field and methodology type
2167: 2. Dynamically configures four card-backed reviewer identities; the fixed Devil's Advocate is the fifth execution seat
2168: 3. 5 role-separated review reports (4 configuration cards plus the fixed Devil's Advocate, with typed execution provenance)
2169: 4. 1 Editorial Decision Letter + Revision Roadmap
2170:

2188: | Need in-depth investigation of a research topic | `deep-research` |
2189: | Need to revise a paper (already have review comments) | `academic-paper` (revision mode) |
2190: 
2191: ### Quick Mode Selection Guide
2192: 
2193: | Your Situation | Recommended Mode | Spectrum |
2194: |----------------|-----------------|----------|
2195: | Need comprehensive review (first submission) | full | balanced |
2196: | Checking if revisions addressed comments | re-review | fidelity |
2197: | Quick quality assessment (15 min) | quick | fidelity |
2198: | Focus only on methods/statistics | methodology-focus | fidelity |
2199: | Want to learn by doing (guided review) | guided | originality |
2200: | Want to measure this reviewer's bounded decision-error profile on an adjudicated target set | calibration | fidelity |
2201: 
2202: **Spectrum** (v3.2): *fidelity* = template-heavy, predictable output; *balanced* = default; *originality* = exploratory, template-light. See `shared/mode_spectrum.md` for the full cross-skill spectrum table.
2203: 
2204: Not sure? Use `full` for pre-submission review, `re-review` for post-revision verification. Current live reviews and Schema 6 packages declare `NOT_CALIBRATED`; a full-tier calibration run may produce a bounded candidate profile, but live-profile application remains unavailable until its closed artifact and replay validator ship. `calibration` is opt-in: its default full tier measures bounded decision-level FNR/FPR, while the explicitly selected 3-paper directional tier gives only a low-cost Minor/Major boundary signal and remains `NOT_CALIBRATED`.
2205: 
2206: ---
2207: 
2208: ## Agent Team (7 Agents)
2209: 
2210: | # | Agent | Role | Phase |
2211: |---|-------|------|-------|
2212: | 1 | `field_analyst_agent` | Analyzes the paper's field and dynamically configures 4 card-backed identities; the Devil's Advocate remains a fixed fifth seat | Phase 0 |
2213: | 2 | `eic_agent` | Journal-Fit Reviewer - journal fit, originality, overall quality; one panel card, no final-decision authority | Phase 1 |
2214: | 3 | `methodology_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 1 - research design, statistical validity, reproducibility | Phase 1 |
2215: | 4 | `domain_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 2 - literature coverage, theoretical framework, domain contribution | Phase 1 |
2216: | 5 | `perspective_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 3 - cross-disciplinary connections, practical impact, challenging fundamental assumptions | Phase 1 |
2217: | 6 | **`devils_advocate_reviewer_agent`** | **Devil's Advocate - core argument challenges, logical fallacy detection, strongest counter-arguments** | **Phase 1** |
2218: | 7 | `editorial_synthesizer_agent` | Synthesizes all reviews, identifies consensus and disagreements, makes editorial decision | Phase 2 |
2219: 
2220: **Role-name compatibility (#611):** the public display name is **Journal-Fit Reviewer**. The stable implementation identifiers remain `eic_agent` (agent), `eic` (`contract_role` / dispatch role), and `EIC` (serialized reviewer/source ID, including `EIC-W<n>`). Those compatibility tokens do not select a Stage 3' agent file: `editorial_synthesizer_agent` emits first-round decisions, while contract-governed re-review uses its three dedicated calls and checker-derived outcome.
2221: 
2222: ---
2223: 
2224: ## Orchestration Workflow (3 Phases)
2225: 
2226: ```
2227: User: "Review this paper"
2228:      |
2229: === Phase 0: FIELD ANALYSIS & PERSONA CONFIGURATION ===
2230:      |
2231:      +-> [field_analyst_agent] -> Reviewer Configuration Card (x4)
2232:          - Reads the complete paper
2233:          - Identifies: primary discipline, secondary discipline, research paradigm, methodology type, target journal tier, paper maturity
2234:          - Dynamically generates specific identities for 4 card-backed reviewers:
2235:            * Journal-Fit Reviewer (internal `EIC`): which journal/editor perspective, area of expertise, review preferences
2236:            * Reviewer 1 (Methodology): Methodological expertise, what they particularly focus on
2237:            * Reviewer 2 (Domain): Domain expertise, research interests
2238:            * Reviewer 3 (Perspective): Cross-disciplinary angle, what unique perspective they bring
2239:          - The fifth execution seat is the fixed Devil's Advocate, which receives no dynamic configuration card
2240:      |
2241:      ** Presents Reviewer Configuration to user for confirmation (adjustable) **
2242:      |
2243: === Phase 1: PARALLEL MULTI-PERSPECTIVE REVIEW ===
2244:      |
2245:      |-> [eic_agent] -------> Journal-Fit Review Report
2246:      |   - Journal fit, originality, significance, relevance to readership
2247:      |   - Does not go deep into methodology (that's Reviewer 1's job)
2248:      |   - One role-separated card among five - no peer-output channel before commitment (Iron Rule #2)
2249:      |
2250:      |-> [methodology_reviewer_agent] -> Methodology Review Report
2251:      |   - Research design rigor, sampling strategy, data collection
2252:      |   - Analysis method selection, statistical validity, effect sizes
2253:      |   - Reproducibility, data transparency
2254:      |
2255:      |-> [domain_reviewer_agent] -------> Domain Review Report
2256:      |   - Literature review completeness, theoretical framework appropriateness
2257:      |   - Academic argument accuracy, incremental contribution to the field
2258:      |   - Missing key references
2259:      |
2260:      |-> [perspective_reviewer_agent] --> Perspective Review Report
2261:      |   - Cross-disciplinary connections and borrowing opportunities
2262:      |   - Practical applications and policy implications
2263:      |   - Broader social or ethical implications
2264:      |
2265:      +-> [devils_advocate_reviewer_agent] --> Devil's Advocate Report
2266:          - Core argument challenges (strongest counter-arguments)
2267:          - Cherry-picking detection
2268:          - Confirmation bias detection
2269:          - Logic chain validation
2270:          - Overgeneralization detection
2271:          - Alternative paths analysis
2272:          - Stakeholder blind spots
2273:          - "So what?" test
2274:      |
2275: === Phase 2: EDITORIAL SYNTHESIS & DECISION ===
2276:      |
2277:      +-> [editorial_synthesizer_agent] -> Editorial Decision Package
2278:          - Consolidates 5 reports (including Devil's Advocate challenges)
2279:          - Identifies consensus (5 agree) vs. disagreement (divergent opinions)
2280:          - Arbitration and argumentation for disputed issues
2281:          - Devil's Advocate CRITICAL issues are specially flagged in the Editorial Decision
2282:          - Editorial Decision Letter
2283:          - Immutable non-ranking Revision Roadmap core (directly consumed with a separate explicit author sidecar)
2284:      |
2285: === Phase 2.5: REVISION COACHING (Socratic Revision Guidance) ===
2286:      |
2287:      ** Only triggered when Decision = Minor/Major Revision **
2288:      |
2289:      +-> [eic_agent] guides the user through Socratic dialogue:
2290:          1. Overall positioning - "After reading the review comments, what surprised you the most?"
2291:          2. Core issue focus - Guides user to understand consensus issues
2292:          3. Contribution framing probe - ask the Layer-5 later-stage anchored forms
2293:             L5-W1 / L5-W2 / L5-W3 (single-sourced under Layer 5 in
2294:             deep-research/agents/socratic_mentor_agent.md - read the question text
2295:             there), anchored to what the manuscript already claims ("the revised
2296:             paper"). Questions only - never propose, substitute, rank, expand, or
2297:             select a contribution claim (Kong L2 verb test); the user answers.
2298:          4. Explicit author triage - records `will_address`, `wont_address`, or `not_on_point` for every source-ordered item, with no inferred work order
2299:          5. Counter-argument response - Guides user to think about how to respond to Devil's Advocate challenges
2300:          6. Implementation planning - confirms exact block/operation scope and any registered-claim or declined-overlap authorization

2855: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:501:8:    volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
2856: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:502:9: 3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
2857: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:503:10:    that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
2858: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:504:11: 4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
2859: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:505:12:    to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
2860: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:506:13: 5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
2861: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:507:14:    input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
2862: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:508:15: 6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
2863: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:509:16:    (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
2864: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:510:17: 7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
2865: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:511:18:    carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
2866: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:512:19: 8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
2867: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:513:20:    so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
2868: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:514:21:    (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
2869: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:515:22: 9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
2870: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:516:23:    ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
2871: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:517:24:    multicomponent cells can be used.

2875: .orchestra/audits\6bc0e190a8_astra.md:521:28: 11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary

177: """Quantum ESPRESSO (pw.x in WSL) as the L3 reference for stresses and elastic constants.
178: 
179: QE lives in a conda-forge env inside WSL (micromamba env "qe", no sudo needed).
180: Pseudopotentials: SSSP 1.3.0 PBE efficiency, md5 a58f1b3373f330179fd0832c48bb9a52,
181: Materials Cloud Archive 2023.65, doi:10.24435/materialscloud:f3-ym.
182: """
183: 
184: from __future__ import annotations
185: 
186: import datetime as dt
187: import json
188: import re
189: import subprocess
190: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
191: from pathlib import Path
192: 
193: import numpy as np
194: from ase import Atoms
195: from ase.io import read, write
196: 
197: from harness.compute import GPA, cubic_average, voigt_reuss_hill
198: 
199: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
200: RUNS = ROOT / "data" / "dft_runs"
201: DISTRO = "Ubuntu-22.04"
202: PSEUDO_DIR = "/home/can02/pseudo/sssp_eff_1.3"
203: SSSP = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "data" / "sssp_1.3.0_pbe_efficiency.json").read_text())
204: 
205: # Collinear starting moments for the magnetic 3d metals. Cr gets an antiferromagnetic
206: # start on the two bcc sublattices; a commensurate AFM cell is an approximation of its SDW.
207: MAGNETIC = {"Fe": 0.4, "Co": 0.4, "Ni": 0.3, "Mn": 0.4, "Cr": 0.4}
208: 
209: 
210: @dataclass
211: class Settings:
212:     kspacing: float = 0.15          # 1/A, Monkhorst-Pack density (2*pi included)
213:     ecut_scale: float = 1.25        # stresses need a margin above the SSSP energy cutoff
214:     degauss: float = 0.01           # Ry, Marzari-Vanderbilt
215:     np: int = 8                     # 8 physical cores
216:     extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
217:     # Elements whose cutoffs also set this run's cutoff. For mixing energies and curvatures pass the alloy's elements
218:     # to the pure references too, so all terms share one basis (before 2026-10-31 each run used only its own).
219:     ecut_elements: tuple = ()
220:     # Fixed Monkhorst-Pack grid. Finite-strain curvatures must use one grid for every strain; the default picks it from
221:     # the strained cell, which changes it between strains (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18 for Cu3Ir, found 2026-10-31).
222:     kpts: tuple | None = None
223: 
224: 
225: def wsl_path(p: Path) -> str:
226:     s = str(p.resolve()).replace("\\", "/")
227:     return f"/mnt/{s[0].lower()}{s[2:]}"
228: 
229: 
230: def kgrid(atoms: Atoms, kspacing: float) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
231:     rec = np.linalg.norm(atoms.cell.reciprocal(), axis=1) * 2 * np.pi
232:     return tuple(max(1, int(np.ceil(r / kspacing))) for r in rec)
233: 
234: 
235: def magnetize(atoms: Atoms) -> bool:
236:     """Set initial moments in place; AFM checkerboard for Cr. Returns True if spin polarised."""
237:     mags = np.array([MAGNETIC.get(s, 0.0) for s in atoms.get_chemical_symbols()])
238:     if not mags.any():
239:         return False
240:     if "Cr" in atoms.get_chemical_symbols():
241:         a = (2 * atoms.get_volume() / len(atoms)) ** (1 / 3)  # bcc conventional lattice parameter
242:         parity = np.round(2 * atoms.positions[:, 0] / a).astype(int) % 2  # corner vs body centre
243:         mags = np.where(np.array(atoms.get_chemical_symbols()) == "Cr", mags * (1 - 2 * parity), mags)
244:     atoms.set_initial_magnetic_moments(mags * 5)  # ASE maps moments to starting_magnetization
245:     return True
246: 
247: 
248: def run_pw(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, relax_ions: bool = False) -> Atoms:
249:     """Run one pw.x scf/relax with stress. Cached: an existing finished output is reused."""
250:     d = RUNS / tag
251:     d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
252:     out = d / "pw.out"
253:     els = sorted(set(atoms.get_chemical_symbols()))
254:     basis = set(els) | set(s.ecut_elements)
255:     ecut = float(s.extra.get("system.ecutwfc", s.ecut_scale * max(SSSP[e]["cutoff_wfc"] for e in basis)))
256:     ecutrho = s.ecut_scale * max(SSSP[e]["cutoff_rho"] for e in basis)
257:     if out.exists() and "JOB DONE" in out.read_text(errors="ignore"):
258:         cached = re.search(r"ecutwfc\s*=\s*([\d.]+)", (d / "pw.in").read_text())
259:         if cached and abs(float(cached.group(1)) - ecut) > 1e-6:  # a cache hit must not silently change the basis
260:             raise RuntimeError(f"{tag}: cached run used ecutwfc {cached.group(1)}, requested {ecut}; use a new tag")
261:         return read(out, format="espresso-out", index=-1)
262:     scratch = tag.replace("/", "__")
263:     atoms = atoms.copy()
264:     # extra={'system.nspin': 1} must switch magnetism off: initial moments make ASE write nspin 2 back (S3 audit)
265:     spin = s.extra.get("system.nspin", 2) != 1 and magnetize(atoms)
266:     data = {"control": {"calculation": "relax" if relax_ions else "scf", "tstress": True,
267:                         "tprnfor": True, "pseudo_dir": PSEUDO_DIR, "outdir": f"/tmp/qe/{scratch}",
268:                         "disk_io": "low", "forc_conv_thr": 1e-4},
269:             "system": {"ecutwfc": ecut, "ecutrho": ecutrho, "occupations": "smearing",
270:                        "smearing": "mv", "degauss": s.degauss, "nspin": 2 if spin else 1},
271:             "electrons": {"conv_thr": 1e-10 * len(atoms), "mixing_beta": 0.3}}
272:     for k, v in s.extra.items():
273:         data.setdefault(k.split(".")[0], {})[k.split(".")[1]] = v
274:     write(d / "pw.in", atoms, format="espresso-in", input_data=data,
275:           pseudopotentials={e: SSSP[e]["filename"] for e in els}, kpts=s.kpts or kgrid(atoms, s.kspacing))
276:     cmd = (f"export MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX=~/mamba OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; mkdir -p /tmp/qe/{scratch}; cd '{wsl_path(d)}' && "
277:            f"~/bin/micromamba run -n qe mpirun -np {s.np} pw.x -nk {min(s.np, 4)} -in pw.in > pw.out 2> pw.err; "
278:            f"rm -rf /tmp/qe/{scratch}")
279:     subprocess.run(["wsl", "-d", DISTRO, "--", "bash", "-lc", cmd], check=True)
280:     text = out.read_text(errors="ignore")
281:     if "JOB DONE" not in text or "convergence NOT achieved" in text:
282:         raise RuntimeError(f"pw.x failed for {tag}, see {out}")
283:     return read(out, format="espresso-out", index=-1)
284: 
285: 
286: def stress(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, relax_ions: bool) -> np.ndarray:
287:     return read_stress(run_pw(atoms, tag, s, relax_ions))
288: 
289: 
290: def read_stress(a: Atoms) -> np.ndarray:
291:     return a.get_stress(voigt=True) * GPA  # ASE sign: tensile positive
292: 
293: 
294: def elastic_cubic(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, eps: float = 0.01, full: bool = False,
295:                   relax_ions: bool | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
296:     """6x6 tensor (GPa) by central differences. full=False uses only e_xx and e_yz,
297:     which is exact for a cubic crystal and enough for pure elements (4 pw.x runs)."""
298:     if relax_ions is None:
299:         relax_ions = len(set(atoms.get_chemical_symbols())) > 1
300:     cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
301:     voigt = [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1)]
302:     cols = range(6) if full else (0, 3)
303:     C = np.full((6, 6), np.nan)
304:     for j in cols:
305:         k, l = voigt[j]
306:         sig = []
307:         for sign in (+1, -1):
308:             e = np.zeros((3, 3))
309:             if k == l:
310:                 e[k, k] = sign * eps
311:             else:
312:                 e[k, l] = e[l, k] = sign * eps / 2
313:             st = atoms.copy()
314:             st.set_cell(cell0 @ (np.eye(3) + e), scale_atoms=True)
315:             sig.append(stress(st, f"{tag}/e{j}{'p' if sign > 0 else 'm'}", s, relax_ions))
316:         C[:, j] = (sig[0] - sig[1]) / (2 * eps)
317:     if not full:  # fill the cubic tensor from the two columns
318:         c11, c12, c44 = C[0, 0], 0.5 * (C[1, 0] + C[2, 0]), C[3, 3]
319:         C = np.zeros((6, 6))
320:         C[:3, :3] = c12
321:         np.fill_diagonal(C[:3, :3], c11)
322:         C[3:, 3:] = np.eye(3) * c44
323:     return 0.5 * (C + C.T)
324: 
325: 
326: def relax_lattice(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, eps: float = 0.01) -> Atoms:
327:     """Cubic lattice parameter from a parabola fit of pressure vs volume (3 pw.x runs).
328:     Avoids vc-relax Pulay stress issues and keeps every run cached and inspectable."""
329:     cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
330:     scales = np.array([1 - eps, 1.0, 1 + eps])
331:     P = []
332:     for sc in scales:
333:         a = atoms.copy()
334:         a.set_cell(cell0 * sc, scale_atoms=True)
335:         sig = stress(a, f"{tag}/lat{sc:.3f}", s, relax_ions=len(set(a.symbols)) > 1)
336:         P.append(-sig[:3].mean())
337:     root = np.roots(np.polyfit(scales, P, 2))
338:     root = root[np.isreal(root)].real
339:     best = root[np.argmin(abs(root - 1))]
340:     out = atoms.copy()
341:     out.set_cell(cell0 * best, scale_atoms=True)
342:     return out
343: 
344: 
345: def run_alloy(comp_atoms: Atoms, label: str, s: Settings, full: bool | None = None) -> dict:
346:     full = (len(set(comp_atoms.symbols)) > 1) if full is None else full
347:     tag = f"{label}_k{s.kspacing}_e{s.ecut_scale}"
348:     a = relax_lattice(comp_atoms, tag, s)
349:     c11, c12, c44 = cubic_average(elastic_cubic(a, tag, s, full=full))
350:     row = {"label": label, "formula": a.get_chemical_formula(mode="metal"), "natoms": len(a),
351:            "vol_per_atom": a.get_volume() / len(a), "C11": c11, "C12": c12, "C44": c44,
352:            "method": f"QE7.6 PBE SSSP1.3eff k{s.kspacing} ecut x{s.ecut_scale} mv{s.degauss}",
353:            "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
354:     row.update(voigt_reuss_hill(c11, c12, c44))
355:     return row
356:
