411: # Lessons for derivation agents (Astra, Opus)
412: 
413: Read before proposing. Each line is a way a candidate died or nearly died for the wrong reason. Updated 2026-10-31.
414: 
415: 1. Ratios of energies blow up where the denominator crosses zero (R3: n_eff = -3 b/a reached -102 for Cu-Ir). Prefer
416:    predictions linear in measured quantities; if a ratio is essential, say where it is undefined.
417: 2. Compare like with like: clamped with clamped, relaxed with relaxed, random with random. R3 compared a relaxed random
418:    volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
419: 3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
420:    that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
421: 4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
422:    to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
423: 5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
424:    input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
425: 6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
426:    (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
427: 7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
428:    carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
429: 8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
430:    so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
431:    (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
432: 9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
433:    ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
434:    multicomponent cells can be used.
435: 10. Round R2 (Astra): the arena's permutation count capped the smallest reachable p at 1/501, so after five tests no
436:     candidate could pass however good it was. Fixed: n_perm grows with m. Also open: generators set V0 from nominal
437:     fractions while comp_actual differs (~0.5% in volume, ~0.06 meV RMSE effect, not the cause of k ~ 0.8).
438: 11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary
439:     energies at the alloy volume give k 0.94 [0.90, 0.98] and RMSE 10.3 meV with no parameter (data/binary_vgrid.csv).
440: 12. Swarm S1 audit (Astra): (a) scripts/hiso_l12.py did not use ecut_elements, and harness/dft.py picks the k-grid
441:     from the strained cell (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18), so 0.1 meV/atom of strain-dependent error moves K by 1.6 to 4.7
442:     GPa. H-iso results before the fix are not evidence either way; the run is stopped. (b) fix_counts.py treated
443:     0.3333 as the reference weight of equiatomic ternaries (36+36+36 atoms are exact): +0.3 to +0.7 meV added.
444:     (c) B_chem and R in *_fixed.csv are stale. (d) K44 ~ K' is not Zener invariance.
445: 13. k at fixed composition (h1/h3 E(V) curves vs exact binary response): 0.976 [0.956, 1.001]. No reduced volume
446:     response; k ~ 0.8 is the curvature the linear transfer leaves out (94% of the shift).
447: 
448: 14. Shear-curvature volume transfer (prereg 4c29d9754c, result 6e0923b413), 113 unseen h3 alloys, binary curvatures
449:     at the alloy volume, no parameter. Kp: 4.77 -> 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08 (pass). K44: 3.29 -> 2.62,
450:     gain 0.20, p 0.023, refit k 0.86 (fail at p < 0.005). Joint claim FAIL. The first design (sigma = pair-sum residual,
451:     which contains the signal) had power 0.45 and was stopped before any target existed. K44's worst rule errors are
452:     Co-rich (Co ~0.46 with Pt or Cu), where the rule is worse than no transfer; cause not yet audited (hypothesis,
453:     design or numerics). Do not re-split the joint claim after the fact: a K44 or Kp claim needs its own fresh test.
454: 
455: 15. K' alone, fresh blind test (prereg 67a358fc59, result d92844787f, L2 entry recorded): 94 hm_fresh alloys, K' 4.22 ->
456:     1.89 GPa, gain 0.55, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08, 75/94 better. Two independent blind sets now agree for K' (k 1.08 both).
457:     K44 again weaker (gain 0.12, k 0.69, not gated). Why K44 transfers worse than K' is open: Co-rich outliers, or
458:     internal (non-affine) relaxation channels that the clamped protocol suppresses differently for the two shears.
459: 
460: 16. Model swap of the K' rule (prereg 851aec6883, result 86767e478d): medium-mpa-0, same geometry, same 94 hm_fresh
461:     alloys, binaries seed 0 only. K' 4.73 -> 2.28 GPa, gain 0.52, p 2.5e-4, but refit k 1.33 [1.11, 1.51]: the
462:     pre-registered k-contains-1 condition FAILS. K44 gain 0.16, k 0.77. Reading: that the alloy's K' follows the binaries
463:     at the alloy volume and cuts the error in half survives a model with a different shear bias; that the coefficient is
464:     exactly 1 does not (omat 1.08 twice, mpa 1.33). Binary seed noise would pull k down, not up. The two models disagree
465:     most at |dlnV| > 0.2 (K' corr 0.80 vs 0.96 within 0.1). Cause not yet audited. Do not claim "parameter-free" across
466:     models; the PBE check decides which k is physical.
467: 
468: 17. K44 transfer fails only with Co (prereg e410c96a32, result d9460850ce). 120 fresh Co-free alloys: K44 pair 4.68 ->
469:     rule 2.30 GPa, gain 0.51, p 2.5e-4, k 1.23 (PASS). 60 fresh alloys with Co >= 15%: gain 0.11, p 0.08, k 0.70. K'
470:     passes in both. Open confound: the Co-free set has a larger volume signal (pair error 4.68 vs 3.36), so "Co breaks
471:     K44" and "K44 needs a large signal" are not yet separated; match the two sets on |rule - pair| before claiming
472:     a Co mechanism (magnetism is a guess, MACE has no spin).
473:     Confound check (exploratory, same fresh rows, tertiles of |rule - pair|): at matched signal Co-free gain 0.37 / 0.58
474:     vs Co 0.08 / 0.22 (mid / large), and Co alloys carry a larger floor at small signal (rule rms 2.61 vs 1.73 GPa).
475:     The Co effect survives signal matching; not yet a registered claim.
476: 
477: 18. Why K44 looked broken (Opus, swarm S2, blind by file timestamp, confirmed on 60 Co alloys). The part the pair rule
478:     misses is the same in both shears (corr 0.71, slope ~1). K44's volume signal is half of K''s, so the shared floor
479:     swamps it; in Co alloys the floor anticorrelates with the signal and drags k to 0.7. Remove the floor (A = K44 - K'
480:     or e' as covariate) and K44 transfers with k ~1. LESSONS 14-16 failure reason: design, not hypothesis.
481: 
482: 19. Shared SQS seed leak (Opus S2 audit, Astra confirmed). compute.py:56 draws the site permutation from (seed, n)
483:     only, so every seed-0 cell thresholds one random field: seed-0 targets and seed-0 binaries share configuration
484:     noise. K' is immune (gain 0.55-0.58, k 1.07-1.10 for every seed split). K44 is not: leak-free gain 0.06-0.14,
485:     k 0.60-0.77. d9460850ce and the LESSONS 18 Co check used the leak; 9cfc8edaf0 was withdrawn before reading and
486:     re-registered as c2eff007ad with target seed 100. Rule: targets and inputs never share a seed.
487: 
488: 20. Shared floor, disjoint seeds (c2eff007ad -> b86e0d8a40 PASS, 150 alloys): A = K44 - K' transfers (gain 0.49),
489:     corr(e44, e') 0.77, joint k 0.91, b 0.94; plain K44 Co-free gain 0.47, Co 0.09. Astra audit: PLAUSIBLE, the
490:     null could not separate a compositional floor from same-cell noise. A shared-channel claim needs targets for the
491:     two channels from different cells. Test fd786169e3.
492: 
493: 21. The shared floor is compositional (fd786169e3 PASS, two cells per composition, unique seeds): cross-cell corr
494:     0.75 vs same-cell 0.79, k 0.92, b 0.95; Astra audit PLAUSIBLE (cell noise ~5% of the shared covariance). Next
495:     doubt is a known identity: clamped curvatures carry the initial stress, K44 = C44 + s_yy, K' = C' + (s_xx+s_yy)/2.
496:     A floor claim must survive subtracting it (k_floor_stress.py). Pre-register every step; one audit, one test.
497: 
498: 22. The floor survives the known pre-stress identity (ede47f1d65 PASS; Astra PLAUSIBLE): corrected cross-cell r
499:     0.67, k 0.99, b 0.79. Mixing pre-stress is 7 GPa rms but pair-additive (rule leaves 0.7 GPa), so it was never the
500:     floor. Remaining doubt: error shared through the binary references (b drops to 0.4-0.5 with single disjoint
501:     seeds). Shared-residual claims need two independent binary panels, as in k_mpa_equiv.py.
502: 23. k = 1 is retired (88b9465108 FAIL, cause hypothesis; Astra found no coding error). Under mpa, 1200 alloys: k 1.14
503:     [1.10, 1.18]; the rule still halves the error (4.81 to 2.21 GPa). k is not a model constant but composition
504:     dependent: 3 elements 1.00, Cu-free 1.00, Cu 1.24, alloys with max|dlnV| > 0.25 1.41; omat shows the same pattern
505:     (1.11). The pair transfer under-predicts at large size mismatch. A power sim that treats the target residual as
506:     cell noise is optimistic: most of it is compositional and does not average out over cells.
507: """H-iso check in cubic L1_2 cells: clamped mixing shear curvatures K44, Kp with MACE or PBE.
508: 
509: python scripts/hiso_l12.py mace | dft
510: A3B L1_2 (4-atom cubic cell, B on the corner site), clamped at Vegard volume, pure fcc references at the same volume
511: and the same deformation. Strains +-0.02 (three-point curvature). PBE uses kspacing 0.10 (shear needs the fine grid).
512: """
513: 
514: import datetime as dt
515: import os
516: import sys
517: from pathlib import Path
518: 
519: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
520: os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
521: sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
522: 
523: import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
524: import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
525: from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402
526: 
527: from harness.compute import GPA  # noqa: E402
528: 
529: CELLS = [("Cu", "Ir"), ("Cu", "Rh"), ("Pd", "Ir"), ("Au", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Rh"),  # A3B with Ir/Rh
530:          ("Cu", "Au"), ("Pt", "Cu")]  # controls without Ir/Rh; order = MACE |K| (PBE is slow, strongest first)
531: S = 0.02
532: SYM_DONE = {"Cu3Ir": ("g-", "t-")}  # computed both signs here; used as the symmetry check
533: METHOD = sys.argv[1]
534: pv = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv").set_index("el")["vol_per_atom"]
535: 
536: if METHOD == "mace":
537:     from harness import compute
538:     calc = compute.calculator()
539: 
540:     def energy(atoms, tag):
541:         atoms.calc = calc
542:         return atoms.get_potential_energy() / len(atoms)
543: else:
544:     from harness import dft
545:     st = dft.Settings(kspacing=0.10, np=int(os.environ.get("HISO_NP", "4")))
546: 
547:     def energy(atoms, tag):
548:         return dft.run_pw(atoms, f"hiso/{tag}", st).get_potential_energy() / len(atoms)
549: 
550: DEF = {"0": np.eye(3), "g+": np.eye(3) + S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
551:        "g-": np.eye(3) - S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
552:        "t+": np.diag([np.exp(S), np.exp(-S), 1.0]), "t-": np.diag([np.exp(-S), np.exp(S), 1.0])}
553: 
554: 
555: def strained(symbols, v, F):
556:     a = bulk("Cu", "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True)
557:     a.symbols = list(symbols)
558:     a.set_cell(a.cell * (v * 4 / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
559:     a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
560:     return a
561: 
562: 
563: OUT = ROOT / "data" / f"hiso_l12_{METHOD}.csv"
564: done = set(pd.read_csv(OUT)["cell"]) if OUT.exists() else set()
565: for A, B in CELLS:
566:     name = f"{A}3{B}"
567:     if name in done:
568:         continue
569:     v = 0.75 * pv[A] + 0.25 * pv[B]
570:     vt = f"{v:.3f}"
571:     em = {}
572:     for k, F in DEF.items():
573:         if k in ("g-", "t-") and k not in SYM_DONE.get(name, ()):  # cubic L1_2: y -> -y and x <-> y are symmetries
574:             continue
575:         e_ab = energy(strained([B, A, A, A], v, F), f"{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
576:         e_a = energy(strained([A] * 4, v, F), f"{A}_{k}_v{vt}")
577:         e_b = energy(strained([B] * 4, v, F), f"{B}_{k}_v{vt}")
578:         em[k] = e_ab - 0.75 * e_a - 0.25 * e_b
579:     em.setdefault("g-", em["g+"])
580:     em.setdefault("t-", em["t+"])
581:     c44 = (em["g+"] + em["g-"] - 2 * em["0"]) / (2 * S**2)   # E = c s^2
582:     cp = (em["t+"] + em["t-"] - 2 * em["0"]) / (2 * S**2)
583:     r = {"cell": name, "method": METHOD, "V": v, "E_mix": em["0"], "K44": 2 * c44 / v * GPA, "Kp": cp / (2 * v) * GPA,
584:          "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
585:     pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(OUT, mode="a", header=not OUT.exists(), index=False)
586:     print(name, f"E_mix {em['0']*1000:+7.1f} meV  K44 {r['K44']:+7.2f}  Kp {r['Kp']:+7.2f} GPa", flush=True)
587: 
588:  succeeded in 2165ms:
589: """H-iso check, corrected numerics (v2): clamped mixing shear curvatures K44, Kp of cubic L1_2 cells with PBE.
590: 
591: python scripts/hiso_l12_v2.py [dense]
592: Fixes found by the swarm S1 audit in scripts/hiso_l12.py: the alloy and both pure references now share one cutoff
593: (ecut_elements = (A, B)) and one k-grid, taken from the unstrained cell, for every strain. "dense" repeats Cu3Ir and
594: Ag3Rh at kspacing 0.08 as a convergence check. Criteria 6cb3c2a936 are unchanged; the old results are not used.
595: A3B L1_2 (4-atom cubic cell, B on the corner site), clamped at Vegard volume, pure fcc references at the same volume
596: and the same deformation. Strains +-0.02 (three-point curvature). PBE uses kspacing 0.10 (shear needs the fine grid).
597: """
598: 
599: import datetime as dt
600: import os
601: import sys
602: from pathlib import Path
603: 
604: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
605: os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
606: sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
607: 
608: import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
609: import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
610: from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402
611: 
612: from harness.compute import GPA  # noqa: E402
613: 
614: CELLS = [("Cu", "Ir"), ("Cu", "Rh"), ("Pd", "Ir"), ("Au", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Rh"),  # A3B with Ir/Rh
615:          ("Cu", "Au"), ("Pt", "Cu")]  # controls without Ir/Rh; order = MACE |K| (PBE is slow, strongest first)
616: S = 0.02
617: SYM_DONE = {"Cu3Ir": ("g-", "t-")}  # computed both signs here; used as the symmetry check
618: METHOD = "dft"
619: DENSE = "dense" in sys.argv
620: KSP = 0.08 if DENSE else 0.10
621: if DENSE:
622:     CELLS = [("Cu", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Rh")]

625: from harness import dft  # noqa: E402

627: NP = int(os.environ.get("HISO_NP", "2"))

629: 
630: 
631: def energy(atoms, tag):
632:     return dft.run_pw(atoms, f"hiso2{'d' if DENSE else ''}/{tag}", ST["s"]).get_potential_energy() / len(atoms)
633: 
634: DEF = {"0": np.eye(3), "g+": np.eye(3) + S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
635:        "g-": np.eye(3) - S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
636:        "t+": np.diag([np.exp(S), np.exp(-S), 1.0]), "t-": np.diag([np.exp(-S), np.exp(S), 1.0])}
637: 
638: 
639: def strained(symbols, v, F):
640:     a = bulk("Cu", "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True)
641:     a.symbols = list(symbols)
642:     a.set_cell(a.cell * (v * 4 / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
643:     a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
644:     return a
645: 
646: 
647: OUT = ROOT / "data" / f"hiso_l12_dft_v2{'_dense' if DENSE else ''}.csv"
648: done = set(pd.read_csv(OUT)["cell"]) if OUT.exists() else set()
649: for A, B in CELLS:
650:     name = f"{A}3{B}"
651:     if name in done:
652:         continue
653:     v = 0.75 * pv[A] + 0.25 * pv[B]
654:     vt = f"{v:.3f}"
655:     ST["s"] = dft.Settings(kspacing=KSP, np=NP, ecut_elements=(A, B),
656:                            kpts=dft.kgrid(strained([B, A, A, A], v, np.eye(3)), KSP))
657:     em = {}
658:     for k, F in DEF.items():
659:         if k in ("g-", "t-") and k not in SYM_DONE.get(name, ()):  # cubic L1_2: y -> -y and x <-> y are symmetries
660:             continue
661:         e_ab = energy(strained([B, A, A, A], v, F), f"{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
662:         e_a = energy(strained([A] * 4, v, F), f"{A}_{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
663:         e_b = energy(strained([B] * 4, v, F), f"{B}_{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
664:         em[k] = e_ab - 0.75 * e_a - 0.25 * e_b
665:     em.setdefault("g-", em["g+"])
666:     em.setdefault("t-", em["t+"])
667:     c44 = (em["g+"] + em["g-"] - 2 * em["0"]) / (2 * S**2)   # E = c s^2
668:     cp = (em["t+"] + em["t-"] - 2 * em["0"]) / (2 * S**2)
669:     r = {"cell": name, "method": "dft_v2", "kpts": "x".join(map(str, ST["s"].kpts)), "V": v, "E_mix": em["0"], "K44": 2 * c44 / v * GPA, "Kp": cp / (2 * v) * GPA,
670:          "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
671:     pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(OUT, mode="a", header=not OUT.exists(), index=False)

705: 1: # Binary shear curvatures read at the alloy's volume: a preregistered test of a transfer rule for fcc solid solutions with machine-learned potentials
706: 2: 
707: 3: Muhammet Can Ergani?
708: 4: Independent researcher, METU graduate, Ankara, T?rkiye. ORCID 0009-0001-1397-6366
709: 5: 
710: 6: Draft v3, 2026-11-01, after the Astra audit of v2 (`.orchestra/audits/draft_v2_astra.md`). Numerical provenance is
711: 7: given through ledger entries in `claims/claims.jsonl` and named analysis files. Exploratory calculations are marked
712: 8: as such and kept apart from preregistered tests. The only open item before submission is the archive DOI.
713: 9: 
714: 10: ## Abstract
715: 11: 
716: 12: Building on established binary extrapolation, volume-dependent interactions and tensorial cluster expansions, we test
717: 13: one specific, fixed-coefficient prescription for the clamped mixing part of the tetragonal shear curvature K' of
718: 14: random fcc solid solutions: each equiatomic binary curvature is evaluated at the multicomponent alloy's Vegard volume
719: 15: rather than at the binary's own. For 3 to 5 component alloys of Ag, Au, Co, Cu, Ir, Ni, Pd, Pt and Rh evaluated with
720: 16: the MACE machine-learned potential, this halves the error of the same pair sum taken at the binary volumes (4.2 to
721: 17: 1.9 GPa on 94 compositions; 4.8 to 2.2 GPa on 1200 further compositions under a second MACE model). The transfer is
722: 18: not exact. The refit slope is 1.08 under one model and 1.14 (90% CI 1.10 to 1.18) under the other, and in
723: 19: exploratory splits it rises with the size mismatch between components, so the rule under-predicts alloys with large
724: 20: volume differences. For the C44-type shear K44 the rule is weak. Correlated residuals of the two shears persist
725: 21: across independent target cells and after removal of the clamped pre-stress, which supports a composition-dependent
726: 22: shared residual, but error shared through the binary references remains an unresolved alternative. Primary tests
727: 23: were entered in an append-only ledger, with simulated power, before their new target calculations, and passing
728: 24: results received separate code-and-data audits by a second language model. All targets are machine-learned-potential
729: 25: energies; first-principles validation is pending and is the main limit of this work.
730: 26: 
731: 27: ## 1. Introduction
732: 28: 
733: 29: 1. Liu et al. (2010) developed CALPHAD-style models for elastic coefficients, and Marker et al. (2017) applied this
734: 30:    approach to bcc Ti alloys using relaxed first-principles inputs, each at its own equilibrium volume. Marker
735: 31:    reported average Young's modulus deviations of about 7 GPa with binary parameters and 5 GPa with ternary terms for
736: 32:    13 multicomponent alloys. Huhn et al. (2014) compared alloy moduli with effective-medium estimates based on pure
737: 33:    elements. Linton and Aidhy (2023) trained ML models on binaries, and Mirzaee et al. (2024) a CNN on charge densities
738: 34:    including binary and ternary data. These studies motivate testing how shear transfers from simpler systems.
739: 35: 2. Volume-dependent effective cluster interactions (Asta et al. 1992; Geng et al. 2005), the alloy-volume formalism
740: 36:    for binaries (Ferreira et al. 1987, 1989) and tensorial or strain-dependent cluster expansions (van de
741: 37:    Walle 2008; Behara et al. 2023, which includes shear strain variables) are established. Our search did not
742: 38:    identify the specific fixed-coefficient transfer tested here: clamped multicomponent mixing K' estimated from
743: 39:    equiatomic binary curvatures at the alloy Vegard volume. This is a search-bounded statement, not proof that no
744: 40:    prior work exists.
745: 41: 3. Formally the rule is a pair-truncated tensorial cluster expansion or a zeroth-order Redlich-Kister sum with a
746: 42:    specified evaluation volume. The contribution is this prescription and its tested performance: (i) where the
747: 43:    binary terms are evaluated, (ii) a preregistered test of that choice, (iii) where it stops working, and (iv) how
748: 44:    the C44-type shear differs. In a different field, Hofgard et al. (2026) obtained large gains by changing the
749: 45:    target representation of an ML model while keeping the model. Here the target stays K'_mix; what changes is the
750: 46:    volume at which unchanged binary inputs are read.
751: 47: 
752: 48: ## 2. Methods
753: 49: 
754: 50: **Cells.** Random fcc solid solutions in 108-atom cubic supercells (3x3x3), built by randomly shuffling species over
755: 51: the sites without SQS optimisation. Atoms stay on ideal sites (no ionic or cell relaxation). The volume is fixed at
756: 52: the composition's Vegard volume V0 from the model's pure-element volumes.
757: 53: 
758: 54: **Observable.** E_mix(V, F) = E_alloy - sum x_i E_i per atom, every pure reference at the same volume and the same
759: 55: deformation F. K' from F = diag(e^t, e^-t, 1), K44 from F = I + g e_x e_y, five amplitudes in [-0.01, 0.01],
760: 56: quadratic fit, K' = c2/(2V), K44 = 2 c2/V. The target generators use the cell's actual integer-count fractions for
761: 57: the pure references; the historical exploratory a2 dataset is an exception (Section 3.1). With tensile-positive
762: 58: mixing stress and Green-Lagrange energy coefficients, K44 = C^L_xyxy + s_yy and K' = (C^L_xxxx + C^L_yyyy -
763: 59: 2 C^L_xxyy)/4 + (s_xx + s_yy)/2. The elastic part reduces to (C11 - C12)/2 only in the cubic limit, and subtracting
764: 60: the stress terms does not give relaxed, zero-pressure elastic constants.
765: 61: 
766: 62: **Binary inputs.** All 36 equiatomic pairs, 13 log-volume points ln(V/V_ij) in [-0.4, 0.4], cubic spline per pair.
767: 63: The omat grid uses seeds 0 to 2; the first mpa grid seed 0; the 1200-composition test two three-seed panels (20 to 22,
768: 64: 23 to 25).
769: 65: 
770: 66: **Rule.** K'_mix(alloy) = sum_{i<j} 4 x_i x_j K'_ij(ln V0/V_ij). Baselines: the same sum at ln V0/V_ij = 0 ("pair at
771: 67: V_ij"), and two own-volume Muggianu analogues built from pure-element curvatures (Section 3.4).
772: 68: 
773: 69: **Seeds.** The site permutation of a cell depends only on (seed, n), so cells with equal seed and size share a
774: 70: permutation field. The original h3 and hm_fresh shear tests used target seed 0 and binary seeds 0 to 2, and the first
775: 71: mpa model swap used seed 0 for both; these historical tests shared a permutation field between targets and inputs.
776: 72: After this was found (Section 4) target and binary seeds were separated: the floor tests use target seeds of 100 and
777: 73: above, and the 1200-composition test uses unique target seeds from 10000 with binary panels 20 to 25. Omat seed-split
778: 74: checks kept the K' improvement (gain 0.55 to 0.58, k 1.07 to 1.10) but showed sensitivity for K44.
779: 75: 
780: 76: **Models.** MACE medium-omat-0 (Batatia et al.), calibrated in this project on 14 cubic metals (fcc B, G MAE about
781: 77: 12%, e5ef5a57a3). Second model: medium-mpa-0, with omat geometry (V_ij, V0) so that only the energies change.
782: 78: 
783: 79: **Protocol.** Hypotheses come from two LLM agents (GPT-6-Astra via Codex, Claude Opus), who see the problem, the
784: 80: limits and the training data, never sealed holdouts. Before the new target calculations of a primary test, the

787: 162: | PBE cutoff mismatch | audit, 7e0ff785d1 | 30.7 meV/atom shift in the Pt reference; correction checked to 0.002 meV/atom | alloy-matched cutoffs; ordered-cell L1 check changed from FAIL to PASS |
788: 163: | Holdout used for model selection | audit, d26bd71285 | 113 of 207 pooled energy rows were selection data | "two independent holdouts" withdrawn; hm_fresh-only RMSE 36.4 to 13.1 meV/atom |

794: 169: 
795: 170: ## 5. Discussion and limits
796: 171: 
797: 172: 1. Model only. Every target is a MACE energy. The slope already differs between datasets and models (1.08 to 1.14).
798: 173:    In an eight-cell ordered L1_2 A3B diagnostic (preliminary, subject to convergence checks and audit), Au3Ir has
799: 174:    K44 = -32.4 GPa in PBE and +3.2 GPa in MACE; sign agreement is 8/8 for K' and 5/8 for K44. This does not validate
800: 175:    transfer to random alloys. An L3 test needs at least 15 independent DFT or experimental rows from composition
801: 176:    families absent from training, with the rule and coefficient frozen beforehand. This is future work.
802: 177: 2. Clamped, unrelaxed cells: K'_mix is not the measured C'. On 43 previously examined equiatomic ternaries, relaxed-
803: 178:    binary Muggianu gives C' RMSE 3.08 GPa and a volume-transfer chain 2.53 GPa (gain 0.18, p about 0.08). The chain
804: 179:    also uses the measured relaxed target volume. This exploratory comparison shows neither a significant improvement
805: 180:    nor equivalence at zero pressure.
806: 181: 3. The rule under-predicts at large size mismatch (Section 3.5). A correction has not been tested.
807: 182: 4. fcc late transition and noble metals only. None of the three calibrated MACE models passed the bcc shear
808: 183:    criterion in this project.
809: 184: 5. The rule is a regular-solution or tensorial-CE truncation with a specified volume; we do not claim a new law.
810: 185:

2434: .orchestra/audits\draft_v3_astra.md:5774:59:{"round": "S3/cobalt", "candidate": "astra_3", "prior": "UNCLEAR", "refs": ["arXiv:2605.28395", "arXiv:2312.17596", "arXiv:2507.18935 (non-magnetic vs spin-polarized DP for Fe-Cr-C: static properties need the spin branch)"], "verdict": "KEEP", "why": "Sound intervention. Switching spin on and off at fixed chemistry, volume and positions isolates the magnetic term. It says correctly that the nonspin arm is not paramagnetic, that the ordered cell is not the random alloy, and that this is not L3. It runs only after astra_2 and after the astra_1 fix. Fix before running: (1) CoCu2Pt in the 4-atom cubic cell is tetragonal (Co on the corner, Pt on one face centre, Cu on two). So C44 differs from C66, and Kp depends on the axes. Fix the Pt axis and use the exact F matrices from k_shear_transfer.py F_of in MACE and in both PBE arms. (2) Report D for the total cell curvature as well as the mixing curvature. Pure Co at 12.6 A^3/atom is expanded about 16% and strongly magnetic, so a mixing D alone can be driven by the reference. (3) Compare MACE on the Co minus Ni difference, so MACE's common shear softening cancels. Four numbers (2 cells x 2 channels) cannot carry an RMSE ratio on their own. (4) The cost is underestimated. Measured hiso2 runs (4-atom L12, kspacing 0.10, 2 MPI, nonmagnetic): 5 min wall unstrained, 18-51 min sheared. With lower symmetry and spin, about 50 SCF is more like 60-150 core-h than 20-50. Prior: implicit magnetism in MLIPs and MACE's partial magnetoelastic failures in Fe-Ni are known. No prior was found for Co in Cu/Pt fcc shear mixing curvatures."}

Rebuilding Ag-Ir with same-mesh 4-atom references gives dE/dlnV -437 to -469 meV (7%) and n_eff 2.57 to 2.74. Pd-Pt moves 13.88 to 13.93, so the L1 verdict 4c5076a083 stands. H-iso: Kp changes by 200272/V GPa per eV, which is 15.9 GPa per meV/atom at V=12.57. The Nb k-test (conv/, 0.10 against 0.07) shows a mesh-switched cell 0.22 meV/atom off against 0.06 for its partner. That implies 1.5 to 5 GPa on Kp for Cu3Ir (-55.7) and Cu3Rh (-36.9), and leaves the sign of Pd3Ir's Kp (-1.5) unresolved. K44 and the silver cells are clean. Also, scripts/hiso_l12.py:39 sets no ecut_elements, so pure references run at their own cutoff (Rh at 43.75 Ry against Cu3Rh at 112.5). The E_mix column in hiso_l12_dft.csv is off by up to 6 meV: Cu3Rh -14.2 should be about -8.2 by ecut_shift_table. The curvatures should be insensitive to this because the strains are isochoric and a volume-only basis error drops out.",

2612: .orchestra/audits\draft_v2_astra.md:14773:59:{"round": "S3/cobalt", "candidate": "astra_3", "prior": "UNCLEAR", "refs": ["arXiv:2605.28395", "arXiv:2312.17596", "arXiv:2507.18935 (non-magnetic vs spin-polarized DP for Fe-Cr-C: static properties need the spin branch)"], "verdict": "KEEP", "why": "Sound intervention. Switching spin on and off at fixed chemistry, volume and positions isolates the magnetic term. It says correctly that the nonspin arm is not paramagnetic, that the ordered cell is not the random alloy, and that this is not L3. It runs only after astra_2 and after the astra_1 fix. Fix before running: (1) CoCu2Pt in the 4-atom cubic cell is tetragonal (Co on the corner, Pt on one face centre, Cu on two). So C44 differs from C66, and Kp depends on the axes. Fix the Pt axis and use the exact F matrices from k_shear_transfer.py F_of in MACE and in both PBE arms. (2) Report D for the total cell curvature as well as the mixing curvature. Pure Co at 12.6 A^3/atom is expanded about 16% and strongly magnetic, so a mixing D alone can be driven by the reference. (3) Compare MACE on the Co minus Ni difference, so MACE's common shear softening cancels. Four numbers (2 cells x 2 channels) cannot carry an RMSE ratio on their own. (4) The cost is underestimated. Measured hiso2 runs (4-atom L12, kspacing 0.10, 2 MPI, nonmagnetic): 5 min wall unstrained, 18-51 min sheared. With lower symmetry and spin, about 50 SCF is more like 60-150 core-h than 20-50. Prior: implicit magnetism in MLIPs and MACE's partial magnetoelastic failures in Fe-Ni are known. No prior was found for Co in Cu/Pt fcc shear mixing curvatures."}

2700: 1:"""H-iso check, corrected numerics (v2): clamped mixing shear curvatures K44, Kp of cubic L1_2 cells with PBE.
2701: 2:
2702: 3:python scripts/hiso_l12_v2.py [dense]
2703: 4:Fixes found by the swarm S1 audit in scripts/hiso_l12.py: the alloy and both pure references now share one cutoff
2704: 5:(ecut_elements = (A, B)) and one k-grid, taken from the unstrained cell, for every strain. "dense" repeats Cu3Ir and
2705: 6:Ag3Rh at kspacing 0.08 as a convergence check. Criteria 6cb3c2a936 are unchanged; the old results are not used.
2706: 7:A3B L1_2 (4-atom cubic cell, B on the corner site), clamped at Vegard volume, pure fcc references at the same volume
2707: 8:and the same deformation. Strains +-0.02 (three-point curvature). PBE uses kspacing 0.10 (shear needs the fine grid).
2708: 9:"""
2709: 10:
2710: 11:import datetime as dt
2711: 12:import os
2712: 13:import sys
2713: 14:from pathlib import Path
2714: 15:
2715: 16:ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
2716: 17:os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
2717: 18:sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
2718: 19:
2719: 20:import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
2720: 21:import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
2721: 22:from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402
2722: 23:
2723: 24:from harness.compute import GPA  # noqa: E402
2724: 25:
2725: 26:CELLS = [("Cu", "Ir"), ("Cu", "Rh"), ("Pd", "Ir"), ("Au", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Rh"),  # A3B with Ir/Rh
2726: 27:         ("Cu", "Au"), ("Pt", "Cu")]  # controls without Ir/Rh; order = MACE |K| (PBE is slow, strongest first)
2727: 28:S = 0.02
2728: 29:SYM_DONE = {"Cu3Ir": ("g-", "t-")}  # computed both signs here; used as the symmetry check
2729: 30:METHOD = "dft"
2730: 31:DENSE = "dense" in sys.argv
2731: 32:KSP = 0.08 if DENSE else 0.10
2732: 33:if DENSE:
2733: 34:    CELLS = [("Cu", "Ir"), ("Ag", "Rh")]
2734: 35:pv = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv").set_index("el")["vol_per_atom"]
2735: 36:
2736: 37:from harness import dft  # noqa: E402
2737: 38:
2738: 39:NP = int(os.environ.get("HISO_NP", "2"))
2739: 40:ST = {}
2740: 41:
2741: 42:
2742: 43:def energy(atoms, tag):
2743: 44:    return dft.run_pw(atoms, f"hiso2{'d' if DENSE else ''}/{tag}", ST["s"]).get_potential_energy() / len(atoms)
2744: 45:
2745: 46:DEF = {"0": np.eye(3), "g+": np.eye(3) + S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
2746: 47:       "g-": np.eye(3) - S * np.outer([1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]),
2747: 48:       "t+": np.diag([np.exp(S), np.exp(-S), 1.0]), "t-": np.diag([np.exp(-S), np.exp(S), 1.0])}
2748: 49:
2749: 50:
2750: 51:def strained(symbols, v, F):
2751: 52:    a = bulk("Cu", "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True)
2752: 53:    a.symbols = list(symbols)
2753: 54:    a.set_cell(a.cell * (v * 4 / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
2754: 55:    a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
2755: 56:    return a
2756: 57:
2757: 58:
2758: 59:OUT = ROOT / "data" / f"hiso_l12_dft_v2{'_dense' if DENSE else ''}.csv"
2759: 60:done = set(pd.read_csv(OUT)["cell"]) if OUT.exists() else set()
2760: 61:for A, B in CELLS:
2761: 62:    name = f"{A}3{B}"
2762: 63:    if name in done:
2763: 64:        continue
2764: 65:    v = 0.75 * pv[A] + 0.25 * pv[B]
2765: 66:    vt = f"{v:.3f}"
2766: 67:    ST["s"] = dft.Settings(kspacing=KSP, np=NP, ecut_elements=(A, B),
2767: 68:                           kpts=dft.kgrid(strained([B, A, A, A], v, np.eye(3)), KSP))
2768: 69:    em = {}
2769: 70:    for k, F in DEF.items():
2770: 71:        if k in ("g-", "t-") and k not in SYM_DONE.get(name, ()):  # cubic L1_2: y -> -y and x <-> y are symmetries
2771: 72:            continue
2772: 73:        e_ab = energy(strained([B, A, A, A], v, F), f"{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
2773: 74:        e_a = energy(strained([A] * 4, v, F), f"{A}_{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
2774: 75:        e_b = energy(strained([B] * 4, v, F), f"{B}_{name}_{k}_v{vt}")
2775: 76:        em[k] = e_ab - 0.75 * e_a - 0.25 * e_b
2776: 77:    em.setdefault("g-", em["g+"])
2777: 78:    em.setdefault("t-", em["t+"])
2778: 79:    c44 = (em["g+"] + em["g-"] - 2 * em["0"]) / (2 * S**2)   # E = c s^2
2779: 80:    cp = (em["t+"] + em["t-"] - 2 * em["0"]) / (2 * S**2)
2780: 81:    r = {"cell": name, "method": "dft_v2", "kpts": "x".join(map(str, ST["s"].kpts)), "V": v, "E_mix": em["0"], "K44": 2 * c44 / v * GPA, "Kp": cp / (2 * v) * GPA,
2781: 82:         "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
2782: 83:    pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(OUT, mode="a", header=not OUT.exists(), index=False)
2783: 84:    print(name, f"E_mix {em['0']*1000:+7.1f} meV  K44 {r['K44']:+7.2f}  Kp {r['Kp']:+7.2f} GPa", flush=True)

2823: 40:    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
2824: 41:    # Elements whose cutoffs also set this run's cutoff. For mixing energies and curvatures pass the alloy's elements
2825: 42:    # to the pure references too, so all terms share one basis (before 2026-10-31 each run used only its own).
2826: 43:    ecut_elements: tuple = ()
2827: 44:    # Fixed Monkhorst-Pack grid. Finite-strain curvatures must use one grid for every strain; the default picks it from
2828: 45:    # the strained cell, which changes it between strains (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18 for Cu3Ir, found 2026-10-31).
2829: 46:    kpts: tuple | None = None
2830: 47:
2831: 48:
2832: 49:def wsl_path(p: Path) -> str:
2833: 50:    s = str(p.resolve()).replace("\\", "/")
2834: 51:    return f"/mnt/{s[0].lower()}{s[2:]}"
2835: 52:
2836: 53:
2837: 54:def kgrid(atoms: Atoms, kspacing: float) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
2838: 55:    rec = np.linalg.norm(atoms.cell.reciprocal(), axis=1) * 2 * np.pi
2839: 56:    return tuple(max(1, int(np.ceil(r / kspacing))) for r in rec)
2840: 57:
2841: 58:
2842: 59:def magnetize(atoms: Atoms) -> bool:
2843: 60:    """Set initial moments in place; AFM checkerboard for Cr. Returns True if spin polarised."""
2844: 61:    mags = np.array([MAGNETIC.get(s, 0.0) for s in atoms.get_chemical_symbols()])
2845: 62:    if not mags.any():
2846: 63:        return False
2847: 64:    if "Cr" in atoms.get_chemical_symbols():
2848: 65:        a = (2 * atoms.get_volume() / len(atoms)) ** (1 / 3)  # bcc conventional lattice parameter
2849: 66:        parity = np.round(2 * atoms.positions[:, 0] / a).astype(int) % 2  # corner vs body centre
2850: 67:        mags = np.where(np.array(atoms.get_chemical_symbols()) == "Cr", mags * (1 - 2 * parity), mags)
2851: 68:    atoms.set_initial_magnetic_moments(mags * 5)  # ASE maps moments to starting_magnetization
2852: 69:    return True
2853: 70:
2854: 71:
2855: 72:def run_pw(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, relax_ions: bool = False) -> Atoms:
2856: 73:    """Run one pw.x scf/relax with stress. Cached: an existing finished output is reused."""
2857: 74:    d = RUNS / tag
2858: 75:    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
2859: 76:    out = d / "pw.out"
2860: 77:    els = sorted(set(atoms.get_chemical_symbols()))
2861: 78:    basis = set(els) | set(s.ecut_elements)
2862: 79:    ecut = float(s.extra.get("system.ecutwfc", s.ecut_scale * max(SSSP[e]["cutoff_wfc"] for e in basis)))
2863: 80:    ecutrho = s.ecut_scale * max(SSSP[e]["cutoff_rho"] for e in basis)
2864: 81:    if out.exists() and "JOB DONE" in out.read_text(errors="ignore"):
2865: 82:        cached = re.search(r"ecutwfc\s*=\s*([\d.]+)", (d / "pw.in").read_text())
2866: 83:        if cached and abs(float(cached.group(1)) - ecut) > 1e-6:  # a cache hit must not silently change the basis
2867: 84:            raise RuntimeError(f"{tag}: cached run used ecutwfc {cached.group(1)}, requested {ecut}; use a new tag")
2868: 85:        return read(out, format="espresso-out", index=-1)
2869: 86:    scratch = tag.replace("/", "__")
2870: 87:    atoms = atoms.copy()
2871: 88:    # extra={'system.nspin': 1} must switch magnetism off: initial moments make ASE write nspin 2 back (S3 audit)
2872: 89:    spin = s.extra.get("system.nspin", 2) != 1 and magnetize(atoms)
2873: 90:    data = {"control": {"calculation": "relax" if relax_ions else "scf", "tstress": True,
2874: 91:                        "tprnfor": True, "pseudo_dir": PSEUDO_DIR, "outdir": f"/tmp/qe/{scratch}",
2875: 92:                        "disk_io": "low", "forc_conv_thr": 1e-4},
2876: 93:            "system": {"ecutwfc": ecut, "ecutrho": ecutrho, "occupations": "smearing",
2877: 94:                       "smearing": "mv", "degauss": s.degauss, "nspin": 2 if spin else 1},
2878: 95:            "electrons": {"conv_thr": 1e-10 * len(atoms), "mixing_beta": 0.3}}
2879: 96:    for k, v in s.extra.items():
2880: 97:        data.setdefault(k.split(".")[0], {})[k.split(".")[1]] = v
2881: 98:    write(d / "pw.in", atoms, format="espresso-in", input_data=data,
2882: 99:          pseudopotentials={e: SSSP[e]["filename"] for e in els}, kpts=s.kpts or kgrid(atoms, s.kspacing))
2883: 100:    cmd = (f"export MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX=~/mamba OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; mkdir -p /tmp/qe/{scratch}; cd '{wsl_path(d)}' && "
2884: 101:           f"~/bin/micromamba run -n qe mpirun -np {s.np} pw.x -nk {min(s.np, 4)} -in pw.in > pw.out 2> pw.err; "
2885: 102:           f"rm -rf /tmp/qe/{scratch}")
2886: 103:    subprocess.run(["wsl", "-d", DISTRO, "--", "bash", "-lc", cmd], check=True)
2887: 104:    text = out.read_text(errors="ignore")
2888: 105:    if "JOB DONE" not in text or "convergence NOT achieved" in text:
2889: 106:        raise RuntimeError(f"pw.x failed for {tag}, see {out}")
2890: 107:    return read(out, format="espresso-out", index=-1)
2891: 108:
2892: 109:
2893: 110:def stress(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, relax_ions: bool) -> np.ndarray:
2894: 111:    return read_stress(run_pw(atoms, tag, s, relax_ions))
2895: 112:
2896: 113:
2897: 114:def read_stress(a: Atoms) -> np.ndarray:
2898: 115:    return a.get_stress(voigt=True) * GPA  # ASE sign: tensile positive
2899: 116:
2900: 117:
2901: 118:def elastic_cubic(atoms: Atoms, tag: str, s: Settings, eps: float = 0.01, full: bool = False,
2902: 119:                  relax_ions: bool | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
2903: 120:    """6x6 tensor (GPa) by central differences. full=False uses only e_xx and e_yz,
2904: 121:    which is exact for a cubic crystal and enough for pure elements (4 pw.x runs)."""
2905: 122:    if relax_ions is None:
2906: 123:        relax_ions = len(set(atoms.get_chemical_symbols())) > 1
2907: 124:    cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
2908: 125:    voigt = [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1)]

# ARS-Codex

This is a Codex adapter for the ARS suite. The vendored ARS content lives under
`ars/`; keep it as source material and route through this file first.

## Versioning

This Codex package is version `0.1.28`. The repo-root `VERSION`, this
`SKILL.md` metadata version, and `manifest.json` `adapter_version` must match.
Vendored ARS suite versions are tracked separately by source repository commit
in `manifest.json`.

## First Rule

Do not load the whole suite by default. Select one workflow, read that workflow's
`WORKFLOW.md`, then load only the agent, reference, template, or shared files needed
for the user's current stage.

The internal workflow entry files are named `WORKFLOW.md`, not `SKILL.md`, so
Codex registers only this root router skill instead of exposing every vendored
upstream workflow as a separate skill.

## Workflow Router

Choose the workflow by intent:

| User intent | Read first |
|---|---|
| Deep research, literature review, systematic review, meta-analysis, fact-checking, research question refinement | `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Academic paper writing, paper outline, abstract, revision, citation formatting, AI disclosure, LaTeX/DOCX/PDF formatting guidance | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Paper review, peer review simulation, editorial decision, reviewer calibration, re-review after revision | `ars/academic-paper-reviewer/WORKFLOW.md` |
| End-to-end research-to-paper pipeline, integrity gate, staged review/revision/finalization workflow | `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` |
| Experiment planning, code experiment execution plan, human study protocol, statistical interpretation, reproducibility validation | `ars/experiment-agent/WORKFLOW.md` |

If the request spans multiple workflows, start with `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md`
unless the user clearly asked for a single phase.

### Paper Topic Scoping Override

Apply this override before the general paper/pipeline routing rule and before the Claude-Style Alias Router below.
The override applies regardless of whether the user invokes ARS via natural
language or via an `ars-*` alias.

If the user says they want to write a paper, thesis, proposal, article, journal
article, or manuscript, but they only provide a broad topic, tentative title,
research interest, or "??/??/??" and do **not** provide a clear,
answerable research question, route to `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` in
`socratic` mode first. This matches the upstream ARS experience where vague
paper-topic requests start with SCR/Socratic narrowing instead of immediate
outline or drafting.

Treat these as Socratic triggers even when the wording contains paper-writing
intent:

- "I want to write a paper on ..."
- "I have a paper topic/title ..."
- "???????,???..."
- "????????/??,???????"
- "???????/??????"
- "??? ?? ??? ?? ??? ?? ???? ??"
- "?? ??/?? ??? ??? ??? ???? ????"

First response in this path:

1. State that the request is being routed to `deep-research` `socratic` mode
   because the research question is not yet precise.
2. Ask 3-5 Socratic narrowing questions using `socratic_mentor_agent` and
   `research_question_agent` guidance.
3. Do not produce an outline, draft, literature review, or full pipeline
   dashboard until the user has converged on at least one candidate RQ.

Route directly to `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` only when the user already
has a clear RQ, approved study frame, data/results, literature matrix, draft,
or explicitly asks to skip scoping and proceed to outline/drafting. Route to
`ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` only when the user explicitly asks for the
full research-to-paper pipeline or says to continue after Socratic scoping.

## Claude-Style Alias Router

Codex does not install Claude slash commands, but this package emulates their
intent. If the user's request starts with a slash alias (`/ars-plan`) or a plain
alias (`ars-plan`), treat it as a mode shortcut, strip the alias token from the
task text, read the matching `ars/commands/ars-*.md` prompt recipe, then route
to the workflow `WORKFLOW.md` below.

The `model:` field in command frontmatter is a Claude routing hint only. Codex
uses the current model unless the user explicitly requests another model.

| Alias | Read command recipe | Then route to |
|---|---|---|
| `/ars-plan`, `ars-plan` | `ars/commands/ars-plan.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `plan` mode |
| `/ars-outline`, `ars-outline` | `ars/commands/ars-outline.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `outline-only` mode |
| `/ars-abstract`, `ars-abstract` | `ars/commands/ars-abstract.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `abstract-only` mode |
| `/ars-lit-review`, `ars-lit-review` | `ars/commands/ars-lit-review.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `lit-review` mode; if the user wants source discovery and synthesis instead, route to `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` in `lit-review` mode |
| `/ars-3w`, `ars-3w` | `ars/commands/ars-3w.md` | `ars/deep-research/WORKFLOW.md` in `three-way-scan` mode |
| `/ars-citation-check`, `ars-citation-check` | `ars/commands/ars-citation-check.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `citation-check` mode |
| `/ars-disclosure`, `ars-disclosure` | `ars/commands/ars-disclosure.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `disclosure` mode |
| `/ars-format-convert`, `ars-format-convert` | `ars/commands/ars-format-convert.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `format-convert` mode |
| `/ars-revision-coach`, `ars-revision-coach` | `ars/commands/ars-revision-coach.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `revision-coach` mode |
| `/ars-revision`, `ars-revision` | `ars/commands/ars-revision.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `revision` mode |
| `/ars-rebuttal-audit`, `ars-rebuttal-audit` | `ars/commands/ars-rebuttal-audit.md` | `ars/academic-paper/WORKFLOW.md` in `rebuttal-audit` mode; requires both reviewer comments and an existing response draft |
| `/ars-reviewer`, `ars-reviewer` | `ars/commands/ars-reviewer.md` | `ars/academic-paper-reviewer/WORKFLOW.md` in `full` mode unless another reviewer mode is explicit |
| `/ars-mark-read`, `ars-mark-read` | `ars/commands/ars-mark-read.md` | Record a user-attested read declaration against the active Material Passport; every new mark requires a user-owned `read_scope`, with locators allowed only for `sections` scope |
| `/ars-unmark-read`, `ars-unmark-read` | `ars/commands/ars-unmark-read.md` | Rescind a prior human-read mark against the active Material Passport |
| `/ars-cache-invalidate`, `ars-cache-invalidate` | `ars/commands/ars-cache-invalidate.md` | Invalidate cached verification entries for one citation key |
| `/ars-full`, `ars-full` | `ars/commands/ars-full.md` | `ars/academic-pipeline/WORKFLOW.md` |

If the request body after the alias is a vague topic, tentative title, research
direction, or "??/??/??" without a clear research question, defer to the Paper Topic Scoping Override above before routing to the alias's target mode.
This applies to `ars-plan`, `ars-outline`, `ars-abstract`, `ars-lit-review`,
and `ars-full`.

If the Codex client reserves slash-prefixed input before it reaches the model,
tell the user to use the plain alias form, for example `ars-plan my topic`.

subset from Section 3.1, the direct baseline gives 5.41 and the rule 1.94 GPa. Neither calculation reproduces the
full fitted CALPHAD model of Marker et al. For the mixing energy, the earlier linearised k = 1 transfer gives 13.3
meV/atom against 11.5 for the own-volume baseline on hm_fresh, and that energy claim was demoted. Exact binary-volume
interpolation gives 8.8 meV/atom on that set, but this exploratory advantage does not replicate significantly on h1
or h3. K' differs from the energy because the binary curvatures change steeply with volume: at the binary Vegard
volume the median dln|K'|/dlnV is -3.16 over the 12 pairs with |K'| > 10 GPa.

**3.5 Second model and the size of k (prereg 88b9465108, result 43370bbb27, verdict 736bcac471).** Under
medium-mpa-0, on 1200 new compositions (Co yes/no x 3/4/5 elements, 200 each, two cells each) with two independent
binary panels, the rule cuts RMSE from 4.81 to 2.21 GPa (gain 0.54) and wins in 934 of 1200. The preregistered
equivalence claim, 90% CI of k inside [0.90, 1.10], failed: k = 1.138, 90% CI [1.098, 1.182], 95% CI [1.091, 1.189].
The audit found no coding error, and every 3+3 panel split gives 1.138 to 1.139. Exploratory splits, not
preregistered: 3-component 1.00 [0.91, 1.09], 4-component 1.25, 5-component 1.17; Cu-free 1.00 [0.94, 1.07],
Cu-containing 1.24; compositions whose largest pair |ln V0/V_ij| is at most 0.15 give 1.07, above 0.25 give 1.41.
The aggregate Co-free and Co-containing slopes are similar (1.137, 1.139), without excluding composition-specific Co
effects. Across datasets, omat slopes are about 1.08 to 1.11 and this mpa test gives 1.14; these are not matched
estimates of a pure model effect. An earlier 94-composition mpa test with shared seeds gave k about 1.33 and failed
its registered slope criterion (86767e478d). Refitting k on the same 1200 targets lowers RMSE from 2.213 to 2.151
GPa, an in-sample gain of 2.8% that does not establish an out-of-sample benefit. We read the pattern as
under-prediction at large size mismatch: the pair transfer captures most of the volume effect but not all of it.

**3.6 The C44-type shear.** On the historical datasets, disjoint target-binary seed checks gave K44 gains of about
0.06 to 0.14. Three sequential preregistered controls on one set of 150 compositions (half with Co >= 15%) support a
shared-residual description of the two shears. They do not establish its physical origin; all three audits returned
PLAUSIBLE.
- Seed-100 target cells (prereg c2eff007ad, result b86e0d8a40; 45 compositions overlap a withdrawn seed-0 run, and
  excluding them keeps the PASS with gain 0.467): the difference A = K44 - K' follows the rule (gain 0.49), the
  residuals of the two shears correlate (r 0.77), and the joint fit gives k 0.91 and b 0.94. Ungated subgroup gains
  for plain K44: 0.474 in 75 Co-free alloys, 0.091 in 75 Co-containing alloys.
- Two new cells per composition with seeds unique to each cell (prereg fd786169e3): the K44 residual of one cell
  correlates with the K' residual of the other (r 0.75; same cell 0.79), k 0.92, b 0.95.
- The same cells after subtracting the clamped mixing pre-stress from targets and binaries alike (prereg ede47f1d65):
  cross-cell r 0.67, k 0.99, b 0.79. The pre-stress is about pair-additive (target rms 7.1 GPa, prediction residual
  0.7 GPa). Removing it lowers the cross-cell residual covariance by about 23% but does not remove the shared
  residual.
The diagnostic regression is K44 - pair44 ? k T44 + b (K' - rule'), with T44 = rule44 - pair44. Because the second
covariate contains a measured K' target, this is a residual association, not a predictor of K44 from binary inputs
alone. Open alternative: b drops to 0.4 to 0.5 when single disjoint binary seeds are used, so part of the shared
residual may be error carried by the binary references. Independent binary panels for both channels and the stress
are needed to separate the two; this is left for future work.

## 4. What the audits caught

Table 2. Errors found by audit. Each was found by the agent that did not write the code.

| Error | Found by | Size | What it changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Integer-count reference mismatch | R1 audits | up to 56.6 meV/atom in the Al-free set; 60.7 including Al | energy references corrected; historical a2 shear and some derived columns remain uncorrected |
| PBE cutoff mismatch | audit, 7e0ff785d1 | 30.7 meV/atom shift in the Pt reference; correction checked to 0.002 meV/atom | alloy-matched cutoffs; ordered-cell L1 check changed from FAIL to PASS |
| Holdout used for model selection | audit, d26bd71285 | 113 of 207 pooled energy rows were selection data | "two independent holdouts" withdrawn; hm_fresh-only RMSE 36.4 to 13.1 meV/atom |
| Shared random-site permutation between targets and binaries | S2 audit (Opus), confirmed by Astra; e7d441a4eb | K44 gains inflated by about 0.06 to 0.18 | historical results amended; 9cfc8edaf0 withdrawn before its targets were read and rerun with disjoint seeds |
| Weak baseline made a linearised energy rule look new | audit | 13.3 vs 11.5 meV/atom | energy rule demoted |
| Power simulation treated a composition-level residual as cell noise | audit of 88b9465108 | reported simulated power 1.0 under an optimistic noise model | audit identified the flaw; the archived preregistration script still uses the original noise model |
| Original power simulation covered only the correlation gate | audit of ede47f1d65, 7ceca1b668 | full-gate audit simulation: 5000/5000 passes under the simulated alternative and 0/5000 under the simulated null | additional simulation recorded; rates remain conditional on the assumed noise models |
| PBE runs with nspin 1 still magnetize Co and Ni | Astra, S3 | not used in any result | fixed in harness/dft.py before any Co/Ni PBE run |
| Equiatomic ternary reference weight 0.3333 instead of 1/3 in the count correction | Astra, S1 | +0.3 to +0.7 meV/atom on 44 energy rows; stale derived columns | corrected in *_fixed2 tables (scripts/fix_counts2.py); energy rows only, no shear result affected |

## 5. Discussion and limits

1. Model only. Every target is a MACE energy. The slope already differs between datasets and models (1.08 to 1.14).
   A preregistered eight-cell ordered L1_2 A3B check (6cb3c2a936, verdict b3214734c2, audited) compared clamped
   mixing shear curvatures from PBE and MACE at the same geometry. MACE gets the sign of K' right in 8 of 8 cells but
   the sign of K44 in only 5 of 8 (Au3Ir: -32.4 GPa in PBE, +3.2 in MACE), and the median |MACE - PBE| is 47% of the
   median |PBE| for K' and 56% for K44. MACE therefore fails our calibration criterion for this quantity. The
   binary inputs and the alloy targets of this work are both such MACE curvatures, so the transfer rule is shown to
   hold within MACE; whether it holds for PBE curvatures is open. Convergence checks of this comparison (denser k-grid,
   higher charge-density cutoff) are running. It does not test transfer to random alloys. An L3 test needs at least 15 independent DFT or experimental rows from composition
   families absent from training, with the rule and coefficient frozen beforehand. This is future work.
2. Clamped, unrelaxed cells: K'_mix is not the measured C'. On 43 previously examined equiatomic ternaries, relaxed-
   binary Muggianu gives C' RMSE 3.08 GPa and a volume-transfer chain 2.52 GPa (gain 0.18, p about 0.08). The chain
   also uses the measured relaxed target volume. This exploratory comparison shows neither a significant improvement
   nor equivalence at zero pressure.
3. The rule under-predicts at large size mismatch (Section 3.5). A correction has not been tested.
4. fcc late transition and noble metals only. None of the three calibrated MACE models passed the bcc shear
   criterion in this project.
5. The rule is a regular-solution or tensorial-CE truncation with a specified volume; we do not claim a new law.

## Data and code

The ledger, literature log, harness, scripts, data tables, audit records and agent transcripts are in the
reproducibility archive (built by `scripts/build_repro.py`, SHA256 manifest included). The exploratory baseline and
relaxed-chain inputs of Sections 3.4 and 5.2 are in `data/archive_s2_opus_scratch` with their scripts, which use
paths relative to the archive root; rerunning `chain.py` from the extracted archive reproduces `chain.csv` byte for
byte. The sealed holdout and raw pw.x runs are not included. Archive DOI: pending deposition.

## Use of AI

Hypotheses, code and audits were produced by two large language model agents (GPT-6-Astra via Codex CLI; Claude Opus
via Claude Code) under the protocol of Section 2, and the agents ran the calculations on the author's computer. The manuscript was
drafted by Claude Opus. The author set the research goal, directed the agents and reviewed the results, and takes
responsibility for the content.

# Academic Paper Reviewer v1.11.1 - Multi-Perspective Academic Paper Review Agent Team

Simulates a complete international journal peer review process: automatically identifies the paper's field, dynamically configures 4 card-backed identities (Journal-Fit Reviewer + 3 peer reviewers), and adds the fixed Devil's Advocate as the fifth execution seat. The five role-separated perspectives cover journal fit, methodology, domain expertise, cross-disciplinary viewpoints, and core argument challenges; a separate editorial synthesizer produces the structured Editorial Decision and Revision Roadmap.

**v1.1 Improvements**:
1. Added Devil's Advocate Reviewer - specifically challenges core arguments, detects logical fallacies, and identifies the strongest counter-arguments
2. Added `re-review` mode - verification review, focused on checking whether revisions address the review comments
3. Expanded review team from 4 to 5 members

> **Routing discipline (v3.9.2):** see `.claude/CLAUDE.md` "Routing Discipline (v3.9.2)" + `shared/references/intent_clarification_protocol.md` for cross-skill routing rules. This skill assumes routing has already settled - ambiguous cross-phase materials should have been clarified upstream.

---

## Quick Start

**Simplest command:**
```
Review this paper: [paste paper or provide file]
```

**Output:**
1. Automatically identifies the paper's field and methodology type
2. Dynamically configures four card-backed reviewer identities; the fixed Devil's Advocate is the fifth execution seat
3. 5 role-separated review reports (4 configuration cards plus the fixed Devil's Advocate, with typed execution provenance)
4. 1 Editorial Decision Letter + Revision Roadmap

---

## Trigger Conditions

### Trigger Keywords

**English**: review paper, peer review, manuscript review, referee report, review my paper, critique paper, simulate review, editorial review, calibrate reviewer, reviewer calibration, measure reviewer accuracy

**???**: ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ??, ?? ???, ??? ???? ??, ??? ??, ?? ??? ??

**????**: ????, ????, ????, ????, ?????, ????????, ?????

### Non-Trigger Scenarios

| Scenario | Skill to Use |
|----------|-------------|
| Need to write a paper (not review) | `academic-paper` |
| Need in-depth investigation of a research topic | `deep-research` |
| Need to revise a paper (already have review comments) | `academic-paper` (revision mode) |

### Quick Mode Selection Guide

| Your Situation | Recommended Mode | Spectrum |
|----------------|-----------------|----------|
| Need comprehensive review (first submission) | full | balanced |
| Checking if revisions addressed comments | re-review | fidelity |
| Quick quality assessment (15 min) | quick | fidelity |
| Focus only on methods/statistics | methodology-focus | fidelity |
| Want to learn by doing (guided review) | guided | originality |
| Want to measure this reviewer's bounded decision-error profile on an adjudicated target set | calibration | fidelity |

**Spectrum** (v3.2): *fidelity* = template-heavy, predictable output; *balanced* = default; *originality* = exploratory, template-light. See `shared/mode_spectrum.md` for the full cross-skill spectrum table.

Not sure? Use `full` for pre-submission review, `re-review` for post-revision verification. Current live reviews and Schema 6 packages declare `NOT_CALIBRATED`; a full-tier calibration run may produce a bounded candidate profile, but live-profile application remains unavailable until its closed artifact and replay validator ship. `calibration` is opt-in: its default full tier measures bounded decision-level FNR/FPR, while the explicitly selected 3-paper directional tier gives only a low-cost Minor/Major boundary signal and remains `NOT_CALIBRATED`.

---

## Agent Team (7 Agents)

| # | Agent | Role | Phase |
|---|-------|------|-------|
| 1 | `field_analyst_agent` | Analyzes the paper's field and dynamically configures 4 card-backed identities; the Devil's Advocate remains a fixed fifth seat | Phase 0 |
| 2 | `eic_agent` | Journal-Fit Reviewer - journal fit, originality, overall quality; one panel card, no final-decision authority | Phase 1 |
| 3 | `methodology_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 1 - research design, statistical validity, reproducibility | Phase 1 |
| 4 | `domain_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 2 - literature coverage, theoretical framework, domain contribution | Phase 1 |
| 5 | `perspective_reviewer_agent` | Peer Reviewer 3 - cross-disciplinary connections, practical impact, challenging fundamental assumptions | Phase 1 |
| 6 | **`devils_advocate_reviewer_agent`** | **Devil's Advocate - core argument challenges, logical fallacy detection, strongest counter-arguments** | **Phase 1** |
| 7 | `editorial_synthesizer_agent` | Synthesizes all reviews, identifies consensus and disagreements, makes editorial decision | Phase 2 |

**Role-name compatibility (#611):** the public display name is **Journal-Fit Reviewer**. The stable implementation identifiers remain `eic_agent` (agent), `eic` (`contract_role` / dispatch role), and `EIC` (serialized reviewer/source ID, including `EIC-W<n>`). Those compatibility tokens do not select a Stage 3' agent file: `editorial_synthesizer_agent` emits first-round decisions, while contract-governed re-review uses its three dedicated calls and checker-derived outcome.

---

## Orchestration Workflow (3 Phases)

```
User: "Review this paper"
     |
=== Phase 0: FIELD ANALYSIS & PERSONA CONFIGURATION ===
     |
     +-> [field_analyst_agent] -> Reviewer Configuration Card (x4)
         - Reads the complete paper
         - Identifies: primary discipline, secondary discipline, research paradigm, methodology type, target journal tier, paper maturity
         - Dynamically generates specific identities for 4 card-backed reviewers:
           * Journal-Fit Reviewer (internal `EIC`): which journal/editor perspective, area of expertise, review preferences
           * Reviewer 1 (Methodology): Methodological expertise, what they particularly focus on
           * Reviewer 2 (Domain): Domain expertise, research interests
           * Reviewer 3 (Perspective): Cross-disciplinary angle, what unique perspective they bring
         - The fifth execution seat is the fixed Devil's Advocate, which receives no dynamic configuration card
     |
     ** Presents Reviewer Configuration to user for confirmation (adjustable) **
     |
=== Phase 1: PARALLEL MULTI-PERSPECTIVE REVIEW ===
     |
     |-> [eic_agent] -------> Journal-Fit Review Report
     |   - Journal fit, originality, significance, relevance to readership
     |   - Does not go deep into methodology (that's Reviewer 1's job)
     |   - One role-separated card among five - no peer-output channel before commitment (Iron Rule #2)
     |
     |-> [methodology_reviewer_agent] -> Methodology Review Report
     |   - Research design rigor, sampling strategy, data collection
     |   - Analysis method selection, statistical validity, effect sizes
     |   - Reproducibility, data transparency
     |
     |-> [domain_reviewer_agent] -------> Domain Review Report
     |   - Literature review completeness, theoretical framework appropriateness
     |   - Academic argument accuracy, incremental contribution to the field
     |   - Missing key references
     |
     |-> [perspective_reviewer_agent] --> Perspective Review Report
     |   - Cross-disciplinary connections and borrowing opportunities
     |   - Practical applications and policy implications
     |   - Broader social or ethical implications
     |
     +-> [devils_advocate_reviewer_agent] --> Devil's Advocate Report
         - Core argument challenges (strongest counter-arguments)
         - Cherry-picking detection
         - Confirmation bias detection
         - Logic chain validation
         - Overgeneralization detection
         - Alternative paths analysis
         - Stakeholder blind spots
         - "So what?" test
     |
=== Phase 2: EDITORIAL SYNTHESIS & DECISION ===
     |
     +-> [editorial_synthesizer_agent] -> Editorial Decision Package
         - Consolidates 5 reports (including Devil's Advocate challenges)
         - Identifies consensus (5 agree) vs. disagreement (divergent opinions)
         - Arbitration and argumentation for disputed issues

FILE scripts/build_repro.py
"""Build the reproducibility archive for paper/draft_v3.md.

python scripts/build_repro.py
Writes paper/repro_<date>.zip with the ledger, literature log, harness, scripts, data tables (no sealed holdout, no
raw pw.x runs), audits, lessons and swarm records, plus a SHA256 manifest. Never overwrites an existing archive.
"""

import datetime as dt
import hashlib
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
INCLUDE = ["claims", "harness", "scripts", "data", ".orchestra/audits", ".orchestra/swarm", ".orchestra/fronts",
           ".orchestra/LESSONS.md", "candidates/README.md", "AGENTS.md", "STATUS.md", "paper/draft_v3.md"]
SKIP = ("data/sealed", "data/dft_runs", "__pycache__")

out = ROOT / "paper" / f"repro_{dt.date.today():%Y%m%d}.zip"
assert not out.exists(), out
files = []
for item in INCLUDE:
    p = ROOT / item
    for f in ([p] if p.is_file() else sorted(p.rglob("*"))):
        rel = f.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
        if f.is_file() and not any(rel.startswith(s) or s in rel for s in SKIP):
            files.append((rel, f))
manifest = "".join(f"{hashlib.sha256(f.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}  {rel}\n" for rel, f in files)
readme = """Reproducibility archive for "Binary shear curvatures read at the alloy's volume".
claims/claims.jsonl is the append-only ledger; every number in the paper cites an id there. Evidence paths in it are
absolute paths of the author's machine; strip the prefix up to the project folder. Scripts run with MACE-MP
(mace-torch) and ASE; each script's docstring gives its command. The sealed arena holdout and raw pw.x runs are not
included. MANIFEST.sha256 lists every file.
"""
with zipfile.ZipFile(out, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for rel, f in files:
        z.write(f, rel)
    z.writestr("MANIFEST.sha256", manifest)
    z.writestr("README.txt", readme)
print(out, len(files), "files", f"{out.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB")


FILE data/archive_s2_opus_scratch/chain.py
"""Relaxed C44, C' of seen scan alloys from pures + binaries only:
C_pred = sum x_i K_i(V*) + sum 4 x_i x_j [K_ij(V*) - N_ij], N_ij = relaxation softening of the 50:50 binary
(clamped prediction at its relaxed volume minus its relaxed scan value). V* = observed relaxed volume (isolates the
elastic step). Baselines: Voigt rule of mixtures of pure relaxed constants, clamped-only (N = 0)."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]; sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
from harness.context import context
from harness.features import parse_comp
SP = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ctx = context()
pk = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(SP/"pure_k.csv"), pd.read_csv(SP/"pure_k_ext.csv")]).sort_values(["el", "dlnV"])
PS = {(el, ch): CubicSpline(g.dlnV, g[ch]) for el, g in pk.groupby("el") for ch in ("K44", "Kp")}
pp = pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data"/"scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv").set_index("el"); pv = pp.vol_per_atom
g = pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data"/"binary_kgrid.csv").groupby(["pair", "dlnV"])[["K44", "Kp"]].mean().reset_index()
BS = {(tuple(k.split("-")), ch): CubicSpline(s.dlnV, s[ch]) for k, s in g.groupby("pair") for ch in ("K44", "Kp")}
s = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data"/f) for f in ("scan_fcc_omat.csv", "scan_fcc_omat_rev.csv")]).drop_duplicates("comp")
s = s[~s.comp.str.contains("Al")]
OBS = {"K44": lambda r: r.C44, "Kp": lambda r: (r.C11-r.C12)/2}
def clamped(c, V, ch):
    return (sum(x*float(PS[(e, ch)](np.log(V/pv[e]))) for e, x in c.items()),
            sum(4*xa*xb*float(BS[((a, b), ch)](np.log(V/ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"]))) for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c)))
N = {}
for r in s.itertuples():
    c = parse_comp(r.comp)
    if len(c) == 2 and all(abs(x-0.5) < 1e-3 for x in c.values()):
        for ch in OBS:
            p, m = clamped(c, r.vol_per_atom, ch); N[(tuple(sorted(c)), ch)] = p+m-OBS[ch](r)
rows = []
for r in s.itertuples():
    c = parse_comp(r.comp)
    if len(c) == 2 and all(abs(x-0.5) < 1e-3 for x in c.values()): continue
    if not all(((a, b), "Kp") in BS for a, b, _, _ in ctx.pairs(c)): continue
    rec = dict(comp=r.comp, n_el=len(c))
    for ch in OBS:
        p, m = clamped(c, r.vol_per_atom, ch)
        nrel = sum(4*xa*xb*N[((a, b), ch)] for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))
        rom = sum(x*(pp.loc[e, "C44"] if ch == "K44" else (pp.loc[e, "C11"]-pp.loc[e, "C12"])/2) for e, x in c.items())
        rec.update({ch+"_obs": OBS[ch](r), ch+"_rom": rom, ch+"_clamped": p+m, ch+"_chain": p+m-nrel, ch+"_N": nrel})
    rows.append(rec)
t = pd.DataFrame(rows); t.to_csv(SP/"chain.csv", index=False)
rm = lambda e: float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(e))))
for lab, q in [("25:75 binaries", t[t.n_el == 2]), ("ternaries", t[t.n_el == 3]), ("quinaries", t[t.n_el == 5])]:
    for ch in OBS:
        y = q[ch+"_obs"]
        print(f"{lab:15s} {ch:3s} n {len(q):2d}  RMSE rom {rm(y-q[ch+'_rom']):6.2f}  clamped {rm(y-q[ch+'_clamped']):6.2f}  "
              f"chain {rm(y-q[ch+'_chain']):6.2f}  mean(obs-chain) {np.mean(y-q[ch+'_chain']):+6.2f}  sd obs {y.std():6.2f}")

"""Same reference-state audit for the shear-curvature L2 (697c2d6d75): targets h3_shear_clamped, hm_shear_clamped.
own-ref: G_ij = K_ij(V_ij) + mean_k [K_k(V_ij) - K_k(V_k)]; pred = sum 4 x_i x_j G_ij - sum x_i [K_i(V0) - K_i(V_i)]"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]; sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
from harness.context import context
from harness.features import parse_comp
SP = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ctx = context()
pk = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(SP/"pure_k.csv"), pd.read_csv(SP/"pure_k_ext.csv")]).sort_values(["el", "dlnV"])
PS = {(el, ch): CubicSpline(g.dlnV, g[ch]) for el, g in pk.groupby("el") for ch in ("K44", "Kp")}
pv = {el: ctx.pure[el]["V"] for el in ctx.pure}
dk = lambda el, v, ch: float(PS[(el, ch)](np.log(v/pv[el])) - PS[(el, ch)](0.0))
g = pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data"/"binary_kgrid.csv").groupby(["pair", "dlnV"])[["K44", "Kp"]].mean().reset_index()
BS = {(tuple(k.split("-")), ch): CubicSpline(s.dlnV, s[ch]) for k, s in g.groupby("pair") for ch in ("K44", "Kp")}
rm = lambda x: float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(x))))
def signflip(y, a, b, n=20000):
    d = (y-b)**2-(y-a)**2; rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    null = np.array([np.mean(d*rng.choice([-1, 1], len(d))) for _ in range(n)]); return (np.sum(null >= d.mean())+1)/(n+1)
for f in ("h3_shear_clamped.csv", "hm_shear_clamped.csv"):
    t = pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data"/f); t = t[t.n_el >= 3]
    for ch in ("Kp", "K44"):
        rows = []
        for r in t.itertuples():
            c = parse_comp(r.comp)
            if not all(((a, b), ch) in BS for a, b, _, _ in ctx.pairs(c)): continue
            v0 = ctx.vegard(c)
            pair = sum(4*xa*xb*float(BS[((a, b), ch)](0.0)) for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))
            rule = sum(4*xa*xb*float(BS[((a, b), ch)](np.log(v0/ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"]))) for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))
            Gij = lambda a, b: float(BS[((a, b), ch)](0.0)) + 0.5*(dk(a, ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"], ch) + dk(b, ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"], ch))
            own = sum(4*xa*xb*Gij(a, b) for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c)) - sum(x*dk(el, v0, ch) for el, x in c.items())
            rows.append((getattr(r, ch), pair, rule, own))
        a = np.array(rows); y = a[:, 0]
        print(f"{f:22s} {ch:3s} n {len(a):3d}  RMSE GPa: pair-at-V_ij {rm(y-a[:,1]):5.2f}  rule {rm(y-a[:,2]):5.2f}  own-volume Muggianu {rm(y-a[:,3]):5.2f}"
              f"  | rule vs own: gain {1-rm(y-a[:,2])/rm(y-a[:,3]):+.2f} p {signflip(y, a[:,2], a[:,3]):.1e}  corr {np.corrcoef(a[:,2], a[:,3])[0,1]:.3f}")

# Candidates

One python file per candidate. The arena (`harness/arena.py`) loads it, fits at most one free coefficient on the
training rows, checks on the sealed holdout's compositions that the test can tell it from the champion, pre-registers
it, then tests it on the sealed targets.

META = {

    "dataset": "emix_random",
    "statement": "one line: the physical claim",
    "mechanism": "a few lines: why",
    "free": [],                      # or [("k", lo, hi)]
}

def predict(comp, ctx, *coef):       # comp: {"Cu": 0.25, ...}; ctx: harness/context.py
    return ...                       # eV/atom
```

The champion is `champion_volume_transfer.py`. A candidate must beat it by 10% RMSE with p < 0.01/m.
